questions.question: An ARP request and an ARP reply are sent respectively as:

options.A: Multicast and broadcast
options.B: Unicast and broadcast
options.C: Unicast and multicast
options.D: Broadcast and unicast

questions.answer_text: Broadcast and unicast
questions.explanation: The request is broadcast to all hosts ('who has 10.0.0.5?'); only the owner replies directly.

questions.question: In the IP header, the 'Protocol' field values 1, 6 and 17 identify:

options.A: ICMP, TCP and UDP
options.B: UDP, ICMP and TCP
options.C: TCP, UDP and ICMP
options.D: ARP, TCP and UDP

questions.answer_text: ICMP, TCP and UDP
questions.explanation: The protocol number tells the receiving host which upper-layer protocol the payload belongs to.

questions.question: The Time To Live (TTL) field in an IPv4 packet is used to:

options.A: Measure how long an idle TCP session can stay open
options.B: Set how long DNS records may be cached by resolvers
options.C: Define how long the packet's encryption key remains valid
options.D: Prevent packets from looping forever by limiting hops

questions.answer_text: Prevent packets from looping forever by limiting hops
questions.explanation: Each router decreases TTL by 1; the packet is dropped when TTL reaches 0.

questions.question: DHCP assigns an IP address to a client through which sequence of messages?

options.A: Request, Offer, Discover, Acknowledge
options.B: Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge
options.C: Discover, Request, Offer, Acknowledge
options.D: Offer, Discover, Acknowledge, Request

questions.answer_text: Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge
questions.explanation: Remembered as DORA. DHCP uses UDP ports 67 (server) and 68 (client).

questions.question: What is the default port of SMTP?
questions.explanation: 110 = POP3, 143 = IMAP, 21 = FTP control. Port 587 is used for authenticated mail submission.

questions.question: Port 22 is used by:

options.A: FTP data
options.B: DNS
options.C: Telnet
options.D: SSH (and SFTP)

questions.answer_text: SSH (and SFTP)
questions.explanation: SFTP = SSH File Transfer Protocol and runs over SSH on port 22.

questions.question: Which protocol is used to synchronise clocks of servers, and on which port does it run?

options.A: NTP on UDP 123
options.B: NNTP on TCP 119
options.C: SNTP on TCP 25
options.D: SNMP on UDP 161

questions.answer_text: NTP on UDP 123
questions.explanation: Accurate time is essential for log correlation, Kerberos and transaction timestamps.

questions.question: SNMP agents listen for queries on which port?

options.A: UDP 161
options.B: TCP 389
options.C: UDP 162
options.D: TCP 3389

questions.answer_text: UDP 161
questions.explanation: UDP 161 for queries; UDP 162 for traps sent to the manager.

questions.question: Match the protocol with its default port: (P) HTTPS (Q) DNS (R) RDP (S) LDAP | (1) 3389 (2) 389 (3) 443 (4) 53
questions.explanation: HTTPS 443, DNS 53, RDP 3389, LDAP 389 (LDAPS 636).

questions.question: Telnet uses port 23 and should not be used for remote server administration because:

options.A: It works only on Windows servers and not on Linux
options.B: It needs a graphical desktop running on the server
options.C: It sends usernames, passwords and data in clear text
options.D: It is too slow for WAN links between branches

questions.answer_text: It sends usernames, passwords and data in clear text
questions.explanation: SSH (port 22) encrypts the session and should be used instead.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid SMTP commands?

options.A: HELO, MAIL FROM, RCPT TO, DATA, QUIT
options.B: SYN, ACK, FIN, RST, PSH, URG
options.C: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH
options.D: USER, PASS, LIST, RETR, DELE

questions.answer_text: HELO, MAIL FROM, RCPT TO, DATA, QUIT
questions.explanation: GET/POST are HTTP methods; USER/PASS/LIST/RETR are POP3 commands; SYN/ACK are TCP flags.

questions.question: Port numbers 0 to 1023 are known as:

options.A: Registered ports
options.B: Dynamic/ephemeral ports
options.C: Well-known ports
options.D: Private ports

questions.answer_text: Well-known ports
questions.explanation: 1024-49151 are registered; 49152-65535 are dynamic/ephemeral.

questions.question: DNS queries normally use which transport protocol and port?

options.A: TCP port 110
options.B: TCP port 25
options.C: UDP port 53
options.D: UDP port 67

questions.answer_text: UDP port 53
questions.explanation: DNS also uses TCP 53 for zone transfers and large responses.

questions.question: FTP uses which ports in active mode?

options.A: 22 for control and 21 for data
options.B: 20 for control and 21 for data
options.C: 69 for both control and data
options.D: 21 for control and 20 for data

questions.answer_text: 21 for control and 20 for data
questions.explanation: TFTP uses UDP 69; SFTP uses 22.

questions.question: A combination of an IP address and a port number (e.g. 10.1.1.5:443) is called a:

options.A: Socket
options.B: MAC address
options.C: Gateway
options.D: Subnet

questions.answer_text: Socket
questions.explanation: A TCP connection is identified by the source and destination sockets.

questions.question: An IPv4 address is ____ bits long and an IPv6 address is ____ bits long.
questions.explanation: IPv4 ~ 4.3 billion addresses; IPv6 ~ 3.4 x 10^38 addresses.

questions.question: The first-octet range of a Class C IPv4 address is:
The default (natural) subnet mask of a Class B network is:
questions.explanation: Class A /8, Class B /16, Class C /24.

questions.question: The IPv4 loopback address range begins with:
questions.explanation: 127.0.0.0/8 is reserved for loopback; 127.0.0.1 is commonly used (localhost).

questions.question: Class D addresses (224.0.0.0 to 239.255.255.255) are used for:

options.A: Private LANs
options.B: Broadcast only
options.C: Loopback testing
options.D: Multicast

questions.answer_text: Multicast
questions.explanation: Class E (240-255) is reserved for experimental use.

questions.question: For the Class A address 10.20.30.40 with its default mask, how many bits are used for network and host?

options.A: 8 network bits, 24 host bits
options.B: 16 network bits, 16 host bits
options.C: 24 network bits, 8 host bits
options.D: 12 network bits, 20 host bits

questions.answer_text: 8 network bits, 24 host bits
questions.explanation: Default Class A mask is 255.0.0.0 (/8), so the network ID is 10.0.0.0.

questions.question: Which of the following is a private (RFC 1918) IPv4 address?
A Windows PC shows the address 169.254.12.7. This most likely means:

options.A: It is configured as a loopback interface for local testing only
options.B: It has joined a multicast group used for video streaming
options.C: It could not reach a DHCP server and self-assigned an APIPA address
options.D: It has received a valid public IP address directly from the ISP

questions.answer_text: It could not reach a DHCP server and self-assigned an APIPA address
questions.explanation: APIPA (169.254.0.0/16) is link-local and indicates DHCP failure.

questions.question: How many usable host addresses are available in a /26 subnet?
questions.explanation: Host bits = 32 - 26 = 6; 2^6 - 2 = 62 (network and broadcast addresses excluded).

questions.question: The subnet mask 255.255.255.224 is equivalent to which CIDR prefix?
questions.explanation: 224 = 11100000, so 24 + 3 = 27 network bits; it gives 30 usable hosts.

questions.question: What is the network address and broadcast address of host 192.168.10.70/26?
Which prefix is commonly used for a point-to-point link between two routers because it gives exactly 2 usable hosts?
questions.explanation: /30: 4 addresses - network - broadcast = 2 hosts (/31 is also allowed on modern routers).

questions.question: A branch network 10.10.0.0/16 must be split into subnets by borrowing 4 bits. How many subnets and how many usable hosts per subnet result?

options.A: 16 subnets, 4094 hosts each
options.B: 16 subnets, 4096 hosts each
options.C: 8 subnets, 8190 hosts each
options.D: 4 subnets, 16382 hosts each

questions.answer_text: 16 subnets, 4094 hosts each
questions.explanation: 2^4 = 16 subnets; new prefix /20 leaves 12 host bits: 2^12 - 2 = 4094.

questions.question: CIDR (Classless Inter-Domain Routing) was introduced mainly to:

options.A: Increase the IPv4 address length from 32 to 64 bits
options.B: Use IP addresses efficiently and allow route aggregation
options.C: Replace MAC addresses with logical addresses on LANs
options.D: Encrypt routing updates exchanged on the Internet

questions.answer_text: Use IP addresses efficiently and allow route aggregation
questions.explanation: CIDR removes fixed class boundaries, e.g. 192.168.0.0/22 aggregates four /24 networks.

questions.question: Which single CIDR block summarises the four networks 192.168.4.0/24, 192.168.5.0/24, 192.168.6.0/24 and 192.168.7.0/24?
questions.explanation: 4 to 7 share the first 6 bits of the third octet (000001xx), so 16 + 6 = /22.

questions.question: Which statement about IPv6 is correct?

options.A: IPv6 addresses are 64 bits long, written as eight decimal groups
options.B: IPv6 does not use broadcast; it uses multicast and anycast instead
options.C: IPv6 has a variable-length base header that includes a checksum
options.D: IPv6 still uses ARP broadcasts to find neighbours' MAC addresses

questions.answer_text: IPv6 does not use broadcast; it uses multicast and anycast instead
questions.explanation: IPv6 uses Neighbor Discovery Protocol (ICMPv6) instead of ARP and has a fixed 40-byte header without checksum.

questions.question: The IPv6 loopback address is:
questions.explanation: FE80::/10 is link-local; FF00::/8 is multicast.

questions.question: What is the correct compressed form of 2001:0db8:0000:0000:0000:ff00:0042:8329?
questions.explanation: Leading zeros in each group can be dropped, and '::' can replace one run of zero groups only once.

questions.question: IPv6 is considered more efficient than IPv4 for routing mainly because:

options.A: It has a simplified fixed-length header and no router fragmentation
options.B: It uses broadcast for discovery, which speeds up routing
options.C: It requires NAT for every host, which simplifies routing
options.D: It uses shorter addresses than IPv4, so routing tables become much smaller

questions.answer_text: It has a simplified fixed-length header and no router fragmentation
questions.explanation: Routers process IPv6 headers faster; fragmentation is done only by the source host.

questions.question: IPv6 addresses beginning with FE80:: are:

options.A: Link-local addresses
options.B: Loopback addresses
options.C: Multicast addresses
options.D: Global unicast addresses

questions.answer_text: Link-local addresses
questions.explanation: Every IPv6 interface automatically gets a link-local address valid only on that link.

questions.question: Arrange the encapsulation of data at the sender in the correct order:

options.A: Data -> Packet -> Segment -> Frame -> Bits
options.B: Data -> Segment -> Packet -> Frame -> Bits
options.C: Bits -> Frame -> Packet -> Segment -> Data
options.D: Data -> Frame -> Packet -> Segment -> Bits

questions.answer_text: Data -> Segment -> Packet -> Frame -> Bits
questions.explanation: Each layer adds its own header (Layer 2 also adds a trailer); the receiver de-encapsulates in reverse.

questions.question: As a packet passes through a router to another network, which addresses normally change?

options.A: Source and destination MAC addresses
options.B: Port numbers
options.C: Nothing changes
options.D: Source and destination IP addresses

questions.answer_text: Source and destination MAC addresses
questions.explanation: IP addresses stay end-to-end (unless NAT is used); Layer 2 headers are rebuilt for every hop.

questions.question: The standard MTU (Maximum Transmission Unit) of Ethernet is:

options.A: 64 KB
options.B: 512 bytes
options.C: 9000 bytes
options.D: 1500 bytes

questions.answer_text: 1500 bytes
questions.explanation: 9000 bytes is used by 'jumbo frames' in data-centre networks.

questions.question: What is the size of a MAC address?

options.A: 32 bits (4 bytes)
options.B: 64 bits (8 bytes)
options.C: 128 bits (16 bytes)
options.D: 48 bits (6 bytes)

questions.answer_text: 48 bits (6 bytes)
questions.explanation: The first 24 bits form the OUI identifying the manufacturer.

questions.question: The size of an IPv4 header is:

options.A: Fixed 40 bytes
options.B: Fixed 128 bytes
options.C: 20 to 60 bytes
options.D: 8 bytes

questions.answer_text: 20 to 60 bytes
questions.explanation: 20 bytes minimum; up to 60 bytes with options. IPv6 has a fixed 40-byte base header.

questions.question: Wi-Fi (wireless LAN) is defined by which IEEE standard?
questions.explanation: 802.3 = Ethernet, 802.1Q = VLAN tagging, 802.15 = WPAN (Bluetooth).

questions.question: Which IEEE standard is used for port-based network access control (authenticating a device before giving it LAN access)?
questions.explanation: 802.1X with a RADIUS server is the basis of most NAC solutions.

questions.question: A routing table entry of 0.0.0.0/0 represents:

options.A: A blocked route that silently drops all packets
options.B: A loopback route pointing back to the router itself
options.C: The default route used when no specific route matches
options.D: A broadcast route that sends packets to all hosts

questions.answer_text: The default route used when no specific route matches
questions.explanation: Packets for unknown destinations are sent to the default gateway.

questions.question: Which routing protocol is a link-state protocol?

options.A: BGP
options.B: RIP
options.C: EIGRP
options.D: OSPF

questions.answer_text: OSPF
questions.explanation: RIP is distance-vector (max 15 hops); BGP is path-vector used between autonomous systems (Internet).

questions.question: Arrange the server lifecycle stages in the correct order: (1) Operation & maintenance (2) Planning & procurement (3) Decommissioning & disposal (4) Build/provisioning & hardening
questions.explanation: Plan/procure -> build and harden -> run/patch/monitor -> decommission with secure data disposal.

questions.question: System hardening primarily means:

options.A: Adding more CPU, RAM and redundant power supplies so that the server can withstand very heavy load and attacks
options.B: Reducing the attack surface by removing unneeded services, software and accounts and applying secure settings
options.C: Installing every available software package so that all business needs are covered
options.D: Replacing the server's hard disks with SSDs to make it more resistant to failure

questions.answer_text: Reducing the attack surface by removing unneeded services, software and accounts and applying secure settings
questions.explanation: Hardening follows least functionality: only what is needed for the business role stays enabled.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a server hardening practice?

options.A: Disabling unused network ports and services
options.B: Changing default passwords and renaming default accounts
options.C: Keeping all default services enabled for compatibility
options.D: Removing unnecessary software packages from the server
options.E: Applying the principle of least privilege to all accounts

questions.answer_text: Keeping all default services enabled for compatibility
questions.explanation: Default services and accounts are common entry points for attackers.

questions.question: CIS Benchmarks are:

options.A: Network bandwidth test tools used to certify data-centre links
options.B: Audit reports issued after ISO 27001 certification of an organisation
options.C: Consensus-based secure configuration guidelines for OS, databases and applications
options.D: Performance benchmarks that compare CPU and storage speeds of server models

questions.answer_text: Consensus-based secure configuration guidelines for OS, databases and applications
questions.explanation: Published by the Center for Internet Security; widely used as hardening baselines.

questions.question: A 'golden image' in server administration refers to:

options.A: A pre-hardened, approved OS template used to build new servers consistently
options.B: The very first full backup taken of a server immediately after installation and configuration
options.C: A disk image of a failed server preserved for audit purposes
options.D: A screenshot of the console kept as evidence after go-live

questions.answer_text: A pre-hardened, approved OS template used to build new servers consistently
questions.explanation: Building from a golden image reduces configuration drift and speeds up provisioning.

questions.question: Which pair of SSH settings best hardens remote access to a Linux server?

options.A: Allow empty passwords for service accounts
options.B: Disable direct root login and use key-based authentication
options.C: Move SSH to port 23 and disable logging so attackers cannot find it
options.D: Allow root login and use password authentication

questions.answer_text: Disable direct root login and use key-based authentication
questions.explanation: PermitRootLogin no and PasswordAuthentication no (keys only) are common SSH hardening steps.

questions.question: While decommissioning a server that stored customer data, the most critical step from a data-security point of view is:

options.A: Shutting the server down gracefully before removal
options.B: Securely sanitising or destroying the storage media
options.C: Removing the server's asset labels from the rack
options.D: Updating the server's warranty and AMC records

questions.answer_text: Securely sanitising or destroying the storage media
questions.explanation: Media sanitisation (overwrite, crypto-erase, degauss or physical destruction) prevents data leakage.

questions.question: Degaussing is a data destruction method that:

options.A: Encrypts the data using a hardware-protected key
options.B: Erases magnetic media using a strong magnetic field
options.C: Compresses data and moves it to tape before deletion
options.D: Overwrites data once with zeros using software

questions.answer_text: Erases magnetic media using a strong magnetic field
questions.explanation: Degaussing is not effective on SSDs or flash memory, which store data electronically.

questions.question: Arrange the patch management steps in the correct order: (1) Test in non-production (2) Identify and assess applicable patches (3) Deploy to production (4) Get change approval (5) Verify and report
questions.explanation: Identify/assess -> test -> approve (CAB) -> deploy -> verify/report. Rollback plans are prepared before deployment.

questions.question: Patches are first applied in a test/UAT environment mainly to:

options.A: Avoid paying licence fees for the production environment
options.B: Skip the change management process for production servers by proving that it works in test
options.C: Make sure the patch does not break applications before production rollout
options.D: Get faster patch downloads from the vendor's servers

questions.answer_text: Make sure the patch does not break applications before production rollout
questions.explanation: A bad patch on production CBS servers can cause an outage.

questions.question: A 'zero-day' vulnerability is one that:

options.A: Has a CVSS score of zero
options.B: Is unknown to the vendor or has no patch available yet
options.C: Has been patched on the same day the vulnerability was announced
options.D: Affects systems only on day zero of the month

questions.answer_text: Is unknown to the vendor or has no patch available yet
questions.explanation: Attackers exploiting it have an advantage because no fix exists.

questions.question: What is a CVE?

options.A: A scoring scale used to rate how severe a vulnerability is
options.B: A vendor's signed installer package for security patches
options.C: A firewall rule format used to block known exploits
options.D: A unique public identifier for a known security vulnerability

questions.answer_text: A unique public identifier for a known security vulnerability
questions.explanation: CVE (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures) list is maintained by MITRE, e.g. CVE-2021-44228 (Log4Shell).

questions.question: Under CVSS v3, a vulnerability with base score 9.0 - 10.0 is rated:

options.A: Medium
options.B: Critical
options.C: High
options.D: Low

questions.answer_text: Critical

questions.question: The National Vulnerability Database (NVD), which enriches CVE entries with CVSS scores, is maintained by:

options.A: MITRE
options.B: OWASP
options.C: ISACA
options.D: NIST

questions.answer_text: NIST
questions.explanation: MITRE runs the CVE programme; NIST's NVD adds severity scores and details.

questions.question: A critical vulnerability is being actively exploited in the wild and affects internet-facing servers. The patch should be applied through:

options.A: A standard pre-approved change applied without any testing
options.B: The emergency change process with expedited testing and ECAB approval
options.C: No change process at all, since security fixes override governance
options.D: The next quarterly maintenance window after full regression testing

questions.answer_text: The emergency change process with expedited testing and ECAB approval
questions.explanation: Emergency changes are fast-tracked but still recorded, approved and reviewed afterwards.

questions.question: Microsoft's 'Patch Tuesday' refers to:

options.A: A fixed day each week on which all Windows servers must be rebooted
options.B: The release of cumulative patches on the last Tuesday of every quarter
options.C: Emergency out-of-band patches released only for zero-day exploits
options.D: The scheduled release of security updates on the second Tuesday of each month

questions.answer_text: The scheduled release of security updates on the second Tuesday of each month
questions.explanation: Predictable schedules help organisations plan testing and deployment.

questions.question: Which statement best describes 'proactive patching'?

options.A: Applying patches on a planned schedule before problems or exploits occur
options.B: Applying patches only after an incident has been reported and analysed
options.C: Patching only user desktops while leaving servers unchanged
options.D: Avoiding patches on stable systems to prevent unexpected outages

questions.answer_text: Applying patches on a planned schedule before problems or exploits occur
questions.explanation: Reactive patching responds after failures; proactive patching reduces exposure.

questions.question: 'Virtual patching' means:

options.A: Patching a virtual machine image instead of the underlying physical server
options.B: Downloading patches in advance but deferring installation until the next audit
options.C: Blocking exploitation of a vulnerability with a WAF/IPS rule until the real patch is applied
options.D: Applying a patch only in the test environment and simulating its effect in production using monitoring

questions.answer_text: Blocking exploitation of a vulnerability with a WAF/IPS rule until the real patch is applied
questions.explanation: It is a compensating control useful for legacy or hard-to-patch systems.

questions.question: A legacy application server cannot be patched because the vendor no longer supports it. The best compensating control is to:

options.A: Disable its logging and antivirus to improve its performance and stability until it is replaced
options.B: Isolate it in a restricted network segment with strict access rules and monitoring
options.C: Connect it directly to the internet so the vendor can support it remotely
options.D: Share its admin password with more support staff for faster fixes

questions.answer_text: Isolate it in a restricted network segment with strict access rules and monitoring
questions.explanation: Segmentation and monitoring reduce risk until the system is upgraded or retired.

questions.question: A hotfix differs from a service pack in that a hotfix:

options.A: Adds only new features, whereas a service pack contains only security fixes
options.B: Is a cumulative bundle of fixes, whereas a service pack fixes one specific issue
options.C: Fixes a specific urgent issue, whereas a service pack is a cumulative bundle of fixes
options.D: Cannot be uninstalled, whereas a service pack can always be rolled back

questions.answer_text: Fixes a specific urgent issue, whereas a service pack is a cumulative bundle of fixes
questions.explanation: Service packs/cumulative updates roll many fixes into one tested package.

questions.question: Which is usually the FIRST step in a vulnerability management programme?

options.A: Building an accurate inventory of assets
options.B: Running penetration tests on all systems
options.C: Applying every available patch immediately
options.D: Buying cyber insurance for the organisation

questions.answer_text: Building an accurate inventory of assets
questions.explanation: You cannot protect or scan what you do not know exists.

questions.question: Which statement correctly differentiates a vulnerability, a threat and a risk?

options.A: Vulnerability is a weakness; threat can exploit it; risk is the likelihood and impact of that happening
options.B: Vulnerability is the attacker; threat is the weakness; risk is the number of incidents
options.C: Threat is a weakness in a system; vulnerability is what exploits it; risk is the cost of the security controls
options.D: Risk is a weakness; threat is the likelihood; vulnerability is the business impact

questions.answer_text: Vulnerability is a weakness; threat can exploit it; risk is the likelihood and impact of that happening
questions.explanation: Risk = Likelihood x Impact; controls reduce vulnerabilities or impact.

questions.question: In vulnerability management, a 'false positive' is:

options.A: A real vulnerability that the scanner failed to report
options.B: A genuine vulnerability that has a low CVSS severity score and can safely be ignored
options.C: A vulnerability that has already been fixed by a patch
options.D: A reported vulnerability that does not actually exist on the system

questions.answer_text: A reported vulnerability that does not actually exist on the system
questions.explanation: Too many false positives waste remediation effort and cause teams to ignore real alerts.

questions.question: Why is a false negative usually more dangerous than a false positive?

options.A: It creates duplicate tickets in the vulnerability tracker
options.B: It wastes the team's time fixing issues that do not exist
options.C: It greatly increases the time taken to complete a scan
options.D: A real vulnerability goes undetected and remains exploitable

questions.answer_text: A real vulnerability goes undetected and remains exploitable
questions.explanation: False negatives give a false sense of security.

questions.question: An authenticated (credentialed) vulnerability scan is preferred over an unauthenticated scan because it:

options.A: Logs into the host and checks installed packages and settings, giving more accurate results
options.B: Can only be run from the internet, so it shows the attacker's real view
options.C: Never needs change approval because it is read-only and does not touch any production system at all
options.D: Runs without being visible to the target, so attackers cannot learn about it

questions.answer_text: Logs into the host and checks installed packages and settings, giving more accurate results
questions.explanation: Credentialed scans find missing patches and misconfigurations with fewer false positives.

questions.question: In VAPT, the main difference between Vulnerability Assessment (VA) and Penetration Testing (PT) is:

options.A: VA is done by internal staff only; PT is done only by the regulator
options.B: VA is done only on networks; PT is done only on web applications
options.C: VA identifies and lists weaknesses; PT actively tries to exploit them to prove impact
options.D: VA actively exploits weaknesses; PT only lists them without exploiting anything

questions.answer_text: VA identifies and lists weaknesses; PT actively tries to exploit them to prove impact
questions.explanation: PT is deeper and riskier, so it needs proper authorisation and scope.

questions.question: A Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) style vulnerability in a widely used logging library is best tracked across all applications using:

options.A: The server's BIOS and firmware configuration settings
options.B: A software inventory / SBOM (Software Bill of Materials)
options.C: Firewall hit counts for internet-facing servers
options.D: Network bandwidth and utilisation reports

questions.answer_text: A software inventory / SBOM (Software Bill of Materials)
questions.explanation: An SBOM lists components and versions so affected applications can be found quickly.

questions.question: A CMDB (Configuration Management Database) stores:

options.A: Network traffic logs collected from firewalls and routers
options.B: Customer transaction data from the core banking system
options.C: Configuration items (CIs) and the relationships between them
options.D: User passwords and their expiry dates for all systems

questions.answer_text: Configuration items (CIs) and the relationships between them
questions.explanation: CIs include servers, applications, databases, network devices and their dependencies.

questions.question: A configuration baseline is:

options.A: The first entry written to a server's log after installation
options.B: The factory default settings shipped by the hardware vendor with every new server model
options.C: The minimum hardware specification needed to install a server
options.D: An approved reference configuration against which systems are compared

questions.answer_text: An approved reference configuration against which systems are compared
questions.explanation: Deviations from the baseline must be justified through change control.

questions.question: Over time, several servers built from the same template have different settings due to ad-hoc manual changes. This is called:

options.A: Configuration drift
options.B: Thrashing
options.C: Scope creep
options.D: Data skew

questions.answer_text: Configuration drift
questions.explanation: Automation tools and periodic compliance scans detect and correct drift.

questions.question: Which configuration management tool is agentless and uses SSH with YAML playbooks?

options.A: Chef
options.B: SCCM
options.C: Ansible
options.D: Puppet

questions.answer_text: Ansible
questions.explanation: Puppet and Chef traditionally use agents installed on managed nodes.

questions.question: Infrastructure as Code (IaC) means:

options.A: Documenting infrastructure diagrams and server details in a shared spreadsheet maintained by the team
options.B: Writing application source code directly on production servers
options.C: Defining and provisioning infrastructure through machine-readable code files
options.D: Giving servers code names instead of descriptive hostnames

questions.answer_text: Defining and provisioning infrastructure through machine-readable code files
questions.explanation: Tools like Terraform and Ansible make builds repeatable, reviewable and version-controlled.

questions.question: Version control (e.g. Git) is essential even for Infrastructure-as-Code files because it provides:

options.A: Change history, peer review, audit trail and easy rollback to a known good state
options.B: Free hosting of infrastructure in the version control provider's cloud
options.C: Faster execution of scripts, because the repository compiles them before they are run on servers
options.D: Automatic encryption of the servers that the code builds and configures

questions.answer_text: Change history, peer review, audit trail and easy rollback to a known good state
questions.explanation: Infrastructure changes can break production just like code changes.

questions.question: In Git, which command sends local commits to a remote repository?

options.A: git status
options.B: git clone
options.C: git commit
options.D: git push

questions.answer_text: git push
questions.explanation: commit saves a snapshot locally; push uploads to remote; pull/fetch download changes.

questions.question: On a shared branch, a bad commit has already been pushed. The safest way to undo it without rewriting history is:

options.A: git reset --hard <commit> and force push
options.B: git revert <commit>
options.C: Delete the repository and recreate it
options.D: git stash

questions.answer_text: git revert <commit>
questions.explanation: revert creates a new commit that reverses the change, keeping history intact for other users.

questions.question: A rollback strategy is necessary because it:

options.A: Speeds up deployments by skipping the approval of changes
options.B: Guarantees that every change will succeed on the first attempt
options.C: Removes the need to test changes before they reach production, since any failure can be undone
options.D: Restores the system quickly to the last known good state if a change fails

questions.answer_text: Restores the system quickly to the last known good state if a change fails
questions.explanation: It limits downtime and business impact when a change goes wrong.

questions.question: When should the rollback (back-out) plan for a change be prepared?

options.A: Before the change is implemented, as part of the change request
options.B: After the post-implementation review is completed
options.C: Only after the change has failed in production
options.D: Only for emergency changes approved by the ECAB, since normal changes are already tested

questions.answer_text: Before the change is implemented, as part of the change request
questions.explanation: CABs normally reject changes without a tested back-out plan.

questions.question: Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA) is an approach in which:

options.A: Applications are built from loosely coupled, reusable services exposed through standard interfaces
options.B: Data is kept only on mainframes and accessed through terminal screens
options.C: Each user is given a dedicated server so that applications never share resources
options.D: All business functions run inside one large program that is built, tested and deployed as a single unit

questions.answer_text: Applications are built from loosely coupled, reusable services exposed through standard interfaces
questions.explanation: Services communicate over the network using contracts (e.g. SOAP/WSDL, REST).

questions.question: An Enterprise Service Bus (ESB) mainly provides:

options.A: Physical cabling and switching between servers in the data centre
options.B: Storage-level replication of data between the primary and the DR data centres in real time
options.C: Antivirus scanning and patching of endpoints across the network
options.D: Central routing, transformation and mediation of messages between applications

questions.answer_text: Central routing, transformation and mediation of messages between applications
questions.explanation: Examples: IBM Integration Bus/App Connect, MuleSoft, Oracle Service Bus.

questions.question: A bank has 10 applications that all need to talk to each other. With direct point-to-point integration, how many interfaces could be needed, compared with an ESB?

options.A: Up to 100 interfaces for point-to-point, versus 1 connection to the ESB
options.B: 20 interfaces in both cases
options.C: Up to 45 interfaces, versus 10 connections to the ESB
options.D: 10 interfaces versus 45 connections to the ESB

questions.answer_text: Up to 45 interfaces, versus 10 connections to the ESB
questions.explanation: Full mesh needs n(n-1)/2 = 10x9/2 = 45 links; with an ESB each application connects once.

questions.question: Middleware is best described as:

options.A: The middle layer of a storage array that caches data between the disks and the servers that read and write them
options.B: A backup tool that copies data between the database and tape library
options.C: Software that sits between applications and the OS/network to enable communication and data exchange
options.D: Firewall hardware placed between the internal network and the DMZ

questions.answer_text: Software that sits between applications and the OS/network to enable communication and data exchange
questions.explanation: Examples: message queues, application servers, ESBs, API gateways.

questions.question: Message-oriented middleware such as IBM MQ is preferred for many banking integrations because it:

options.A: Works only between programs running inside the same server, avoiding the network
options.B: Supports asynchronous, guaranteed delivery through queues even if the receiver is temporarily down
options.C: Sends data without any acknowledgement, which makes it faster than other methods
options.D: Requires both systems to be online at exactly the same moment, so that messages never have to be queued

questions.answer_text: Supports asynchronous, guaranteed delivery through queues even if the receiver is temporarily down
questions.explanation: Queues decouple sender and receiver in time, avoiding message loss.

questions.question: In the publish/subscribe messaging pattern:

options.A: Messages are delivered only by email to a list of subscribed users
options.B: A publisher sends a message to a topic and all subscribers of that topic receive it
options.C: A sender puts a message on a queue and exactly one receiver consumes it, after which it is removed
options.D: The receiver must keep polling the sender's database for new records

questions.answer_text: A publisher sends a message to a topic and all subscribers of that topic receive it
questions.explanation: Point-to-point queues deliver each message to one consumer; topics fan out to many.

questions.question: Which statement best contrasts ESB-based SOA with microservices?

options.A: Microservices always route every call through a central ESB, which holds the shared business logic for all services
options.B: ESB services are always deployed independently in containers, unlike microservices
options.C: ESB uses a central 'smart pipe'; microservices use 'smart endpoints and dumb pipes' with decentralised data
options.D: Both approaches require a single shared database used by all services

questions.answer_text: ESB uses a central 'smart pipe'; microservices use 'smart endpoints and dumb pipes' with decentralised data
questions.explanation: The central ESB can become a bottleneck/single point of failure; microservices own their data and logic.

questions.question: An API (Application Programming Interface) is:

options.A: A defined set of rules that lets one software application request services or data from another
options.B: A physical port on a server used to connect external devices
options.C: A special index that speeds up data access inside a relational database
options.D: A graphical screen through which end users enter and view transactions in a banking application

questions.answer_text: A defined set of rules that lets one software application request services or data from another
questions.explanation: APIs hide internal implementation and expose only what is needed.

questions.question: APIs classified by who can access them include:

options.A: Static, Dynamic, Volatile and Persistent APIs
options.B: Open (public), Partner, Internal (private) and Composite APIs
options.C: REST, SOAP, GraphQL and gRPC APIs, based on the protocol they use
options.D: Hot, Warm, Cold and Archive APIs

questions.answer_text: Open (public), Partner, Internal (private) and Composite APIs
questions.explanation: REST/SOAP/GraphQL are styles/protocols, not access-based types.

questions.question: In SOA, the XML document that describes a SOAP web service's operations, messages and endpoint is the:

options.A: JSON Schema
options.B: WSDL
options.C: YAML manifest
options.D: UDDI

questions.answer_text: WSDL
questions.explanation: WSDL = Web Services Description Language. UDDI was a registry to publish and discover services.

questions.question: A payment message is retried by the middleware after a timeout, but the first attempt had actually succeeded. Which design prevents the customer being debited twice?

options.A: Increasing the middleware timeout to ten minutes so that retries happen less often
options.B: Switching the integration from TCP to UDP
options.C: Disabling retries in all systems permanently
options.D: Idempotent processing using a unique transaction reference

questions.answer_text: Idempotent processing using a unique transaction reference
questions.explanation: The receiver checks the unique reference and ignores duplicates, so retries are safe.

questions.question: Monitoring and control of IT systems is important mainly because it:

options.A: Removes the need for change management since every change is watched live
options.B: Detects performance problems, failures and security events early so action can be taken before business impact
options.C: Eliminates all software bugs by stopping faulty code before it is deployed
options.D: Replaces the need for backups and DR, because every failure is detected and prevented before any data can be lost

questions.answer_text: Detects performance problems, failures and security events early so action can be taken before business impact
questions.explanation: Monitoring supports SLAs, capacity planning, incident detection and audit.

questions.question: Capacity management in IT operations focuses on:

options.A: Writing and testing application code for new business requirements
options.B: Recording every password change made by users across all systems
options.C: Ensuring IT resources meet current and future business demand cost-effectively
options.D: Approving all change requests before they are implemented in production

questions.answer_text: Ensuring IT resources meet current and future business demand cost-effectively
questions.explanation: Trend analysis of CPU, memory, storage and network usage helps plan upgrades before shortages.

questions.question: Under ITIL, a low-risk, pre-authorised, frequently repeated change (e.g. adding a user to a standard group) is a:

options.A: Normal change
options.B: Major change
options.C: Emergency change
options.D: Standard change

questions.answer_text: Standard change
questions.explanation: Standard changes follow a pre-approved procedure and do not need CAB review each time.

questions.question: A 'normal' change is one that:

options.A: Is pre-approved and can be implemented without any further review
options.B: Is implemented first and then approved retrospectively by the CAB
options.C: Must be assessed and authorised (usually by CAB) before implementation
options.D: Can be implemented only by vendors under an annual maintenance contract

questions.answer_text: Must be assessed and authorised (usually by CAB) before implementation
questions.explanation: Normal changes follow the full change lifecycle.

questions.question: An urgent change needed to fix a critical production outage is usually approved by:

options.A: No one, it is done without approval
options.B: Emergency CAB (ECAB)
options.C: The service desk agent
options.D: The developer who wrote the fix

questions.answer_text: Emergency CAB (ECAB)
questions.explanation: ECAB is a smaller group that can meet quickly; the change is still documented and reviewed later.

questions.question: The main role of the Change Advisory Board (CAB) is to:

options.A: Assess, prioritise and advise on authorisation of non-standard (normal) changes
options.B: Write, test and deploy the code for all approved changes in the production environment
options.C: Handle all password reset and access requests from users
options.D: Perform daily backups before any change is implemented

questions.answer_text: Assess, prioritise and advise on authorisation of non-standard (normal) changes
questions.explanation: CAB brings together technical, security and business views to judge risk and impact.

questions.question: Which group is most appropriate as CAB members for a change to the core banking system?

options.A: Application owner, infrastructure, security, business user and service desk representatives
options.B: Only the branch staff who will use the changed screens
options.C: Only the developer who made the change, since they understand its technical details better than anyone
options.D: Only the vendor's account manager and sales team for the application

questions.answer_text: Application owner, infrastructure, security, business user and service desk representatives
questions.explanation: A cross-functional CAB catches dependencies and business impact that one team might miss.

questions.question: In change management, RFC stands for:

options.A: Rollback Failure Code
options.B: Release Forward Control
options.C: Request for Comments
options.D: Request for Change

questions.answer_text: Request for Change
questions.explanation: An RFC is the formal proposal describing what, why, when, risk, impact and back-out plan.

questions.question: Arrange the change lifecycle in the correct order: (1) Implement (2) Raise RFC (3) Post-Implementation Review and closure (4) Assess impact and risk (5) Authorise (CAB) (6) Build and test
questions.explanation: RFC -> assessment -> authorisation -> build/test -> implement -> review/close.

questions.question: A Post-Implementation Review (PIR) is done to:

options.A: Approve the change before it is implemented in the production environment
options.B: Check whether the change met its objectives and capture lessons learned
options.C: Write and unit-test the code required for the change
options.D: Raise the original request for change on behalf of users

questions.answer_text: Check whether the change met its objectives and capture lessons learned
questions.explanation: PIR is mandatory especially for failed or emergency changes.

questions.question: During a monitoring review, a change to a production firewall is found that has no approved RFC. It should be treated as:

options.A: An unauthorised change to be investigated as an incident/security event
options.B: A normal part of routine maintenance by the network team
options.C: A standard change that does not need any approval or record
options.D: Acceptable, as long as the firewall is still working normally and no incident is reported

questions.answer_text: An unauthorised change to be investigated as an incident/security event
questions.explanation: Unauthorised changes break change control and may indicate malicious activity.

questions.question: A 'change freeze' period (e.g. during year-end closing) means:

options.A: Only database changes are allowed while application changes are blocked
options.B: No non-emergency changes are allowed to production during that period
options.C: Changes can be made without approval to finish year-end work quickly
options.D: All pending changes must be implemented together during that period

questions.answer_text: No non-emergency changes are allowed to production during that period
questions.explanation: It protects stability during business-critical periods.

questions.question: A calendar listing all approved changes with their planned implementation dates is called the:

options.A: Known Error Database (KEDB)
options.B: Service catalogue
options.C: Change schedule (Forward Schedule of Changes)
options.D: Risk register of planned implementation activities

questions.answer_text: Change schedule (Forward Schedule of Changes)
questions.explanation: It helps avoid conflicting changes and informs stakeholders of planned downtime.

questions.question: In the change management lifecycle, how does impact assessment differ from risk assessment?

options.A: Risk assessment is needed only for hardware changes; impact assessment only for software changes
options.B: Impact assessment estimates the likelihood of failure and its consequences; risk assessment studies which services and users are affected and how much
options.C: Impact assessment is done only after implementation; risk assessment is done only before implementation
options.D: Impact assessment studies what services and users are affected and how much; risk assessment estimates likelihood of failure and its consequences

questions.answer_text: Impact assessment studies what services and users are affected and how much; risk assessment estimates likelihood of failure and its consequences
questions.explanation: Together they decide the change category, approvals needed and testing depth.

questions.question: Which change is likely to carry the HIGHEST risk rating?

options.A: Changing the desktop wallpaper policy for all branch computers
options.B: Upgrading the core banking database version during business hours with no tested rollback
options.C: Adding a new network printer to a single branch PC during lunch hours, with a vendor engineer present
options.D: Resetting the password of one user who has forgotten it

questions.answer_text: Upgrading the core banking database version during business hours with no tested rollback
questions.explanation: High business impact + high complexity + no back-out = high risk.

questions.question: In change management, segregation of duties requires that:

options.A: The developer of a change should not approve and deploy it alone to production
options.B: Only vendors should deploy changes so that bank staff are not responsible
options.C: Changes should not be documented, so that duties remain separate
options.D: The same person should write, approve and deploy every change for accountability

questions.answer_text: The developer of a change should not approve and deploy it alone to production
questions.explanation: Separating maker and checker reduces fraud and errors.

questions.question: Planned changes to production are usually scheduled:

options.A: During peak business hours when support staff are available
options.B: At any time, without informing users in advance
options.C: Only on the first working day of every month
options.D: In an agreed maintenance window with low business activity

questions.answer_text: In an agreed maintenance window with low business activity
questions.explanation: Low-traffic windows reduce the impact of downtime or failure.

questions.question: Release management is mainly concerned with:

options.A: Planning, scheduling and controlling the build, test and deployment of releases
options.B: Recording customer complaints and tracking them to closure
options.C: Approving every request for change raised by the business before it is built and tested
options.D: Purchasing hardware and software licences for new projects

questions.answer_text: Planning, scheduling and controlling the build, test and deployment of releases
questions.explanation: It makes sure the right versions reach production in a controlled way.

questions.question: How is a 'release' related to 'changes'?

options.A: A release is the back-out plan used when a change fails
options.B: A release replaces the need for individual changes to be assessed and approved by the CAB
options.C: A release is a single bug report raised by a user after go-live
options.D: A release is a set of one or more authorised changes packaged and deployed together

questions.answer_text: A release is a set of one or more authorised changes packaged and deployed together
questions.explanation: Change management authorises; release management packages and deploys.

questions.question: What is the usual order of environments a release moves through?

options.A: Development -> Production -> Test/QA -> UAT/Staging
options.B: Development -> Test/QA -> UAT/Staging -> Production
options.C: Production -> UAT -> Test -> Development
options.D: Test -> Development -> Production -> UAT

questions.answer_text: Development -> Test/QA -> UAT/Staging -> Production
questions.explanation: Each stage adds confidence before the change reaches customers.

questions.question: A staging environment is important before production because it:

options.A: Stores copies of production backups for quick restoration
options.B: Is where developers write, compile and unit-test their code every day before check-in
options.C: Is used only for training new staff on the application
options.D: Mirrors production closely so final validation catches issues before go-live

questions.answer_text: Mirrors production closely so final validation catches issues before go-live
questions.explanation: Differences between staging and production are a common cause of failed releases.

questions.question: In Blue/Green deployment:

options.A: Servers are upgraded one small batch at a time while the remaining servers continue to serve users normally
options.B: The new version is first given to a small percentage of users and gradually expanded
options.C: The new version is deployed to all servers at the same instant, with no fallback environment
options.D: Two identical environments exist; traffic is switched from the old (blue) to the new (green) after testing

questions.answer_text: Two identical environments exist; traffic is switched from the old (blue) to the new (green) after testing
questions.explanation: Rollback is simply switching traffic back, giving near-zero downtime.

questions.question: The biggest challenge in using Blue/Green deployment for a core banking system is usually:

options.A: Buying enough network switches to connect the two environments
options.B: Training branch users on the colour coding of the two environments
options.C: Keeping a shared database schema and data compatible with both old and new versions
options.D: Getting separate software licences for the blue and green application servers

questions.answer_text: Keeping a shared database schema and data compatible with both old and new versions
questions.explanation: Database changes must be backward compatible (expand-contract approach) so traffic can switch back safely.

questions.question: A canary release means:

options.A: Releasing the new version only in the test environment for a trial period
options.B: Releasing the new version only on weekends when transaction volumes are low
options.C: Releasing the new version to a small group of users first and expanding if it behaves well
options.D: Releasing the new version to all users at once and rolling back if problems appear

questions.answer_text: Releasing the new version to a small group of users first and expanding if it behaves well
questions.explanation: Problems affect only a small group and can be rolled back quickly.

questions.question: In a rolling deployment:

options.A: A full duplicate environment is built and traffic is switched
options.B: All servers are shut down and updated together in one window
options.C: Servers are updated in batches while the rest keep serving users
options.D: Only the database is updated while application servers stay the same

questions.answer_text: Servers are updated in batches while the rest keep serving users
questions.explanation: It avoids full downtime but both versions run together for some time.

questions.question: The 'big bang' deployment approach means:

options.A: The system is released module by module
options.B: The old and new systems run in parallel for several months before the old one is retired
options.C: The whole new system goes live at once, replacing the old one
options.D: Users are moved gradually

questions.answer_text: The whole new system goes live at once, replacing the old one
questions.explanation: It is simple but risky, because any failure affects everyone at the same time.

questions.question: Feature flags (feature toggles) allow teams to:

options.A: Delete old releases automatically after deployment
options.B: Turn features on or off at runtime without redeploying code
options.C: Encrypt source code before storing it in the repository
options.D: Skip testing of features that are hidden from users

questions.answer_text: Turn features on or off at runtime without redeploying code
questions.explanation: Flags support dark launches, canaries and quick disabling of a faulty feature.

questions.question: Running the old and new systems together for a period and comparing outputs before switching over is called:

options.A: Parallel run
options.B: Hot fix
options.C: Canary release
options.D: Big bang cutover

questions.answer_text: Parallel run
questions.explanation: Safe but costly; common for CBS migrations and accounting systems.

questions.question: Under Semantic Versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH), a backward-compatible bug fix to version 2.4.1 should be released as:
questions.explanation: MAJOR for breaking changes, MINOR for new compatible features, PATCH for compatible fixes.

questions.question: Under Semantic Versioning, a change that breaks backward compatibility of an API requires incrementing the:

options.A: MINOR version
options.B: PATCH version
options.C: Build number only
options.D: MAJOR version

questions.answer_text: MAJOR version
questions.explanation: Consumers can tell from a major version jump that they may need to change their code.

questions.question: In Git, a 'tag' is commonly used to:

options.A: Encrypt the repository before pushing it
options.B: Merge two repositories into a single one
options.C: Delete a branch after it has been merged into the main branch
options.D: Mark a specific commit as a release point (e.g. v2.4.0)

questions.answer_text: Mark a specific commit as a release point (e.g. v2.4.0)
questions.explanation: Tags make it easy to rebuild or roll back to an exact released version.

questions.question: A secure repository holding the authorised, approved versions of all software released to production is called the:

options.A: Definitive Media Library (DML)
options.B: Known Error Database (KEDB)
options.C: Forward schedule of changes
options.D: Configuration baseline

questions.answer_text: Definitive Media Library (DML)
questions.explanation: Builds for production are taken only from the DML to avoid untested or tampered binaries.

questions.question: A good rollback plan for a database upgrade should include:

options.A: Deleting the old version immediately after go-live to avoid confusion
options.B: Disabling monitoring during the change so that false alerts are not raised
options.C: A verified backup/snapshot before the change, tested back-out steps and a clear go/no-go time limit
options.D: Only the vendor's escalation phone number, since the vendor will handle any failure during the upgrade window

questions.answer_text: A verified backup/snapshot before the change, tested back-out steps and a clear go/no-go time limit
questions.explanation: Defining in advance when to abort prevents extended outages.

questions.question: Fixing a failed release by quickly deploying another corrective change instead of reverting to the previous version is called:

options.A: Big bang
options.B: Rollback
options.C: Freeze
options.D: Roll-forward

questions.answer_text: Roll-forward
questions.explanation: Roll-forward is used when reverting is harder or riskier than fixing forward.

questions.question: In IT service management, what is the difference between incident management and problem management?

options.A: Both incident and problem management aim only at finding the root cause
options.B: Incident management restores service quickly; problem management finds and removes the root cause
options.C: Incident management deals only with hardware; problem management only with software
options.D: Incident management finds and removes the root cause; problem management restores the service as quickly as possible

questions.answer_text: Incident management restores service quickly; problem management finds and removes the root cause
questions.explanation: A recurring incident triggers a problem record and RCA.

questions.question: A problem whose root cause has been identified and documented along with a workaround is called a:

options.A: Standard change
options.B: Known error
options.C: Major incident
options.D: Service request

questions.answer_text: Known error
questions.explanation: Known errors are stored in the Known Error Database (KEDB) to help resolve future incidents faster.

questions.question: Which techniques are commonly used for Root Cause Analysis (RCA)?

options.A: Hashing and salting
options.B: Round robin and least-connections algorithms
options.C: 5 Whys and Fishbone (Ishikawa) diagram
options.D: Paging and segmentation

questions.answer_text: 5 Whys and Fishbone (Ishikawa) diagram
questions.explanation: Both drill down from the symptom to the underlying cause.

questions.question: In ITIL, incident priority is usually derived from:

options.A: Impact and urgency
options.B: Time of day only
options.C: Number of emails received
options.D: The user's designation only

questions.answer_text: Impact and urgency
questions.explanation: High impact + high urgency = critical priority (P1).

questions.question: A user asking for a password reset or access to a shared folder is an example of a:

options.A: Change advisory
options.B: Problem
options.C: Incident
options.D: Service request

questions.answer_text: Service request
questions.explanation: Incidents are unplanned interruptions or reductions in service quality.

questions.question: ITIL stands for:

options.A: Integrated Technology Information Ledger
options.B: International Telecom Infrastructure Law
options.C: Information Technology Infrastructure Library
options.D: IT Incident Logging

questions.answer_text: Information Technology Infrastructure Library
questions.explanation: ITIL is a widely used framework of IT service management best practices.

questions.question: The service desk in ITIL acts as:

options.A: The team that owns and runs the data centre
options.B: The board that approves all changes to production
options.C: The single point of contact between IT and users
options.D: The internal audit function for IT controls

questions.answer_text: The single point of contact between IT and users
questions.explanation: It logs incidents and requests and routes them to resolver groups.

questions.question: The three basic goals of information security (CIA triad) are:

options.A: Compliance, Integrity, Audit
options.B: Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability
options.C: Control, Identity, Access
options.D: Confidentiality, Identity, Authentication

questions.answer_text: Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability
questions.explanation: Every security control protects one or more of these three properties.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of protecting INTEGRITY?

options.A: Keeping the location of the server room confidential
options.B: Using a hash/MAC to ensure a fund transfer amount is not altered in transit
options.C: Encrypting customer data so that outsiders cannot read it even if they steal it
options.D: Using a UPS and redundant servers to keep the system running

questions.answer_text: Using a hash/MAC to ensure a fund transfer amount is not altered in transit
questions.explanation: Integrity = data is accurate and not modified without authorisation.

questions.question: A DDoS attack that makes internet banking unreachable mainly violates:

options.A: Availability
options.B: Non-repudiation
options.C: Integrity
options.D: Confidentiality

questions.answer_text: Availability
questions.explanation: Availability means authorised users can access systems when needed.

questions.question: Leakage of customers' account statements to an unauthorised person violates:

options.A: Accountability only
options.B: Integrity
options.C: Availability
options.D: Confidentiality

questions.answer_text: Confidentiality
questions.explanation: Confidentiality = information is disclosed only to authorised parties.

questions.question: Non-repudiation ensures that:

options.A: A sender cannot later deny having sent a message or authorised a transaction
options.B: Data and systems remain available to authorised users whenever they need them
options.C: Only administrators are allowed to read the security logs
options.D: Users cannot reuse any of their last five passwords

questions.answer_text: A sender cannot later deny having sent a message or authorised a transaction
questions.explanation: Digital signatures with the sender's private key provide non-repudiation.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes authentication and authorisation?

options.A: Authorisation always happens before authentication
options.B: Authorisation verifies who you are; authentication decides what you are then allowed to do
options.C: Authentication verifies who you are; authorisation decides what you are allowed to do
options.D: Both mean verifying a password

questions.answer_text: Authentication verifies who you are; authorisation decides what you are allowed to do
questions.explanation: First identity is proved (authentication), then permissions are checked (authorisation).

questions.question: In AAA security, the three A's stand for:

options.A: Authentication, Authorisation, Accounting
options.B: Authentication, Access, Administration
options.C: Access, Audit, Availability
options.D: Authorisation, Availability, Accuracy

questions.answer_text: Authentication, Authorisation, Accounting
questions.explanation: Accounting records what the user did (logs) for audit and billing.

questions.question: Biometric authentication (fingerprint, iris, face) is based on:

options.A: Somewhere you are
options.B: Something you know
options.C: Something you are
options.D: Something you have

questions.answer_text: Something you are
questions.explanation: Password/PIN = something you know; token/card/phone = something you have.

questions.question: Which of the following is a TRUE two-factor authentication?

options.A: Password plus OTP sent to the registered mobile
options.B: Password plus a 4-digit transaction PIN
options.C: Two different passwords entered one after another
options.D: PIN plus an answer to a security question

questions.answer_text: Password plus OTP sent to the registered mobile
questions.explanation: 2FA must combine different factor types; password and PIN are both 'something you know'.

questions.question: A smart card used to log in to a terminal is an example of which authentication factor?

options.A: Something you know
options.B: Something you have
options.C: Something you are
options.D: Something you do

questions.answer_text: Something you have
questions.explanation: It is a physical possession factor, often combined with a PIN for 2FA.

questions.question: The main purpose of an account lockout after a fixed number of failed login attempts is to:

options.A: Force users to choose a new and stronger username
options.B: Save server memory used by inactive login sessions
options.C: Defend against brute-force and password-guessing attacks
options.D: Reduce network traffic generated by repeated logins

questions.answer_text: Defend against brute-force and password-guessing attacks
questions.explanation: Lockout or progressive delays make online guessing impractical.

questions.question: Single Sign-On (SSO) allows a user to:

options.A: Access applications without any authentication from the office network
options.B: Log in once and access multiple authorised applications without logging in again
options.C: Share one login account among many users of the same department
options.D: Use a single strong password that never expires across all the applications they use

questions.answer_text: Log in once and access multiple authorised applications without logging in again
questions.explanation: SSO improves user experience but makes the central identity provider a critical asset.

questions.question: Kerberos authentication is based on:

options.A: Passwords sent in clear text to each application server
options.B: One-time passwords sent by SMS for every login
options.C: Records stored on a public blockchain for verification
options.D: Tickets issued by a trusted Key Distribution Center (KDC)

questions.answer_text: Tickets issued by a trusted Key Distribution Center (KDC)
questions.explanation: Kerberos (port 88) is used by Active Directory; it needs synchronised clocks.

questions.question: Automatic logout of a CBS terminal after a period of inactivity mainly protects against:

options.A: Virus infection through USB drives
options.B: Network congestion during peak hours
options.C: Misuse of an unattended, logged-in session
options.D: Hard disk failure on the branch terminal

questions.answer_text: Misuse of an unattended, logged-in session
questions.explanation: Session timeout reduces the risk of someone else using an open session.

questions.question: The principle of least privilege means:

options.A: Users get only the minimum access required to perform their job
options.B: Users get all access that their department has, to avoid delays
options.C: Access rights are given based on seniority and length of service
options.D: Access is granted once at joining and never reviewed afterwards

questions.answer_text: Users get only the minimum access required to perform their job
questions.explanation: It limits damage from mistakes, insider misuse and compromised accounts.

questions.question: Why do organisations maintain segregation of duties?

options.A: So that passwords are no longer needed for sensitive transactions
options.B: So that no single person can complete a critical transaction alone, reducing fraud and error
options.C: So that every employee is trained to perform every task in the process when colleagues are absent
options.D: So that fewer employees are needed to complete each business process

questions.answer_text: So that no single person can complete a critical transaction alone, reducing fraud and error
questions.explanation: E.g. the person who creates a payee should not also approve the payment.

questions.question: In CBS, the 'maker-checker' concept means:

options.A: Transactions are entered daily but checked only at the year-end audit
options.B: Only the system administrator is allowed to enter and verify transactions
options.C: The same user enters a transaction and then approves it after checking
options.D: One user enters a transaction and a different authorised user verifies it

questions.answer_text: One user enters a transaction and a different authorised user verifies it
questions.explanation: Maker-checker is a dual-control implementation of segregation of duties.

questions.question: In a bank, access in CBS is granted according to job functions such as teller, officer or branch manager. This is:

options.A: Discretionary Access Control (DAC)
options.B: Mandatory Access Control (MAC)
options.C: Rule-Based Access Control
options.D: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)

questions.answer_text: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
questions.explanation: RBAC simplifies administration: permissions attach to roles and users are assigned roles.

questions.question: In Mandatory Access Control (MAC), access decisions are based on:

options.A: The user's job role, with permissions attached to each role
options.B: The data owner's own decision about which users may access each object they own
options.C: Security labels/classifications assigned by the system, not by the data owner
options.D: The time of day and the location from which the user logs in

questions.answer_text: Security labels/classifications assigned by the system, not by the data owner
questions.explanation: MAC is used in military/high-security systems; DAC lets owners decide.

questions.question: Rule-based access control, where traffic is allowed or denied by predefined rules, is typically implemented by:

options.A: UPS systems
options.B: CCTV cameras
options.C: Biometric readers at entry doors
options.D: Firewalls and router ACLs

questions.answer_text: Firewalls and router ACLs
questions.explanation: Rules apply to everyone equally regardless of identity.

questions.question: An access method using smart cards, security guards and guard dogs is an example of:

options.A: Physical access control
options.B: Network access control
options.C: Administrative control only
options.D: Logical access control

questions.answer_text: Physical access control
questions.explanation: Physical controls protect premises and hardware; logical controls protect systems and data.

questions.question: Which of the following is a LOGICAL access control?

options.A: Biometric door lock on the server room
options.B: Security guard checking ID cards at the gate
options.C: Mantrap at the data centre entrance
options.D: User ID and password with role-based permissions

questions.answer_text: User ID and password with role-based permissions
questions.explanation: Logical (technical) controls include passwords, ACLs, encryption, firewalls.

questions.question: Periodic user access review (recertification) in CBS is done mainly to:

options.A: Force every user to change their password periodically
options.B: Speed up the login process for users
options.C: Remove excess, outdated or dormant access rights
options.D: Create additional user IDs for new joiners

questions.answer_text: Remove excess, outdated or dormant access rights
questions.explanation: Transfers and role changes often leave users with access they no longer need ('privilege creep').

questions.question: Privileged Access Management (PAM) solutions help by:

options.A: Vaulting admin passwords, granting just-in-time access and recording privileged sessions
options.B: Disabling all logging for administrator accounts to protect their privacy
options.C: Replacing the perimeter firewall with host-based firewalls
options.D: Giving every user local administrator rights so that support calls for installations are reduced

questions.answer_text: Vaulting admin passwords, granting just-in-time access and recording privileged sessions
questions.explanation: Privileged accounts are the top target for attackers and insiders.

questions.question: In Active Directory, the top-most logical container holding one or more domain trees is the:

options.A: Group Policy Object
options.B: Forest
options.C: Site
options.D: Organisational Unit (OU)

questions.answer_text: Forest
questions.explanation: Forest > Tree > Domain > OU. The forest is the security boundary.

questions.question: In Active Directory, an Organisational Unit (OU) is mainly used to:

options.A: Issue Kerberos tickets to users and computers in the domain
options.B: Store the Active Directory database file (NTDS.dit) for the whole domain
options.C: Organise objects and apply Group Policy or delegate administration
options.D: Replicate directory data between different physical sites

questions.answer_text: Organise objects and apply Group Policy or delegate administration
questions.explanation: OUs mirror administrative structure (e.g. by region or department).

questions.question: Data validation checks at the time of input (e.g. rejecting an invalid IFSC) are what type of control?

options.A: Preventive
options.B: Deterrent
options.C: Corrective
options.D: Detective

questions.answer_text: Preventive
questions.explanation: They stop errors from entering the system.

questions.question: Taking regular data backups is classified as which type of control?

options.A: Corrective (recovery) control
options.B: Preventive (protective) control
options.C: Deterrent control
options.D: Detective control

questions.answer_text: Corrective (recovery) control
questions.explanation: Backups do not stop an incident; they help restore after it.

questions.question: Parity bits added to data during transmission mainly ensure:

options.A: Compression of data to save bandwidth
options.B: Detection of errors so data accuracy is maintained
options.C: Faster transmission of data over the network
options.D: Encryption of the data so that it cannot be read in transit

questions.answer_text: Detection of errors so data accuracy is maintained
questions.explanation: Parity is a detective control for integrity/accuracy of data.

questions.question: CCTV cameras, intrusion detection systems and audit logs are examples of:

options.A: Compensating controls
options.B: Corrective controls
options.C: Preventive controls
options.D: Detective controls

questions.answer_text: Detective controls
questions.explanation: They identify that something has happened or is happening.

questions.question: Which cybersecurity concept uses multiple layers of defensive controls so that if one fails, others still protect the asset?

options.A: Defense in depth
options.B: Security through obscurity
options.C: Single point of control
options.D: Zero day

questions.answer_text: Defense in depth
questions.explanation: E.g. perimeter firewall + IPS + endpoint protection + access control + encryption + monitoring.

questions.question: A warning banner on a login screen stating that unauthorised access is a punishable offence is a:

options.A: Recovery control
options.B: Deterrent control
options.C: Detective control
options.D: Corrective control

questions.answer_text: Deterrent control
questions.explanation: Deterrents discourage attackers but do not technically block them.

questions.question: What is the difference between standards and guidelines in a security policy framework?

options.A: Guidelines are mandatory requirements; standards are recommended practices
options.B: Standards apply only to vendors; guidelines apply only to employees
options.C: Standards are mandatory requirements; guidelines are recommended practices
options.D: Both standards and guidelines are optional suggestions for staff

questions.answer_text: Standards are mandatory requirements; guidelines are recommended practices
questions.explanation: Hierarchy: Policy -> Standards -> Procedures (step-by-step) -> Guidelines (advisory).

questions.question: ISO/IEC 27001 is an international standard for:

options.A: Business Continuity Management System (BCMS)
options.B: Information Security Management System (ISMS)
options.C: Quality Management System (QMS) for manufacturing
options.D: IT Service Management System (SMS)

questions.answer_text: Information Security Management System (ISMS)
questions.explanation: ISO 9001 = quality, ISO 22301 = business continuity, ISO 20000 = IT service management.

questions.question: Annex A of ISO/IEC 27001:2022 contains how many controls, grouped into how many themes?

options.A: 93 controls in 14 domains
options.B: 114 controls in 14 domains
options.C: 114 controls in 4 themes
options.D: 93 controls in 4 themes

questions.answer_text: 93 controls in 4 themes
questions.explanation: Themes: Organisational (37), People (8), Physical (14), Technological (34). 114/14 was the 2013 version.

questions.question: Which ISO standard specifies requirements for a Business Continuity Management System?

options.B: ISO 9001

questions.explanation: ISO 31000 gives risk management guidelines.

questions.question: ISO/IEC 27002 provides:

options.A: The certification requirements against which an ISMS is audited
options.B: Requirements for establishing a business continuity management system
options.C: Specific security controls for protecting PII in public clouds
options.D: Guidance / code of practice for implementing information security controls

questions.answer_text: Guidance / code of practice for implementing information security controls
questions.explanation: Organisations are certified against 27001; 27002 explains how to implement controls.

questions.question: In an ISO 27001 ISMS, the document listing which Annex A controls are applicable, with justification for inclusion or exclusion, is the:

options.A: Service Level Agreement (SLA)
options.B: Statement of Applicability (SoA)
