options.C: Business Impact Analysis (BIA)
options.D: Risk treatment register

questions.answer_text: Statement of Applicability (SoA)
questions.explanation: The SoA links risk treatment decisions to selected controls and is a key audit document.

questions.question: The COBIT framework for IT governance and management is published by:

options.A: PCI SSC
options.B: ISACA
options.C: NIST
options.D: ISO

questions.answer_text: ISACA
questions.explanation: ISACA also runs CISA/CISM certifications. ISO 27001 is from ISO/IEC.

questions.question: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 (2024) added which new core function to Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond and Recover?

options.A: Govern
options.B: Audit
options.C: Encrypt
options.D: Comply

questions.answer_text: Govern
questions.explanation: Govern covers strategy, roles, policy and supply-chain risk oversight.

questions.question: PCI DSS compliance is mandatory for organisations that:

options.A: Use open-source software in their systems
options.B: Operate ATMs that dispense cash without cards
options.C: Store, process or transmit payment card data
options.D: Have more than 100 employees on their payroll

questions.answer_text: Store, process or transmit payment card data
questions.explanation: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard is managed by the PCI Security Standards Council.

questions.question: RBI issued the 'Cyber Security Framework in Banks' circular, requiring a board-approved cyber security policy and a C-SOC, in:

options.A: April 2024
options.B: March 2011
options.C: January 2020
options.D: June 2016

questions.answer_text: June 2016
questions.explanation: It required cyber security policy distinct from IT policy, C-SOC, Cyber Crisis Management Plan and incident reporting.

questions.question: Under RBI's cyber security framework, banks must report unusual cyber security incidents to RBI within:

options.A: 2 to 6 hours
options.B: 7 days
options.C: 30 days
options.D: 24 to 48 hours

questions.answer_text: 2 to 6 hours
questions.explanation: Prompt reporting helps RBI and other banks respond to spreading threats.

questions.question: As per CERT-In directions of April 2022, service providers and organisations must report specified cyber incidents to CERT-In within:

options.A: 15 days
options.B: 6 hours of noticing
options.C: 24 hours of noticing the incident
options.D: 72 hours

questions.answer_text: 6 hours of noticing
questions.explanation: The directions also require ICT system logs to be kept securely for 180 days within India.

questions.question: Under the CERT-In directions (2022), ICT system logs must be maintained for a rolling period of:

options.A: 30 days
options.B: 180 days
options.C: 5 years
options.D: 90 days

questions.answer_text: 180 days
questions.explanation: Logs must be kept within Indian jurisdiction and shared with CERT-In when asked.

questions.question: RBI's Master Direction on 'Information Technology Governance, Risk, Controls and Assurance Practices' (November 2023) came into effect from:

options.A: 1 January 2023
options.B: 1 April 2021
options.C: 1 October 2025
options.D: 1 April 2024

questions.answer_text: 1 April 2024
questions.explanation: It consolidated earlier IT governance guidelines for banks, NBFCs and other regulated entities.

questions.question: Under RBI IT governance guidelines, the board-level committee that oversees IT strategy and IT risk is the:

options.A: IT Strategy Committee
options.B: Branch Expansion Committee
options.C: Customer Service Committee
options.D: Audit Committee of Executives

questions.answer_text: IT Strategy Committee
questions.explanation: It is supported by an IT Steering Committee at the management level.

questions.question: To avoid conflict of interest, RBI guidance says the CISO should NOT report to:

options.A: The head of IT operations
options.B: The Chief Risk Officer
options.C: The Executive Director overseeing risk
options.D: The Board / risk management

questions.answer_text: The head of IT operations
questions.explanation: The CISO must be independent of IT operations, which they are expected to oversee from a security angle.

questions.question: The Information Technology Act, 2000 is administered by which ministry?

options.A: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
options.B: Ministry of Finance (Department of Financial Services)
options.C: Ministry of Home Affairs (Cyber and Information Security)
options.D: Ministry of Communications (Department of Telecommunications)

questions.answer_text: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
questions.explanation: CERT-In also functions under MeitY.

questions.question: The government banned 59 Chinese mobile apps in 2020 under which provision?

options.A: Section 66A of the IT Act, 2000
options.B: Section 43 of the IT Act, 2000
options.C: Section 69A of the IT Act, 2000
options.D: Section 124A of the IPC

questions.answer_text: Section 69A of the IT Act, 2000
questions.explanation: Section 69A allows blocking public access to information in the interest of sovereignty and security.

questions.question: Under the IT Act, 2000, identity theft (fraudulent use of someone's password or digital signature) is punishable under:

options.A: Section 72
options.B: Section 66C
options.C: Section 66F
options.D: Section 69A

questions.answer_text: Section 66C
questions.explanation: 66D = cheating by personation using a computer; 66F = cyber terrorism.

questions.question: CERT-In is the national nodal agency for cyber incident response under which section of the IT Act?

options.A: Section 70B
options.B: Section 66E
options.C: Section 43
options.D: Section 79

questions.answer_text: Section 70B
questions.explanation: Section 70A deals with NCIIPC, which protects Critical Information Infrastructure.

questions.question: Under the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023, the entity that decides the purpose and means of processing personal data is the:

options.A: Data Principal
options.B: Consent Manager
options.C: Data Processor
options.D: Data Fiduciary

questions.answer_text: Data Fiduciary
questions.explanation: A bank processing customer data is a Data Fiduciary; the customer is the Data Principal.

questions.question: Under the DPDP Act, 2023, the individual to whom the personal data relates is called the:

options.A: Data Controller
options.B: Data Owner
options.C: Data Principal
options.D: Data Fiduciary

questions.answer_text: Data Principal
questions.explanation: For a child or person with disability, the term includes parents or lawful guardians.

questions.question: The maximum penalty under the DPDP Act, 2023 for failing to take reasonable security safeguards to prevent a personal data breach is up to:

options.A: ₹250 crore
options.B: ₹5 crore
options.C: ₹1,000 crore
options.D: ₹50 lakh

questions.answer_text: ₹250 crore
questions.explanation: Penalties are imposed by the Data Protection Board of India.

questions.question: Which body adjudicates personal data breaches and imposes penalties under the DPDP Act, 2023?

options.A: Indian Computer Emergency Response Team
options.B: Data Protection Board of India
options.C: Reserve Bank of India
options.D: National Critical Information Infrastructure Protection Centre

questions.answer_text: Data Protection Board of India
questions.explanation: Appeals against the Board's orders go to the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal (TDSAT).

questions.question: 'Humans are the weakest link in cybersecurity' mainly because:

options.A: Employees always choose strong passwords, which attackers cannot guess
options.B: Attackers use social engineering to trick people into revealing information or bypassing controls
options.C: Technical controls never fail, so humans are the only remaining source of risk
options.D: Humans make more errors than computers when doing complex mathematical calculations in banking systems

questions.answer_text: Attackers use social engineering to trick people into revealing information or bypassing controls
questions.explanation: Phishing, pretexting and vishing exploit trust and lack of awareness.

questions.question: A 'clean desk policy' requires employees to:

options.A: Remove all personal items from their desks at work
options.B: Clean and sanitise their desks and keyboards at the end of every hour of work
options.C: Not leave sensitive documents, media or unlocked screens unattended
options.D: Use only paper records instead of computer screens

questions.answer_text: Not leave sensitive documents, media or unlocked screens unattended
questions.explanation: It reduces the risk of information being read or stolen by others.

questions.question: Information classified as 'Confidential/Restricted' in a bank (e.g. customer KYC data) should be:

options.A: Accessed on a need-to-know basis and protected by encryption and access controls
options.B: Stored in plain text without logging so that access remains fast
options.C: Shared freely within the bank because all staff have signed confidentiality clauses
options.D: Published on the intranet so that any branch can verify customer identity

questions.answer_text: Accessed on a need-to-know basis and protected by encryption and access controls
questions.explanation: Classification decides handling rules: who can access, how it is stored, transmitted and destroyed.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: Which statement correctly differentiates BCP and DRP?

options.A: DRP keeps people, processes and facilities running during a crisis; BCP restores only IT systems and data
options.B: BCP covers only natural disasters; DRP covers only cyber attacks
options.C: Both are the same document, prepared once by the IT department
options.D: BCP keeps critical business functions running; DRP restores IT systems and data after a disaster

questions.answer_text: BCP keeps critical business functions running; DRP restores IT systems and data after a disaster
questions.explanation: DRP is a subset of the broader Business Continuity Plan.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: A flood damages the primary data centre. Activating the DR site and restoring CBS services is governed mainly by the:

options.A: Password Policy
options.B: Change Management Policy
options.C: Patch Management Policy
options.D: Disaster Recovery Plan

questions.answer_text: Disaster Recovery Plan
questions.explanation: The DRP gives the technical steps, roles and sequence to recover IT services.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: An organisation needs a robust BCP mainly to:

options.A: Reduce the number of branches by shifting customers to digital channels
options.B: Continue critical services during and after a disruption, protecting customers, revenue and reputation
options.C: Avoid paying for insurance cover by relying entirely on the bank's own internal staff and recovery arrangements
options.D: Replace the need for IT security controls such as firewalls and antivirus

questions.answer_text: Continue critical services during and after a disruption, protecting customers, revenue and reputation
questions.explanation: For banks, BCP is also a regulatory expectation.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: Arrange the BCP development steps in the correct order: (1) Business Impact Analysis (2) Plan development (3) Recovery strategy selection (4) Testing and training (5) Project initiation with management approval
questions.explanation: Initiation -> BIA -> strategy -> plan -> test/train -> maintain.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: The main purpose of a Business Impact Analysis (BIA) is to:

options.A: Prepare the incident report after a disaster has been resolved
options.B: Select and purchase backup hardware and DR site infrastructure
options.C: Identify critical processes and the impact of their disruption over time, to set RTO/RPO
options.D: Test the DR site by failing over all critical applications at least once in every financial year

questions.answer_text: Identify critical processes and the impact of their disruption over time, to set RTO/RPO
questions.explanation: BIA results drive recovery priorities and investment.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: The minimum level of services or products that is acceptable to the organisation during a disruption is called the:

options.A: Maximum Tolerable Downtime (MTD)
options.B: Recovery Point Objective (RPO)
options.C: Service Level Objective (SLO)
options.D: Minimum Business Continuity Objective (MBCO)

questions.answer_text: Minimum Business Continuity Objective (MBCO)
questions.explanation: MBCO defines what must be delivered in degraded mode until full recovery.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: The DR team's main role during a disaster is to:

options.A: Approve the annual budget for business continuity and DR investments
options.B: Communicate with the media and handle public relations for the bank
options.C: Execute the recovery procedures to restore systems and data at the DR site
options.D: Investigate which employees were responsible for causing the disaster

questions.answer_text: Execute the recovery procedures to restore systems and data at the DR site
questions.explanation: The team follows the DR runbook and coordinates with business and vendors.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: How often should a BCP be reviewed and updated?

options.A: Periodically (at least annually) and after major business or IT changes
options.B: Every ten years, along with the data centre technology refresh
options.C: Only after a real disaster has occurred and the lessons learned have been documented
options.D: Only once, when the plan is first created and approved

questions.answer_text: Periodically (at least annually) and after major business or IT changes
questions.explanation: An outdated plan with wrong contacts or systems fails when needed.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: A 'call tree' in a BCP is used to:

options.A: Notify staff and stakeholders quickly in a predefined sequence during a crisis
options.B: Draw the hierarchy of network devices from the core to the branches
options.C: Record and analyse customer complaints received at the call centre
options.D: Route customer phone calls automatically to the DR site's call centre during an outage

questions.answer_text: Notify staff and stakeholders quickly in a predefined sequence during a crisis
questions.explanation: Clear communication is a key part of crisis management.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: Recovery Time Objective (RTO) is:

options.A: The average time a system runs between two consecutive failures
options.B: The maximum acceptable time to restore a system or process after a disruption
options.C: The maximum acceptable amount of data loss, measured as time before the disruption
options.D: The time interval between two consecutive backups of a system

questions.answer_text: The maximum acceptable time to restore a system or process after a disruption
questions.explanation: RTO answers 'how fast must we be back up?'

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: Recovery Point Objective (RPO) is:

options.A: The time taken to detect that an incident has occurred
options.B: The time taken by the vendor to replace failed hardware
options.C: The maximum acceptable time to restore a system or process after a disruption
options.D: The maximum acceptable amount of data loss, measured as time before the disruption

questions.answer_text: The maximum acceptable amount of data loss, measured as time before the disruption
questions.explanation: RPO answers 'how much data can we afford to lose?'

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: An application has an RPO of 15 minutes. This means:

options.A: The DR site must be activated within 15 minutes of a disaster
options.B: Backups must be retained for at least 15 minutes after creation
options.C: Data must be backed up or replicated at least every 15 minutes
options.D: The system must be restored and running within 15 minutes

questions.answer_text: Data must be backed up or replicated at least every 15 minutes
questions.explanation: Restoring within 15 minutes would be an RTO, not RPO.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: Backups are taken daily at 11 PM. The server fails at 3 PM the next day. What is the worst-case data loss?

options.A: No data loss
options.B: About 16 hours of data
options.C: About 8 hours of data
options.D: About 24 hours of data

questions.answer_text: About 16 hours of data
questions.explanation: Everything entered after the last backup (11 PM to 3 PM) is lost, so achievable RPO here is 16 hours.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: An RPO close to zero is best achieved by:

options.A: Monthly archival to a cold site
options.B: Asynchronous replication every few hours
options.C: Weekly full backups shipped to an offsite vault
options.D: Synchronous data replication to the DR site

questions.answer_text: Synchronous data replication to the DR site
questions.explanation: Synchronous replication commits each write at both sites before acknowledging.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: Maximum Tolerable Downtime (MTD) and RTO are related as:

options.A: RTO must be less than or equal to MTD
options.B: They are unrelated
options.C: RTO must always be greater than MTD
options.D: They are always equal

questions.answer_text: RTO must be less than or equal to MTD
questions.explanation: MTD = RTO + Work Recovery Time (WRT). Exceeding MTD causes unacceptable damage.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: After systems are restored at the DR site, staff spend time validating data and catching up on transactions before business resumes. This period is called:

options.A: Lead time
options.B: Recovery Point Objective (RPO)
options.C: Work Recovery Time (WRT)
options.D: Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF)

questions.answer_text: Work Recovery Time (WRT)
questions.explanation: MTD = RTO + WRT.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: An organisation needs an RTO of 20 minutes for its critical application. Which type of DR site is appropriate?

options.A: Cold site
options.B: Reciprocal arrangement with another bank
options.C: Hot site
options.D: Warm site

questions.answer_text: Hot site
questions.explanation: Only a hot site with ready systems and current data can meet such a short RTO.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes a cold site?

options.A: It runs the live workload together with the primary site at all times
options.B: It is fully equipped and holds real-time data, so failover can happen within minutes
options.C: It has partial hardware installed and network links ready, needing only data restoration before use
options.D: It has space, power and cooling but no ready equipment or data, so recovery takes days or weeks

questions.answer_text: It has space, power and cooling but no ready equipment or data, so recovery takes days or weeks
questions.explanation: Cold sites are cheapest but slowest.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: A warm site typically has:

options.A: Only paper records and manual procedures for business continuity
options.B: Only empty space, power and cooling with no hardware installed at all
options.C: Real-time mirrored data and instant automatic failover of all critical systems and applications
options.D: Partial hardware and connectivity, needing data restore and configuration before use

questions.answer_text: Partial hardware and connectivity, needing data restore and configuration before use
questions.explanation: Recovery from a warm site typically takes hours to a day or two.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: Arrange DR sites from FASTEST to SLOWEST recovery:

options.A: Warm site, Hot site, Cold site
options.B: Cold site, Warm site, Hot site
options.C: Hot site, Warm site, Cold site
options.D: Hot site, Cold site, Warm site

questions.answer_text: Hot site, Warm site, Cold site
questions.explanation: Cost follows the same order: hot is the most expensive.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: Two organisations agree to use each other's facilities in case of a disaster. This is a:

options.A: Mirror site
options.B: Hot site contract
options.C: Reciprocal agreement
options.D: Cloud bursting arrangement

questions.answer_text: Reciprocal agreement
questions.explanation: Cheap but risky: the partner may lack spare capacity or compatible systems.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: In an Active-Active DR architecture:

options.A: Only the primary site runs, while the DR site stays powered off until needed
options.B: Both sites serve live traffic at the same time and each can take over the full load
options.C: Data is restored from tape at the DR site whenever the primary fails
options.D: The DR site is used only for testing and training, not for production

questions.answer_text: Both sites serve live traffic at the same time and each can take over the full load
questions.explanation: Benefits: near-zero RTO and load sharing; challenge: keeping data consistent across sites.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: In an Active-Passive setup:

options.A: Users choose which site to connect to based on their location
options.B: The standby site stays ready but does not serve users until failover
options.C: Both sites process customer transactions simultaneously at all times
options.D: There is no standby site at all; only backups are kept offsite

questions.answer_text: The standby site stays ready but does not serve users until failover
questions.explanation: Simpler to manage, but standby resources sit idle and failover takes some time.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: The main limitation of synchronous replication is that:

options.A: It cannot be used for databases, only for file servers
options.B: Write latency increases with distance, so sites must be relatively close
options.C: It always loses a few minutes of the most recent data whenever a failover takes place
options.D: It works only with tape libraries and not with disk storage

questions.answer_text: Write latency increases with distance, so sites must be relatively close
questions.explanation: The application waits for the remote write; hence sync is used for near-DR sites.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: Asynchronous replication is preferred for a far-away DR site because:

options.A: It does not wait for the remote site to confirm each write, so distance does not slow the application
options.B: It does not need any network link because data is shipped on physical media
options.C: It replicates data only once a month, which saves network bandwidth
options.D: It guarantees zero data loss even when the DR site is thousands of kilometres away from the primary data centre

questions.answer_text: It does not wait for the remote site to confirm each write, so distance does not slow the application
questions.explanation: Trade-off: a small amount of recent data may be lost (non-zero RPO).

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: Many banks use a three-site setup: Primary DC, Near DR (synchronous) and far DR (asynchronous). The main benefit is:

options.A: It allows the bank to use cheaper, lower-capacity servers at all sites
options.B: Zero data loss for local failures plus protection from regional disasters
options.C: It eliminates the need for DR drills because failover is automatic
options.D: It removes the need for taking any backups of the databases

questions.answer_text: Zero data loss for local failures plus protection from regional disasters
questions.explanation: Near DR gives RPO ~0 and can feed the far DR, which sits in a different seismic/flood zone.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: Switching operations from the primary site to the DR site is called ____, and returning to the primary site after it is fixed is called ____.

options.A: Rollback, roll-forward
options.B: Backup, restore
options.C: Failover, failback
options.D: Failback, failover

questions.answer_text: Failover, failback
questions.explanation: Failback must also be planned and tested to avoid data loss.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: In a two-node cluster, both nodes lose the heartbeat link and each assumes it is the primary, writing to shared data. This is called:

options.A: Thrashing
options.B: Deadlock
options.C: Failback
options.D: Split-brain

questions.answer_text: Split-brain
questions.explanation: Quorum disks/witness nodes and fencing prevent split-brain and data corruption.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: A 'heartbeat' in a high-availability cluster is used to:

options.A: Let nodes detect whether the other node is alive
options.B: Measure the CPU temperature of each cluster node
options.C: Encrypt the data exchanged between cluster nodes
options.D: Back up configuration files between cluster nodes

questions.answer_text: Let nodes detect whether the other node is alive
questions.explanation: Missing heartbeats trigger failover of resources to the surviving node.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: Why are periodic backups still needed even when data is replicated to a DR site in real time?

options.A: Replication never works reliably between data centres in different cities
options.B: Backups are always faster than replication and need less storage
options.C: Replication also copies corruption, accidental deletion and ransomware encryption instantly
options.D: Replication of core banking data to another site is not permitted by RBI under any circumstances

questions.answer_text: Replication also copies corruption, accidental deletion and ransomware encryption instantly
questions.explanation: Backups provide older, clean restore points; replication provides availability.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: Oracle Data Guard protects a database by:

options.A: Shipping redo data to one or more standby databases that can take over on failure
options.B: Encrypting backup tapes before they are sent to the offsite vault
options.C: Indexing all columns so that queries run faster after a failover
options.D: Compressing tables and indexes so as to reduce the storage used on the primary database

questions.answer_text: Shipping redo data to one or more standby databases that can take over on failure
questions.explanation: A physical standby applies redo continuously; it can be switched over or failed over.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: Which Oracle Data Guard protection mode guarantees zero data loss by shutting down the primary if it cannot write redo to at least one synchronous standby?

options.A: Maximum Protection
options.B: Snapshot Standby
options.C: Maximum Performance
options.D: Maximum Availability

questions.answer_text: Maximum Protection
questions.explanation: Maximum Availability falls back to async if the standby is unavailable; Maximum Performance (default) is asynchronous.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: After a DR switchover, customers must reach the DR site using the same website name. This is commonly achieved using:

options.A: Disabling SSL so that the certificate name does not matter
options.B: DNS-based failover / Global Server Load Balancing (GSLB)
options.C: Updating ARP tables on customers' home routers
options.D: Asking customers to change their browser settings

questions.answer_text: DNS-based failover / Global Server Load Balancing (GSLB)
questions.explanation: GSLB health-checks sites and points the domain to the active site.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: The main purpose of conducting DR drills is to:

options.A: Demonstrate newly purchased DR hardware to auditors and regulators during their annual inspections
options.B: Replace the BCP document, since a successful drill proves the plan
options.C: Validate that systems can actually be recovered within RTO/RPO and staff know their roles
options.D: Reduce the electricity bill by shifting load to the DR site permanently

questions.answer_text: Validate that systems can actually be recovered within RTO/RPO and staff know their roles
questions.explanation: Untested plans often fail due to missing steps, outdated scripts or dependencies.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: A BCP test where team members discuss a disaster scenario around a table and walk through their roles, without touching live systems, is a:

options.A: Full interruption test
options.B: Simulation with failover
options.C: Tabletop exercise
options.D: Parallel test

questions.answer_text: Tabletop exercise
questions.explanation: Tabletop tests are cheap and safe, good for training and finding plan gaps.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: Which type of DR test carries the HIGHEST risk to business operations?

options.A: Checklist review
options.B: Full interruption test
options.C: Parallel test
options.D: Tabletop exercise

questions.answer_text: Full interruption test
questions.explanation: Production is actually shut down and operations move fully to DR.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: In a parallel test:

options.A: Production is shut down completely and all business operations are moved to the DR site for the test
options.B: Team members only review the plan documents and checklists at their desks
options.C: DR systems are brought up and process data alongside production, without stopping the primary
options.D: Only the call tree is tested by contacting each staff member in sequence

questions.answer_text: DR systems are brought up and process data alongside production, without stopping the primary
questions.explanation: Results from DR are compared with production to verify correctness.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: During a DR drill, the CBS came up at DR in 3 hours against an RTO of 2 hours. The correct next step is:

options.A: Record the gap, perform root cause analysis and fix it, then re-test
options.B: Ignore the delay since the system did come up successfully
options.C: Change the RTO to 3 hours in the BCP without further discussion
options.D: Stop conducting DR drills since they disrupt normal operations

questions.answer_text: Record the gap, perform root cause analysis and fix it, then re-test
questions.explanation: Drill findings must be tracked to closure and reported to management.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: An availability SLA of 99.99% allows approximately how much downtime per year?

options.A: About 52.6 minutes
options.B: About 3.65 days
options.C: About 8.76 hours
options.D: About 5.26 minutes

questions.answer_text: About 52.6 minutes
questions.explanation: 99.9% = 8.76 hours, 99.99% = 52.6 minutes, 99.999% = 5.26 minutes per year.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: 'Five nines' (99.999%) availability allows approximately how much downtime per year?

options.A: About 8.76 hours
options.B: About 5.26 minutes
options.C: About 1 hour
options.D: About 52.6 minutes

questions.answer_text: About 5.26 minutes
questions.explanation: Each extra nine cuts allowed downtime by a factor of ten.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: A system has MTBF of 990 hours and MTTR of 10 hours. Its availability is:
questions.explanation: Availability = MTBF / (MTBF + MTTR) = 990 / 1000 = 99%.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: MTTR stands for:

options.A: Minimum Time To Replicate
options.B: Mean Transaction Time Rate
options.C: Mean Time To Repair / Recover
options.D: Maximum Time To Restart

questions.answer_text: Mean Time To Repair / Recover
questions.explanation: Lower MTTR = faster recovery = higher availability.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: A single point of failure (SPOF) is best eliminated by:

options.A: Adding redundancy such as dual power supplies, clustered servers and multiple network links
options.B: Reducing the frequency of backups so that systems are less loaded
options.C: Increasing log retention so that the cause of each failure can be investigated thoroughly afterwards
options.D: Adding more users and branches so that the load is spread across the system

questions.answer_text: Adding redundancy such as dual power supplies, clustered servers and multiple network links
questions.explanation: If one component's failure stops the whole service, it is a SPOF.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: 'N+1' redundancy means:

options.A: Two complete, fully duplicated systems are always kept running side by side at all times
options.B: Exactly one component is needed to run the entire load
options.C: One component is removed for maintenance every month
options.D: One extra component is available beyond the number needed to run the load

questions.answer_text: One extra component is available beyond the number needed to run the load
questions.explanation: 2N means a fully duplicated set; N+1 tolerates one component failure.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: As per the Uptime Institute classification, a data centre that is 'concurrently maintainable' (any component can be serviced without shutting down IT load) is:

options.A: Tier II
options.B: Tier III
options.C: Tier I
options.D: Tier IV

questions.answer_text: Tier III
questions.explanation: Tier IV is fault tolerant (survives any single failure); Tier III is concurrently maintainable.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: Which Uptime Institute tier is described as 'fault tolerant' with the highest expected availability (about 99.995%)?

options.A: Tier II
options.B: Tier III
options.C: Tier I
options.D: Tier IV

questions.answer_text: Tier IV
questions.explanation: Higher tiers are needed for critical banking workloads that require continuous availability.

questions.topic: DR / BCP Framework in Banking Systems
questions.question: A DR site is generally located in a different seismic and flood zone from the primary data centre mainly to:

options.A: Reduce network latency between the two data centres for synchronous replication
options.B: Get cheaper electricity and land for the DR site
options.C: Make inspections easier for auditors and regulators
options.D: Avoid both sites being affected by the same regional disaster

questions.answer_text: Avoid both sites being affected by the same regional disaster
questions.explanation: Geographic separation is a key DR design principle.

questions.question: In cryptography, converting readable plaintext into unreadable ciphertext using an algorithm and a key is called:

options.A: Hashing
options.B: Compression
options.C: Encoding
options.D: Encryption

questions.answer_text: Encryption
questions.explanation: Decryption reverses it using the correct key. Encoding (e.g. Base64) is not security.

questions.question: Kerckhoffs's principle states that a cryptosystem should remain secure even if:

options.A: The ciphertext is intercepted and deleted
options.B: The algorithm and the key are both kept secret from everyone
options.C: The secret key becomes known to the attacker
options.D: Everything about the system except the key is public

questions.answer_text: Everything about the system except the key is public
questions.explanation: Security must depend on the secrecy of the key, not on hiding the algorithm.

questions.question: The effort (time and resources) required to break an encryption is called the:

options.A: Cipher suite
options.B: Work factor
options.C: Key space
options.D: Entropy pool

questions.answer_text: Work factor
questions.explanation: Longer keys and stronger algorithms increase the work factor.

questions.question: Increasing a symmetric key length by just one bit has what effect on a brute-force attack?

options.A: It has no effect on the brute-force effort
options.B: It halves the number of possible keys to try
options.C: It doubles the number of possible keys to try
options.D: It adds exactly one more key to the search

questions.answer_text: It doubles the number of possible keys to try
questions.explanation: Key space = 2^n, so each extra bit doubles it.

questions.question: Hiding a secret message inside an image or audio file is called:

options.A: Cryptanalysis
options.B: Steganography
options.C: Tokenization
options.D: Hashing

questions.answer_text: Steganography
questions.explanation: Steganography hides the existence of the message; cryptography hides its meaning.

questions.question: Which statement about block and stream ciphers is correct?

options.A: Stream ciphers always need 128-bit blocks
options.B: Both AES and RC4 are hash functions
options.C: AES is a stream cipher; RC4 is a block cipher
options.D: AES is a block cipher; RC4 is a stream cipher

questions.answer_text: AES is a block cipher; RC4 is a stream cipher
questions.explanation: Block ciphers encrypt fixed-size blocks; stream ciphers encrypt bit/byte by bit/byte.

questions.question: In symmetric encryption:

options.A: The same secret key is used for encryption and decryption
options.B: A public key encrypts the data and a matching private key decrypts it
options.C: Only hashing is performed
options.D: No key is used

questions.answer_text: The same secret key is used for encryption and decryption
questions.explanation: Symmetric encryption is fast and suited for bulk data.

questions.question: Which of the following is a symmetric encryption algorithm?

options.A: AES
options.B: ECC
options.C: DSA
options.D: Diffie-Hellman

questions.answer_text: AES
questions.explanation: RSA, ECC, DH and DSA are asymmetric (public-key) techniques.

questions.question: Which of the following is an asymmetric encryption algorithm?

options.A: DES
options.B: AES
options.C: 3DES
options.D: RSA

questions.answer_text: RSA
questions.explanation: RSA uses a public/private key pair.

questions.question: The main practical problem with symmetric encryption is:

options.A: It can encrypt only text, not binary files or images
options.B: It always needs digital certificates from a trusted CA
options.C: Securely sharing and managing the secret key between parties
options.D: It is much slower than asymmetric encryption for large data

questions.answer_text: Securely sharing and managing the secret key between parties
questions.explanation: Asymmetric cryptography (or key exchange like DH) solves key distribution.

questions.question: For 10 users to communicate privately in pairs, how many keys are needed with symmetric and with asymmetric cryptography respectively?

options.A: 90 and 10
options.B: 20 and 45
options.C: 45 and 20
options.D: 10 and 10

questions.answer_text: 45 and 20
questions.explanation: Symmetric: n(n-1)/2 = 45 unique keys. Asymmetric: 2 keys per user = 20.

questions.question: What are the key sizes supported by AES (Rijndael)?

options.A: 128, 192 and 256 bits
options.C: 64, 128 and 512 bits
options.D: 56, 112 and 168 bits

questions.answer_text: 128, 192 and 256 bits
questions.explanation: AES always uses a 128-bit block size. 56 bits = DES.

questions.question: AES was selected by NIST in 2001. The original name of the algorithm chosen was:

options.A: Blowfish
options.B: Serpent
options.C: Twofish
options.D: Rijndael

questions.answer_text: Rijndael
questions.explanation: Serpent and Twofish were other finalists.

questions.question: DES is no longer considered secure mainly because:

options.A: It is a one-way hash, so data cannot be decrypted
options.B: It uses a public key that anyone can obtain
options.C: Its effective 56-bit key can be brute-forced quickly
options.D: Its 256-bit key makes it too slow for modern use

questions.answer_text: Its effective 56-bit key can be brute-forced quickly
questions.explanation: 3DES extended its life; AES replaced it.

questions.question: The security of RSA is based on the difficulty of:

options.A: Solving large systems of linear equations
options.B: Factoring the product of two large prime numbers
options.C: Finding two inputs that produce the same hash
options.D: Reversing a one-way hash function like SHA-256

questions.answer_text: Factoring the product of two large prime numbers
questions.explanation: Shor's algorithm on a large quantum computer could factor efficiently, which is why post-quantum cryptography is being adopted.

questions.question: The main advantage of Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) over RSA is:

options.A: It is fully resistant to attacks from future quantum computers
options.B: Similar security with much smaller keys, saving computation and bandwidth
options.C: It is a symmetric algorithm, so the same key is used at both ends of the link
options.D: It needs no private key, so key management becomes much simpler

questions.answer_text: Similar security with much smaller keys, saving computation and bandwidth
questions.explanation: A 256-bit ECC key gives security roughly comparable to a 3072-bit RSA key; good for mobile and smart cards.

questions.question: Diffie-Hellman is primarily used for:

options.A: Securely agreeing on a shared secret key over an insecure channel
options.B: Signing documents so that the sender cannot deny sending them
options.C: Encrypting bulk data directly between the client and the server
options.D: Creating a fixed-length hash value to verify message integrity

questions.answer_text: Securely agreeing on a shared secret key over an insecure channel
questions.explanation: Ephemeral DH (DHE/ECDHE) is used in TLS to provide forward secrecy.

questions.question: Protocols like TLS use 'hybrid encryption'. This means:

options.A: Asymmetric cryptography establishes a symmetric session key, which then encrypts the bulk data
options.B: Only asymmetric encryption is used for all data, so no session key is needed
options.C: Only hashing is used, so the data can be verified but never decrypted by anyone
options.D: Data is first encrypted with a symmetric key and then encrypted again with the same key

questions.answer_text: Asymmetric cryptography establishes a symmetric session key, which then encrypts the bulk data
questions.explanation: This combines the key-management benefit of asymmetric with the speed of symmetric encryption.

questions.question: Mathew wants to send a confidential file to Priya so that only Priya can read it. Mathew should encrypt it with:

options.A: Mathew's public key
options.B: Priya's private key
options.C: Mathew's private key
options.D: Priya's public key

questions.answer_text: Priya's public key
questions.explanation: Only Priya's private key can decrypt data encrypted with her public key.

questions.question: To digitally sign a document, the sender encrypts the document's hash using:

options.A: A shared symmetric key
options.B: The sender's own private key
options.C: The receiver's private key
options.D: The receiver's public key

questions.answer_text: The sender's own private key
questions.explanation: Anyone can verify using the sender's public key, proving origin and integrity.

questions.question: In a digital signature process, where is the message digest (hash) computed?

options.A: Only at the sender
options.B: At both the sender and the receiver
options.C: Only at the Certifying Authority
options.D: Only at the receiver

questions.answer_text: At both the sender and the receiver
questions.explanation: The receiver recomputes the hash and compares it with the hash obtained from the signature.

questions.question: A digital signature provides all of the following EXCEPT:

options.A: Authentication of the sender
options.B: Non-repudiation
options.C: Integrity of the message
options.D: Confidentiality

questions.answer_text: Confidentiality
questions.explanation: The message itself is not encrypted by signing; encryption is needed for confidentiality.

questions.question: The key difference between hashing and encryption is:

options.A: Both hashing and encryption can be reversed with the right key
options.B: Hashing is one-way; encryption can be reversed with the correct key
options.C: Encryption always gives a fixed-length output; hashing does not
options.D: Hashing needs a secret key; encryption does not need any key

questions.answer_text: Hashing is one-way; encryption can be reversed with the correct key
questions.explanation: Hashes verify integrity and store passwords; encryption protects confidentiality.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a required property of a cryptographic hash function?

options.A: It can be reversed to get the original input
options.B: It is hard to find two inputs with the same hash
options.C: It produces a fixed-length output
options.D: Small input changes give very different outputs

questions.answer_text: It can be reversed to get the original input
questions.explanation: Hashes must be one-way (pre-image resistant) and collision resistant.

questions.question: SHA-256 produces a hash output of:

options.A: 256 bits
options.B: 512 bits
options.C: 128 bits
options.D: 160 bits

questions.answer_text: 256 bits
questions.explanation: MD5 = 128 bits, SHA-1 = 160 bits, SHA-512 = 512 bits.

questions.question: MD5 and SHA-1 should not be used for digital signatures today because:

options.A: They are far too slow for signing large documents on modern servers
options.B: They produce outputs of variable length
options.C: Practical collision attacks have been demonstrated against them
options.D: They require a public key to compute the hash

questions.answer_text: Practical collision attacks have been demonstrated against them
questions.explanation: Use SHA-256 or stronger (SHA-2/SHA-3 family).

questions.question: A 'salt' is added to passwords before hashing in order to:

options.A: Allow the original password to be recovered later from the stored hash
options.B: Make identical passwords produce different hashes and defeat rainbow-table attacks
options.C: Shorten long passwords so that they fit into a fixed-length database column
options.D: Encrypt the password so that administrators can decrypt it when users forget it

questions.answer_text: Make identical passwords produce different hashes and defeat rainbow-table attacks
questions.explanation: Each user gets a unique random salt stored with the hash.

questions.question: Which is the BEST way to store user passwords in a database?

options.A: Encrypted with AES-256 using a strong key that is stored in the same table
options.B: Plain text in a hidden column that only DBAs can access
options.C: Fast MD5 hash without salt so that logins are quicker
options.D: Salted hash using a slow algorithm like bcrypt, scrypt, Argon2 or PBKDF2

questions.answer_text: Salted hash using a slow algorithm like bcrypt, scrypt, Argon2 or PBKDF2
questions.explanation: Slow, salted hashes make offline cracking expensive.

questions.question: HMAC (Hash-based Message Authentication Code) provides:

options.A: Non-repudiation, by signing the message hash with the sender's own private key
options.B: Compression of the message before it is sent over the network
options.C: Integrity and authenticity using a hash combined with a shared secret key
options.D: Confidentiality by encrypting the message with a shared secret key

questions.answer_text: Integrity and authenticity using a hash combined with a shared secret key
questions.explanation: Because the key is shared, HMAC cannot provide non-repudiation (unlike digital signatures).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of a Public Key Infrastructure (PKI)?

options.A: Certificate Authority (CA)
options.B: Load balancer
options.C: Registration Authority (RA)
options.D: Certificate Revocation List (CRL)

questions.answer_text: Load balancer
questions.explanation: PKI also includes certificate repositories, OCSP responders and policies.

questions.question: The main role of a Certifying Authority (CA) is to:

options.A: Verify identity and issue digitally signed certificates binding a public key to that identity
options.B: Generate and safely store the private keys of all certificate holders in its own data centre
options.C: Assign IP addresses and domain names to websites that use HTTPS
options.D: Encrypt all internet traffic flowing between browsers and web servers

questions.answer_text: Verify identity and issue digitally signed certificates binding a public key to that identity
questions.explanation: Browsers trust certificates that chain to a trusted root CA.

questions.question: In PKI, the Registration Authority (RA):

options.A: Generates and stores private keys for all certificate holders
options.B: Signs every issued certificate using the root CA's private key
options.C: Publishes the list of trusted root CAs used by browsers
options.D: Verifies the identity of certificate applicants on behalf of the CA

questions.answer_text: Verifies the identity of certificate applicants on behalf of the CA
questions.explanation: The CA issues the certificate after the RA validates the request.

questions.question: In India, Certifying Authorities that issue Digital Signature Certificates are licensed and regulated by:

options.A: Controller of Certifying Authorities (CCA)
options.B: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
options.C: Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In)
options.D: Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS)

questions.answer_text: Controller of Certifying Authorities (CCA)
questions.explanation: CCA was set up under the IT Act, 2000 and operates the Root Certifying Authority of India.

questions.question: Digital certificates used in SSL/TLS and PKI follow which standard format?

options.B: ISO 9001
options.D: IEEE 802.1X

questions.explanation: X.509 defines fields like subject, issuer, validity, public key and signature.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT contained in a digital certificate?

options.A: The issuer (CA) name and its signature
options.B: The owner's private key
options.C: Validity period and serial number
options.D: The owner's public key

questions.answer_text: The owner's private key
questions.explanation: The private key never leaves its owner; certificates are public documents.

questions.question: Before trusting a certificate, a browser checks whether it has been revoked. Which mechanism gives a real-time status for one certificate?

options.A: OCSP (Online Certificate Status Protocol)
options.B: CSR (Certificate Signing Request) validation
options.C: CRL (Certificate Revocation List) checked yearly
options.D: DNSSEC (DNS Security Extensions) lookup

questions.answer_text: OCSP (Online Certificate Status Protocol)
questions.explanation: A CRL is a periodically published list of revoked certificates; OCSP queries status on demand.

questions.question: PKI is a cryptographic framework that uses:

options.A: Only symmetric encryption with shared keys
options.B: Only hashing without any encryption
options.C: Only asymmetric encryption for all data
options.D: Both asymmetric and symmetric encryption

questions.answer_text: Both asymmetric and symmetric encryption
questions.explanation: Certificates and signatures use asymmetric keys; actual sessions use symmetric keys established through them.

questions.question: An SSL/TLS certificate makes a banking website trustworthy because:

options.A: The browser verifies that a trusted CA has confirmed the domain owner and an encrypted channel is set up
options.B: The certificate makes the website load faster by compressing all pages before sending them to the user's browser
options.C: The certificate hides the website's real IP address from attackers on the internet
options.D: The certificate scans the website for malware and blocks infected pages automatically

questions.answer_text: The browser verifies that a trusted CA has confirmed the domain owner and an encrypted channel is set up
questions.explanation: It authenticates the server and encrypts traffic, protecting against eavesdropping and spoofed sites.

questions.question: The private key of a Root CA is usually kept:

options.A: With each customer, so that they can verify certificates without internet access
options.B: In the browser's certificate store, so that sessions can be decrypted if required
options.C: Offline in a hardware security module, used only to sign intermediate CA certificates
options.D: On the CA's public web server so that browsers can download it when needed

questions.answer_text: Offline in a hardware security module, used only to sign intermediate CA certificates
questions.explanation: Compromise of a root key would break trust in every certificate under it.

questions.question: A Hardware Security Module (HSM) in a bank is used to:

options.A: Run the core banking application on dedicated tamper-proof hardware
options.B: Securely generate, store and use cryptographic keys, e.g. for PIN processing and signing
options.C: Accelerate internet bandwidth for branches by compressing and caching all outgoing network traffic
options.D: Store CCTV footage of the data centre in tamper-proof encrypted form

questions.answer_text: Securely generate, store and use cryptographic keys, e.g. for PIN processing and signing
questions.explanation: HSMs are tamper-resistant; keys never leave them in plain form.

questions.question: Arrange the cryptographic key lifecycle in a logical order: (1) Distribution (2) Generation (3) Destruction (4) Usage and rotation (5) Storage
questions.explanation: Generate -> distribute -> store securely -> use/rotate -> revoke/destroy (archive if needed).

questions.question: Periodic key rotation is done mainly to:

options.A: Limit the amount of data exposed if a key is compromised
options.B: Reduce the storage space needed for encrypted data
options.C: Avoid the need for digital certificates on servers
options.D: Speed up encryption, because newly generated keys are shorter

questions.answer_text: Limit the amount of data exposed if a key is compromised
questions.explanation: Shorter key lifetimes limit damage and the volume of ciphertext available to attackers.

questions.question: In 'envelope encryption' (used by cloud KMS):

options.A: Data is hashed instead of encrypted, and the hash is stored inside a digital envelope
options.B: The master key is stored in plain text next to the data so that decryption is fast
options.C: Data is encrypted with a data key, and the data key is encrypted with a master key held in KMS/HSM
options.D: Data is encrypted twice with the same key so that brute-force attacks become twice as hard to perform

questions.answer_text: Data is encrypted with a data key, and the data key is encrypted with a master key held in KMS/HSM
questions.explanation: Rotating the master key does not require re-encrypting all data.

questions.question: Oracle Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) protects:

options.A: Data at rest in data files and backups, without application changes
options.B: Data in transit between the customer's browser and the bank's web server
options.C: Network routing tables of the database server's host
options.D: User passwords held in the memory of the application server

questions.answer_text: Data at rest in data files and backups, without application changes
questions.explanation: Keys are kept in a wallet/keystore or HSM; data is decrypted automatically for authorised sessions.

questions.question: BitLocker (Windows) and LUKS (Linux) are examples of:

options.A: Host-based network firewalls
options.B: Enterprise password managers
options.C: TLS libraries for securing data in transit
options.D: Full disk encryption for data at rest

questions.answer_text: Full disk encryption for data at rest
questions.explanation: They protect data if a laptop or disk is lost or stolen.

questions.question: Oracle Native Network Encryption is used to:

options.A: Hash database user passwords using a salted algorithm before storing them
options.B: Encrypt Oracle data files and backups on disk using encryption keys stored in an Oracle wallet or a hardware security module
options.C: Encrypt and integrity-check traffic between Oracle client and database server via sqlnet.ora settings, without certificates
options.D: Mask sensitive columns in query results shown to non-privileged users

questions.answer_text: Encrypt and integrity-check traffic between Oracle client and database server via sqlnet.ora settings, without certificates
questions.explanation: It is an alternative to TLS for Oracle Net traffic; TLS needs certificates and wallets.

questions.question: Which of the following is an improvement of TLS 1.3 over TLS 1.2?

options.A: Faster handshake and removal of weak ciphers and static RSA key exchange
options.B: Encryption made optional to improve handshake performance
options.C: Use of MD5 and SHA-1 for faster signature verification
options.D: Added support for SSL 2.0 and SSL 3.0 so that older browsers can still connect

questions.answer_text: Faster handshake and removal of weak ciphers and static RSA key exchange
questions.explanation: TLS 1.3 makes forward secrecy mandatory and reduces handshake to one round trip.

questions.question: Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS) ensures that:

options.A: Passwords are never stored on the server because each session uses a different key
options.B: If the server's long-term private key is stolen later, past recorded sessions still cannot be decrypted
options.C: Certificates no longer need to be issued by a trusted CA because the session keys are exchanged directly
options.D: Session keys never expire, so an established connection can be resumed at any later time

questions.answer_text: If the server's long-term private key is stolen later, past recorded sessions still cannot be decrypted
questions.explanation: Each session uses ephemeral (EC)DHE keys that are discarded after use.

questions.question: Which protocol versions should be disabled on bank web servers because they are insecure?

options.A: Only TLS 1.3, as it is not yet stable
options.B: HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 protocols
options.C: SSL 3.0, TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1
options.D: TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 only

questions.answer_text: SSL 3.0, TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1
questions.explanation: Only TLS 1.2 (with strong cipher suites) and TLS 1.3 should be allowed.

questions.question: NIST's first post-quantum standard for key establishment (FIPS 203, August 2024), ML-KEM, is based on:

options.A: SHA-3
options.B: CRYSTALS-Kyber
options.D: AES-256

questions.answer_text: CRYSTALS-Kyber
questions.explanation: FIPS 204 (ML-DSA, from Dilithium) and FIPS 205 (SLH-DSA, from SPHINCS+) cover signatures.

questions.question: Tokenization in card payments means:

options.A: Printing a masked card number on receipts so that only the last four digits show
options.B: Encrypting the card number with the customer's PIN so only they can decrypt it
options.C: Replacing the actual card number with a unique surrogate token that is useless if stolen
options.D: Storing the card number and CVV with the merchant for faster future payments

questions.answer_text: Replacing the actual card number with a unique surrogate token that is useless if stolen
questions.explanation: RBI's card-on-file tokenization rules (from October 2022) stop merchants storing actual card data.

questions.question: How does tokenization differ from encryption?

options.A: A token has no mathematical relation to the original data and can only be mapped back through a secure token vault
options.B: Tokenization always increases data size, whereas encryption keeps the original size unchanged
options.C: Encryption cannot be reversed, whereas tokens can be reversed using a standard algorithm
options.D: A token can be converted back into the original data by anyone who holds the token issuer's published public key

questions.answer_text: A token has no mathematical relation to the original data and can only be mapped back through a secure token vault
questions.explanation: Stolen tokens cannot be 'decrypted' because there is no key to break.

questions.question: Displaying an account number as XXXXXXXX1234 on a statement is an example of:

options.A: Encryption
options.B: Hashing
options.C: Compression
options.D: Data masking

questions.answer_text: Data masking
questions.explanation: Masking hides part of the data from people who do not need to see it.

questions.question: Copying production data to a UAT environment with customer names and PANs permanently replaced by realistic fake values is called:

options.A: Tokenization by the card network
options.B: Static data masking
options.C: Transparent data encryption
options.D: Dynamic data masking

questions.answer_text: Static data masking
questions.explanation: Dynamic masking hides data on the fly at query time, leaving stored data unchanged.

questions.question: Format-Preserving Encryption (FPE) is useful because:

options.A: It compresses the data so that the encrypted columns take less storage space than the original plain-text values
options.B: It is a one-way hash, so the original values can never be recovered by anyone
options.C: It does not need any encryption key, so key management is not required at all
options.D: The ciphertext keeps the same format and length as the original (e.g. a 16-digit number stays 16 digits)

questions.answer_text: The ciphertext keeps the same format and length as the original (e.g. a 16-digit number stays 16 digits)
questions.explanation: Legacy systems and database columns can store encrypted values without schema changes.

questions.question: In the client-server computing model:

options.A: Only one computer is involved
options.B: Servers send requests to clients for processing
options.C: Clients send requests and servers process them and return responses
options.D: Every computer stores all its data locally and works without any network connection

questions.answer_text: Clients send requests and servers process them and return responses
questions.explanation: Internet banking: the browser/app is the client; bank web and application servers serve it.

questions.question: Cluster computing differs from grid computing in that a cluster:

options.A: Never shares workload
options.B: Runs only on mobile phones
options.C: Uses tightly coupled, usually identical nodes in one location acting as a single system
options.D: Uses loosely coupled heterogeneous computers spread across many different organisations

questions.answer_text: Uses tightly coupled, usually identical nodes in one location acting as a single system
questions.explanation: Grids pool geographically spread, heterogeneous resources for large tasks.

questions.question: In a loosely coupled (distributed) system:

options.A: Each processor has its own memory and they communicate over a network
options.B: Processes on different processors cannot communicate at all
options.C: All processors share a single common main memory and a common system clock
options.D: There is only one processor that handles all tasks in turn

questions.answer_text: Each processor has its own memory and they communicate over a network
questions.explanation: Tightly coupled systems (multiprocessors) share memory and a clock.

questions.question: 'Latency' and 'throughput' in system design mean respectively:

options.A: Delay caused by the network only; total data stored on the server
options.B: Time taken to serve one request; number of requests served per unit time
options.C: Number of requests served per unit time; time taken to serve one request
options.D: Total disk capacity of the server; network bandwidth of the server

questions.answer_text: Time taken to serve one request; number of requests served per unit time
questions.explanation: A system can have high throughput but still high latency for each request, so both are measured.

questions.question: Upgrading a server by adding more CPU and RAM is called ____, while adding more servers behind a load balancer is called ____.

options.A: Horizontal scaling (scale out); vertical scaling (scale up)
options.B: Replication (mirroring); partitioning (sharding)
options.C: Vertical scaling (scale up); horizontal scaling (scale out)
options.D: Virtualization (consolidation); clustering (high availability)

questions.answer_text: Vertical scaling (scale up); horizontal scaling (scale out)
questions.explanation: Horizontal scaling is preferred for cloud-native web workloads; vertical scaling has hardware limits.

questions.question: Blade servers are preferred in data centres mainly because they:

options.A: Share power, cooling and networking in a common chassis, giving high density and easier management
options.B: Are larger than tower servers, so they hold more disks and expansion cards for each server
options.C: Cannot be virtualized, so each blade runs a single application with dedicated resources
options.D: Need no separate power or cooling because they draw everything from the network cables

questions.answer_text: Share power, cooling and networking in a common chassis, giving high density and easier management
questions.explanation: Many blades fit in one enclosure, saving space and cabling.

questions.question: Rack-mounted servers are measured in rack units (U). One rack unit (1U) equals:

options.A: 3.5 inches
options.B: 1 inch
options.C: 1.75 inches (44.45 mm)
options.D: 19 inches

questions.answer_text: 1.75 inches (44.45 mm)
questions.explanation: 19 inches is the standard rack width; a typical full rack is 42U.

questions.question: Hyper-Threading (simultaneous multithreading) allows:

options.A: The CPU to run programs directly without using any cache memory
options.B: Part of the RAM to be used as a fast disk for swap space
options.C: Two physical CPUs to share a single memory module between them
options.D: A single physical core to appear as two logical processors to the OS

questions.answer_text: A single physical core to appear as two logical processors to the OS
questions.explanation: It improves utilisation of execution units, but is not equal to doubling physical cores.

questions.question: Which statement about RISC and CISC is correct?

options.A: Intel/AMD x86 is a pure RISC architecture, while ARM is a classic CISC architecture
options.B: RISC processors have fewer registers than CISC processors and rely more on memory access
options.C: RISC uses a small set of simple fixed-length instructions; CISC uses many complex variable-length instructions
options.D: CISC uses a small set of simple fixed-length instructions; RISC uses many complex variable-length instructions

questions.answer_text: RISC uses a small set of simple fixed-length instructions; CISC uses many complex variable-length instructions
questions.explanation: ARM, SPARC and IBM POWER are RISC; Intel/AMD x86 is CISC.

questions.question: Servers use ECC (Error-Correcting Code) memory because it:

options.A: Runs faster than all other types of RAM because it does not need any refresh cycles at all
options.B: Detects and corrects single-bit memory errors, avoiding silent data corruption and crashes
options.C: Uses much less electricity than normal RAM, reducing data-centre power costs
options.D: Encrypts data in memory so that it cannot be read by malicious processes

questions.answer_text: Detects and corrects single-bit memory errors, avoiding silent data corruption and crashes
questions.explanation: Silent memory errors in financial calculations are unacceptable, so ECC is standard in servers.

questions.question: Which memory sits between the CPU and main memory (RAM) to speed up access?

options.A: Virtual memory
options.B: ROM
options.C: Secondary storage
options.D: Cache memory

questions.answer_text: Cache memory
questions.explanation: L1/L2/L3 caches hold frequently used data close to the CPU.

questions.question: Arrange the following from FASTEST to SLOWEST access: (1) RAM (2) CPU registers (3) Hard disk (4) Cache (5) SSD
questions.explanation: Registers -> cache -> RAM -> SSD -> HDD. Cost per GB falls in the same order.

questions.question: In a NUMA (Non-Uniform Memory Access) server:

options.A: All memory is accessed by every CPU at exactly the same speed through a single shared memory bus
options.B: There is no main memory; each CPU uses only its own cache to store all data
options.C: Only one CPU can access memory at a time, so the others wait in a queue
options.D: Each CPU socket has local memory that it accesses faster than memory attached to other sockets

questions.answer_text: Each CPU socket has local memory that it accesses faster than memory attached to other sockets
questions.explanation: Hypervisors and databases try to keep a workload's CPU and memory on the same NUMA node.

questions.question: A Network Interface Card (NIC) in a server:

options.A: Stores the operating system and boot loader of the server
options.B: Connects the server to Fibre Channel SAN storage
options.C: Connects the server to the network and has a unique MAC address
options.D: Converts incoming AC power to the DC power used by components

questions.answer_text: Connects the server to the network and has a unique MAC address
questions.explanation: Servers often have multiple NICs for production, backup and management networks.

questions.question: NIC teaming (bonding) is used to:

options.A: Encrypt network traffic leaving the server's NICs
options.B: Assign two IP addresses to a single network cable
options.C: Connect a server to SAN storage over Fibre Channel using multiple fibre cables
options.D: Combine multiple network cards for redundancy and/or higher bandwidth

questions.answer_text: Combine multiple network cards for redundancy and/or higher bandwidth
questions.explanation: If one NIC or switch port fails, traffic continues on the other.

questions.question: A Host Bus Adapter (HBA) in a server is mainly used to:

options.A: Connect the server to Fibre Channel SAN storage
options.B: Add extra RAM slots to the motherboard
options.C: Connect the server to the Ethernet LAN
options.D: Provide remote out-of-band console and power access

questions.answer_text: Connect the server to Fibre Channel SAN storage
questions.explanation: Two HBAs connected to two fabrics with multipathing avoid a single point of failure.

questions.question: HPE iLO, Dell iDRAC and IPMI are examples of:

options.A: Out-of-band management controllers allowing remote console and power control even when the OS is down
options.B: Agent-based monitoring tools that report CPU, memory and disk usage only while the operating system is running
options.C: Hypervisors that run directly on the hardware and host multiple virtual machines
options.D: Hardware load balancers that distribute traffic across a pool of servers

questions.answer_text: Out-of-band management controllers allowing remote console and power control even when the OS is down
questions.explanation: They must be on a secured management network because they give full control of the server.

questions.question: Redundant, hot-swappable power supplies in a server allow:

options.A: The CPU to run at higher clock speeds by drawing more power
options.B: A failed power supply to be replaced without shutting down the server
options.C: The server to keep running for hours during a total power outage
options.D: The server to take automatic backups when power fluctuates

questions.answer_text: A failed power supply to be replaced without shutting down the server
questions.explanation: Hot-swap components (PSU, fans, disks) improve availability.

questions.question: A hypervisor (Virtual Machine Monitor) is software that:

options.A: Creates and runs virtual machines by sharing physical hardware among them
options.B: Manages user passwords and authentication for all servers
options.C: Monitors network traffic for viruses and blocks infected packets before they reach servers
options.D: Backs up databases and virtual machine images to tape

questions.answer_text: Creates and runs virtual machines by sharing physical hardware among them
questions.explanation: It allocates CPU, memory, storage and network to each VM and keeps them isolated.

questions.question: A Type 1 hypervisor:

options.A: Needs no hardware
options.B: Runs as an application on top of a host operating system
options.C: Is a type of container
options.D: Runs directly on the physical hardware (bare-metal)

questions.answer_text: Runs directly on the physical hardware (bare-metal)
questions.explanation: Examples: VMware ESXi, Microsoft Hyper-V, KVM, Xen. Used in data centres.

questions.question: Which of the following is a Type 2 (hosted) hypervisor?

options.A: KVM
options.B: Microsoft Hyper-V Server
options.C: Xen
options.D: Oracle VirtualBox

questions.answer_text: Oracle VirtualBox
questions.explanation: Type 2 runs on top of a desktop OS; VMware Workstation is another example.

questions.question: KVM (Kernel-based Virtual Machine) is considered a Type 1 hypervisor because:

options.A: It is a container engine that shares the host kernel instead of running full VMs
options.B: It runs as an application inside a desktop OS, like VirtualBox or VMware Workstation
options.C: It is built into the Linux kernel, turning Linux itself into a bare-metal hypervisor
options.D: It needs Windows Server to be installed first, with Hyper-V enabled underneath it

questions.answer_text: It is built into the Linux kernel, turning Linux itself into a bare-metal hypervisor
questions.explanation: KVM is the basis of many private and public cloud platforms.

questions.question: Hardware-assisted virtualization features in processors are known as:

options.A: SSE and AVX
options.B: Intel VT-x and AMD-V
options.C: Hyper-Threading and SMT
options.D: Intel Turbo Boost and AMD Precision Boost

questions.answer_text: Intel VT-x and AMD-V
questions.explanation: They let the CPU handle privileged guest instructions efficiently, improving VM performance.

questions.question: In full virtualization:

options.A: The guest OS runs unmodified because the hypervisor fully emulates/virtualizes the hardware
options.B: No hypervisor is used, because the guest runs directly on the physical hardware
options.C: The guest OS must be modified so that it makes hypercalls directly to the hypervisor
options.D: All guests run as containers that share the host operating system's kernel

questions.answer_text: The guest OS runs unmodified because the hypervisor fully emulates/virtualizes the hardware
questions.explanation: Uses binary translation or hardware assistance; any standard OS can run as a guest.

questions.question: In para-virtualization:

options.A: Applications run directly on the hypervisor without any guest operating system
options.B: The guest OS is modified to make hypercalls to the hypervisor, improving performance
options.C: The guest OS is unmodified and unaware that it is running inside a virtual machine
options.D: The hypervisor itself runs as an application inside the guest operating system

questions.answer_text: The guest OS is modified to make hypercalls to the hypervisor, improving performance
questions.explanation: Xen popularised para-virtualization; it reduces the overhead of trapping privileged instructions.

questions.question: OS-level virtualization (containers such as Docker and LXC):

options.A: Requires a Type 2 hypervisor
options.B: Runs isolated user spaces that share the host OS kernel
options.C: Gives each instance its own full guest kernel
options.D: Can run a Windows kernel inside a Linux container natively

questions.answer_text: Runs isolated user spaces that share the host OS kernel
questions.explanation: Containers are lightweight and start in seconds, but all must be compatible with the host kernel.

questions.question: The key difference between a container and a virtual machine is that:

options.A: Containers need much more memory than VMs because each includes a full OS
options.B: VMs start faster than containers because they do not need to boot an OS
options.C: Containers share the host OS kernel, while each VM has its own full guest OS
options.D: VMs share the host OS kernel, while each container has its own full guest OS

questions.answer_text: Containers share the host OS kernel, while each VM has its own full guest OS
questions.explanation: Containers are better for microservices; VMs give stronger isolation and OS flexibility.

questions.question: Match the virtualization type with its feature: (P) Full virtualization (Q) Para-virtualization (R) OS-level virtualization | (1) Shared host kernel (2) Unmodified guest OS (3) Modified guest OS using hypercalls
questions.explanation: Full = unmodified guest; Para = modified guest with hypercalls; OS-level = containers sharing the kernel.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of server virtualization?

options.A: Server consolidation and lower hardware cost
options.B: Reduced power, cooling and space
options.C: It removes the need to patch guest operating systems
options.D: Faster provisioning of new servers
options.E: Easier disaster recovery through VM replication to another site

questions.answer_text: It removes the need to patch guest operating systems
questions.explanation: Every VM's guest OS still needs patching and hardening.

questions.question: A bank runs 40 physical servers each at about 10% CPU utilisation. Moving them as VMs onto 5 powerful hosts is an example of:

options.A: Data replication
options.B: Horizontal scaling
options.C: Load shedding
options.D: Workload consolidation

questions.answer_text: Workload consolidation
questions.explanation: Consolidation raises utilisation and cuts power, space and maintenance costs.

questions.question: Resource pooling in virtualization means:

options.A: Storing all VM images in a single shared folder so that they can be copied quickly
options.B: Grouping VMs by department so that each department gets an equal share of hosts
options.C: Aggregating CPU, memory, storage and network of many hosts into a shared pool allocated dynamically to VMs
options.D: Giving each VM its own dedicated physical server so that CPU, memory and storage are never shared with other VMs

questions.answer_text: Aggregating CPU, memory, storage and network of many hosts into a shared pool allocated dynamically to VMs
questions.explanation: It is also one of NIST's essential characteristics of cloud computing.

questions.question: 'Abstraction' in virtualization refers to:

options.A: Hiding the details of the physical hardware from the VMs, which see standard virtual devices
options.B: Encrypting VM memory so that the hypervisor cannot read guest data
