options.C: Compressing VM disk files so that they take less storage space
options.D: Removing unused VMs automatically after a fixed period of inactivity to free up host resources

questions.answer_text: Hiding the details of the physical hardware from the VMs, which see standard virtual devices
questions.explanation: Abstraction lets VMs move between different physical hosts without reconfiguration.

questions.question: Green computing is supported by virtualization mainly because it:

options.A: Increases the number of servers, spreading heat more evenly in the data centre
options.B: Allows servers to run on solar power without any connection to the grid
options.C: Reduces the number of physical servers, lowering energy and cooling needs
options.D: Removes the need for air conditioning because VMs generate no heat

questions.answer_text: Reduces the number of physical servers, lowering energy and cooling needs
questions.explanation: Green computing aims at energy-efficient and environmentally responsible use of IT.

questions.question: Moving a running VM from one physical host to another without downtime is called:

options.A: Snapshot rollback to an earlier state
options.B: Cold migration after shutting the VM down
options.C: P2V (physical-to-virtual) conversion
options.D: Live migration (e.g. VMware vMotion)

questions.answer_text: Live migration (e.g. VMware vMotion)
questions.explanation: It enables hardware maintenance and load balancing without service interruption.

questions.question: Why should a VM snapshot NOT be treated as a backup?

options.A: Snapshots are copied to tape automatically, so they cannot be restored quickly
options.B: It depends on the base disk on the same storage and long-lived snapshots also degrade performance
options.C: Snapshots can never be restored once the VM has been powered off and restarted on a different host in the cluster
options.D: Snapshots are always encrypted with a key that is lost when the host reboots

questions.answer_text: It depends on the base disk on the same storage and long-lived snapshots also degrade performance
questions.explanation: If the underlying storage fails, both the VM and its snapshots are lost.

questions.question: Allocating more total vCPUs or memory to VMs than the host physically has, assuming they will not all peak together, is called:

options.A: Overcommitment
options.B: Thin provisioning of disks
options.C: Consolidation
options.D: Live migration

questions.answer_text: Overcommitment
questions.explanation: Moderate overcommit is efficient, but heavy overcommit causes contention and swapping.

questions.question: 'VM sprawl' refers to:

options.A: Spreading one large VM across many physical hosts to use their combined capacity
options.B: Expanding a VM's disk beyond its allocated size
options.C: A single VM that consumes too much CPU on its host
options.D: Uncontrolled growth of VMs that are unused, unpatched or unmanaged

questions.answer_text: Uncontrolled growth of VMs that are unused, unpatched or unmanaged
questions.explanation: Sprawl wastes resources and leaves forgotten, vulnerable systems in the network.

questions.question: A 'VM escape' attack is serious because the attacker:

options.A: Moves the VM to another data centre without the knowledge of the administrators
options.B: Gains administrator access only to the files inside that particular guest VM
options.C: Breaks out of a guest VM to access the hypervisor and potentially all other VMs on the host
options.D: Deletes the VM's snapshots so that it can no longer be rolled back after an incident

questions.answer_text: Breaks out of a guest VM to access the hypervisor and potentially all other VMs on the host
questions.explanation: Keeping hypervisors patched and minimising guest-to-host features reduces this risk.

questions.question: Converting an existing physical server into a virtual machine is called:

options.A: V2V (Virtual-to-Virtual) migration
options.B: Live migration between hosts
options.C: P2V (Physical-to-Virtual) migration
options.D: V2P (Virtual-to-Physical) migration

questions.answer_text: P2V (Physical-to-Virtual) migration
questions.explanation: Tools capture the disk and drivers of the physical server and create an equivalent VM.

questions.question: Which is a key RISK when migrating many physical servers onto a few virtualization hosts?

options.A: Failure of one host can affect many critical VMs at once unless HA is configured
options.B: Software licensing terms never change when moving to virtual servers
options.C: Virtual servers cannot be backed up with standard enterprise backup tools
options.D: Virtual servers cannot be connected to VLANs or production networks

questions.answer_text: Failure of one host can affect many critical VMs at once unless HA is configured
questions.explanation: Other risks: resource contention, legacy app compatibility, licensing and new skills.

questions.question: In VMware, which feature keeps a live shadow copy of a VM running in lockstep on another host so that a host failure causes no downtime at all?

options.A: High Availability (HA)
options.B: Fault Tolerance (FT)
options.C: Distributed Resource Scheduler (DRS)
options.D: Storage vMotion

questions.answer_text: Fault Tolerance (FT)
questions.explanation: HA restarts VMs on another host after a failure (short downtime); FT gives continuous availability.

questions.question: Virtual Desktop Infrastructure (VDI) means:

options.A: Desktops are installed on USB drives that users carry between branches
options.B: Every user gets a powerful physical PC with a hypervisor installed locally to run several desktops
options.C: Users access servers directly through the console in the data centre
options.D: User desktops run as VMs in the data centre and are accessed from thin clients or PCs

questions.answer_text: User desktops run as VMs in the data centre and are accessed from thin clients or PCs
questions.explanation: VDI centralises data and control, useful for branches and secure remote work.

questions.question: A virtual switch (vSwitch) in a hypervisor is used to:

options.A: Switch the host's power on and off remotely through the management network
options.B: Change the VM's guest operating system without reinstalling applications
options.C: Swap VM memory pages to disk when the host runs short of physical RAM
options.D: Connect VMs to each other and to the physical network through the host's NICs

questions.answer_text: Connect VMs to each other and to the physical network through the host's NICs
questions.explanation: Port groups/VLANs on the vSwitch separate VM traffic just like a physical switch.

questions.question: A SAN provides ____ storage, while a NAS provides ____ storage.

options.A: File-level; object-level
options.B: Object-level; block-level
options.C: Block-level; file-level
options.D: File-level; block-level

questions.answer_text: Block-level; file-level
questions.explanation: SAN presents raw disks (LUNs) to servers; NAS shares files over the network.

questions.question: NAS devices share files with clients mainly using which protocols?

options.A: NFS and SMB/CIFS
options.B: SNMP and NTP
options.C: Fibre Channel and FCoE
options.D: iSCSI and FC

questions.answer_text: NFS and SMB/CIFS
questions.explanation: NFS is common for UNIX/Linux; SMB/CIFS for Windows.

questions.question: Which storage network typically uses dedicated fibre optic links and switches?

options.A: SAN (Fibre Channel)
options.B: Wi-Fi storage
options.C: DAS
options.D: NAS

questions.answer_text: SAN (Fibre Channel)
questions.explanation: Fibre Channel SANs give low-latency, high-throughput block access.

questions.question: iSCSI is a protocol that:

options.A: Is used only to connect tape libraries to backup servers
options.B: Needs dedicated Fibre Channel switches and HBAs to work
options.C: Carries SCSI block commands over standard TCP/IP Ethernet networks
options.D: Shares files with Windows clients using the SMB/CIFS protocol

questions.answer_text: Carries SCSI block commands over standard TCP/IP Ethernet networks
questions.explanation: iSCSI gives SAN-like block storage at lower cost using existing Ethernet.

questions.question: Direct Attached Storage (DAS) is:

options.A: Storage accessed by many servers over a dedicated Fibre Channel fabric
options.B: Storage connected directly to a single server and not shared over a network
options.C: Storage rented from a cloud provider and accessed over the internet
options.D: File storage shared with clients over the LAN using NFS or SMB

questions.answer_text: Storage connected directly to a single server and not shared over a network
questions.explanation: Internal disks or an external enclosure cabled to one server are DAS.

questions.question: Object storage (like Amazon S3) stores data as:

options.A: Fixed-size blocks presented to servers as raw disks (LUNs)
options.B: Files arranged in a hierarchical folder tree and shared with clients over NFS
options.C: Rows and columns of relational tables with SQL access
options.D: Objects with metadata and a unique ID, accessed through HTTP-based APIs

questions.answer_text: Objects with metadata and a unique ID, accessed through HTTP-based APIs
questions.explanation: It scales massively and suits unstructured data, backups, archives and data lakes.

questions.question: A high-transaction Oracle database needing low-latency disk I/O is best placed on:

options.A: A shared USB drive
options.B: Object storage via HTTP
options.C: SAN block storage
options.D: An FTP server

questions.answer_text: SAN block storage
questions.explanation: Databases need block-level random I/O with consistent low latency.

questions.question: How does HDFS differ from a traditional NAS?

options.A: HDFS is a single central file server appliance; NAS spreads replicated blocks across many commodity nodes and moves computation to the data
options.B: HDFS is block storage dedicated to a single database, while NAS is object storage accessed over HTTP
options.C: NAS replicates every block three times by default, while HDFS keeps only a single copy of each block
options.D: HDFS spreads replicated blocks across many commodity nodes and moves computation to data; NAS serves files from a central appliance

questions.answer_text: HDFS spreads replicated blocks across many commodity nodes and moves computation to data; NAS serves files from a central appliance
questions.explanation: HDFS is designed for huge files and parallel processing; NAS for shared file access.

questions.question: A storage system that can serve both block (FC/iSCSI) and file (NFS/SMB) access from the same array is called:

options.A: Direct attached storage
options.B: Unified storage
options.C: Tape library
options.D: Object gateway only

questions.answer_text: Unified storage
questions.explanation: It simplifies management when both databases and file shares are needed.

questions.question: In SAN terminology, a LUN is:

options.A: A RAID controller card installed inside the storage array
options.B: A fibre optic cable connecting the server's HBA to the SAN switch
options.C: A unique hardware identifier assigned to each Fibre Channel port
options.D: A logical disk carved from the storage array and presented to a host

questions.answer_text: A logical disk carved from the storage array and presented to a host
questions.explanation: LUN = Logical Unit Number. The host sees it as a local disk.

questions.question: Zoning in a Fibre Channel SAN is configured on the ____ to control which devices can communicate.

options.A: FC switch (fabric)
options.B: Database
options.C: Host operating system
options.D: Backup tape

questions.answer_text: FC switch (fabric)
questions.explanation: Zoning is like VLANs for the SAN fabric: hosts only see the storage ports in their zone.

questions.question: LUN masking is configured on the ____ to decide which hosts can access which LUNs.

options.A: DNS server
options.B: FC switch
options.C: Storage array
options.D: Application server

questions.answer_text: Storage array
questions.explanation: Zoning (switch) + LUN masking (array) together prevent unauthorised hosts from seeing data.

questions.question: A World Wide Name (WWN) in Fibre Channel is:

options.A: The registered name of the storage vendor, printed on the front panel of the array
options.B: A unique identifier for an FC port or device, similar to a MAC address
options.C: A DNS hostname assigned to the SAN management interface
options.D: The administrator password used to log in to the SAN switch

questions.answer_text: A unique identifier for an FC port or device, similar to a MAC address
questions.explanation: WWNs/WWPNs are used in zoning and LUN masking.

questions.question: Multipathing software on a server connected to a SAN provides:

options.A: Encryption of all disks presented from the storage array
options.B: Redundant paths to storage for failover and load balancing
options.C: Replication of databases from primary to DR storage
options.D: Additional CPU capacity for I/O-intensive applications

questions.answer_text: Redundant paths to storage for failover and load balancing
questions.explanation: If one HBA, cable or switch fails, I/O continues on another path.

questions.question: NVMe (Non-Volatile Memory Express) improves storage performance because:

options.A: It is designed for flash over PCIe with very low latency and many parallel queues
options.B: It replaces RAM by acting as the server's main memory for applications
options.C: It uses high-speed spinning disks with larger caches than SATA drives
options.D: It runs over Wi-Fi, removing the need for storage cables in the data centre

questions.answer_text: It is designed for flash over PCIe with very low latency and many parallel queues
questions.explanation: NVMe over Fabrics (NVMe-oF) extends these benefits across a network.

questions.question: With thin provisioning:

options.A: All requested space is reserved upfront on physical disks when the LUN is created
options.B: Data is automatically compressed so that more of it fits on each disk
options.C: Physical space is allocated only as data is actually written, allowing over-subscription
options.D: Disks are formatted with a thinner file system to reduce metadata overhead

questions.answer_text: Physical space is allocated only as data is actually written, allowing over-subscription
questions.explanation: Thin provisioning saves space but pools must be monitored to avoid running out.

questions.question: Arrange the typical SAN storage provisioning steps: (1) Host rescans, partitions and creates a file system (2) Create LUN from storage pool (3) Configure zoning and LUN masking (4) Create RAID group/storage pool
questions.explanation: Pool -> LUN -> zoning/masking -> host discovery and formatting.

questions.question: In Linux LVM, the correct hierarchy is:

options.A: Volume Group -> Physical Volume -> Logical Volume
options.B: Logical Volume -> Volume Group -> Physical Volume
options.C: Partition -> Logical Volume -> Physical Volume
options.D: Physical Volume -> Volume Group -> Logical Volume

questions.answer_text: Physical Volume -> Volume Group -> Logical Volume
questions.explanation: LVM allows resizing and spanning disks without repartitioning.

questions.question: Storage virtualization means:

options.A: Using part of each server's RAM as a fast storage layer for frequently used data
options.B: Pooling capacity from multiple physical storage devices into a single logical pool managed centrally
options.C: Deleting unused LUNs automatically so that space can be reused by other servers
options.D: Running the storage controller software inside a virtual machine instead of on dedicated hardware

questions.answer_text: Pooling capacity from multiple physical storage devices into a single logical pool managed centrally
questions.explanation: It simplifies provisioning, migration and tiering across arrays.

questions.question: RAID 0 provides:

options.A: Striping for performance with no redundancy
options.B: Mirroring of data on two disks for redundancy
options.C: Striping with double distributed parity
options.D: Striping with single distributed parity

questions.answer_text: Striping for performance with no redundancy
questions.explanation: Failure of any one disk in RAID 0 loses all data.

questions.question: RAID 1 is also known as:

options.A: Spanning
options.B: Parity
options.C: Striping
options.D: Mirroring

questions.answer_text: Mirroring
questions.explanation: Data is written identically to two disks; usable capacity is 50%.

questions.question: Which RAID level stripes data with parity distributed across all disks and needs at least 3 disks?

options.A: RAID 4
options.B: RAID 1
options.C: RAID 0
options.D: RAID 5

questions.answer_text: RAID 5
questions.explanation: RAID 5 tolerates the failure of one disk.

questions.question: RAID 6 differs from RAID 5 in that it:

options.A: Uses a single dedicated parity disk instead of distributing parity
options.B: Uses double distributed parity and can survive two simultaneous disk failures
options.C: Uses no parity at all and relies on mirroring every disk for protection
options.D: Needs only two disks and can survive the failure of either one

questions.answer_text: Uses double distributed parity and can survive two simultaneous disk failures
questions.explanation: RAID 6 needs at least 4 disks.

questions.question: RAID 10 (1+0) combines:

options.A: Two striped arrays without mirroring, needing 2 disks
options.B: Mirroring and striping, needing at least 4 disks
options.C: Striping and double parity, needing at least 4 disks
options.D: Parity on a dedicated disk, needing at least 3 disks

questions.answer_text: Mirroring and striping, needing at least 4 disks
questions.explanation: It gives high performance and redundancy; capacity efficiency is 50%.

questions.question: Which RAID level uses block-level striping with a DEDICATED parity disk?

options.A: RAID 5
options.B: RAID 10
options.C: RAID 6
options.D: RAID 4

questions.answer_text: RAID 4
questions.explanation: The dedicated parity disk becomes a write bottleneck, which RAID 5 solves by distributing parity.

questions.question: What is the usable capacity of five 2 TB disks in RAID 5?

options.A: 8 TB
options.B: 5 TB
options.C: 10 TB
options.D: 6 TB

questions.answer_text: 8 TB
questions.explanation: RAID 5 usable = (n - 1) x disk size = 4 x 2 TB.

questions.question: What is the usable capacity of six 4 TB disks in RAID 6?

options.A: 12 TB
options.B: 16 TB
options.C: 24 TB
options.D: 20 TB

questions.answer_text: 16 TB
questions.explanation: RAID 6 usable = (n - 2) x disk size = 4 x 4 TB.

questions.question: What is the usable capacity of eight 1 TB disks in RAID 10?

options.A: 4 TB
options.B: 8 TB
options.C: 7 TB
options.D: 6 TB

questions.answer_text: 4 TB
questions.explanation: Half of the raw capacity is used for mirrors.

questions.question: Why is RAID NOT a substitute for backup?

options.A: RAID disks cannot be replaced once they fail, so the data must come from backup anyway
options.B: It cannot be used to store databases, which are the most critical data in a bank
options.C: It does not protect against accidental deletion, corruption or ransomware, which are instantly applied to all disks
options.D: It is much slower than backup software, so restoring data from a RAID array after a failure takes far too long

questions.answer_text: It does not protect against accidental deletion, corruption or ransomware, which are instantly applied to all disks
questions.explanation: RAID protects against disk failure only (availability), not against logical data loss.

questions.question: A 'hot spare' disk in a RAID array:

options.A: Stores only the parity information for all the other disks in the array to speed up rebuilds
options.B: Holds the storage array's operating system and boot files
options.C: Sits idle and automatically replaces a failed disk so the rebuild starts immediately
options.D: Is used as a read cache to speed up frequently accessed data

questions.answer_text: Sits idle and automatically replaces a failed disk so the rebuild starts immediately
questions.explanation: It shortens the period in which the array runs degraded.

questions.question: Why is RAID 10 often preferred over RAID 5 for write-heavy OLTP databases and redo logs?

options.A: RAID 5 cannot be used for databases at all, while RAID 10 is the only level certified by database vendors
options.B: RAID 5 has a write penalty for parity calculation, while RAID 10 writes faster and rebuilds quicker
options.C: RAID 10 gives more usable capacity than RAID 5 from the same number of disks
options.D: RAID 10 needs fewer disks than RAID 5 for the same level of protection

questions.answer_text: RAID 5 has a write penalty for parity calculation, while RAID 10 writes faster and rebuilds quicker
questions.explanation: Each small RAID 5 write needs 4 back-end I/Os (read data, read parity, write data, write parity); RAID 10 needs 2.

questions.question: With very large disks, RAID 6 is often recommended instead of RAID 5 because:

options.A: Long rebuild times increase the chance of a second failure or read error, which RAID 5 cannot survive
options.B: RAID 6 is always faster than RAID 5 for both reads and writes on large disks
options.C: RAID 6 needs no parity calculation, so rebuilds of large disks finish much sooner
options.D: RAID 5 controllers cannot address individual disks larger than two terabytes, so the extra capacity of large disks is wasted

questions.answer_text: Long rebuild times increase the chance of a second failure or read error, which RAID 5 cannot survive
questions.explanation: Rebuilding a multi-TB disk can take many hours, during which RAID 5 has no protection.

questions.question: IOPS in storage performance stands for:

options.A: Input/Output Operations Per Second
options.B: Internet Operations Per Session
options.C: Indexed Objects Per Storage
options.D: Internal Operations Processing Speed

questions.answer_text: Input/Output Operations Per Second
questions.explanation: OLTP workloads with small random I/O are measured mainly by IOPS and latency.

questions.question: Large sequential workloads like backups and video are mainly measured by ____, while small random OLTP workloads are measured by ____.

options.A: IOPS; throughput (MB/s)
options.B: Capacity; latency
options.C: Latency; capacity
options.D: Throughput (MB/s); IOPS

questions.answer_text: Throughput (MB/s); IOPS
questions.explanation: Throughput = IOPS x I/O size.

questions.question: In a hard disk, the time taken for the required sector to rotate under the read/write head is called:

options.A: Seek time
options.B: Transfer time
options.C: Rotational latency
options.D: Access control time

questions.answer_text: Rotational latency
questions.explanation: Seek time is the time to move the head to the correct track.

questions.question: In a hard disk, the time taken to move the read/write head to the correct track is called:

options.A: Rotational latency
options.B: Mean time to repair
options.C: Queue time
options.D: Seek time

questions.answer_text: Seek time
questions.explanation: Total access time ~ seek time + rotational latency + transfer time.

questions.question: What is the average rotational latency of a 15,000 RPM disk?

options.A: 4 milliseconds
options.B: 2 milliseconds
options.C: 1 millisecond
options.D: 8 milliseconds

questions.answer_text: 2 milliseconds
questions.explanation: One rotation = 60/15000 s = 4 ms; average latency = half a rotation = 2 ms.

questions.question: Compared to HDDs, SSDs provide:

options.A: Mechanical read/write heads that give faster seek times
options.B: Lower speed than HDDs, but always a much lower cost per GB of capacity stored
options.C: Much higher IOPS and lower latency because they have no moving parts
options.D: Better performance only for sequential tape-like workloads

questions.answer_text: Much higher IOPS and lower latency because they have no moving parts
questions.explanation: SSDs are used for performance tiers; HDDs for cheap capacity.

questions.question: Automated storage tiering means:

options.A: Frequently used (hot) data is moved to fast SSD tiers and rarely used (cold) data to cheaper disks
options.B: Data older than 30 days is deleted automatically to free up space on the fast tier
options.C: Each user or application gets its own dedicated disk tier that is never shared
options.D: All data is kept permanently on the slowest and cheapest tier so that overall storage cost is minimised

questions.answer_text: Frequently used (hot) data is moved to fast SSD tiers and rarely used (cold) data to cheaper disks
questions.explanation: It balances performance and cost based on access patterns.

questions.question: Storage deduplication:

options.A: Mirrors every data block to a second disk for redundancy
options.B: Splits files into stripes spread across several disks
options.C: Stores only one copy of identical data blocks and replaces duplicates with references
options.D: Encrypts duplicate files so that only the original owner of the data can read the copies

questions.answer_text: Stores only one copy of identical data blocks and replaces duplicates with references
questions.explanation: Very effective for backups and VDI where much data repeats.

questions.question: A storage array snapshot is typically implemented using:

options.A: An automatic backup of the volume to tape at the moment the snapshot is created
options.B: A full physical copy of all the data on the volume each time a snapshot is taken
options.C: Deleting old blocks from the volume so that new data can be written in their place
options.D: Copy-on-write or redirect-on-write, recording only changed blocks after the snapshot

questions.answer_text: Copy-on-write or redirect-on-write, recording only changed blocks after the snapshot
questions.explanation: Snapshots are quick and space-efficient but depend on the source volume.

questions.question: Write-back caching in a storage controller improves write performance, but it must be protected by:

options.A: Battery/flash backup so cached data is not lost on power failure
options.B: Reducing the number of disks behind the controller
options.C: Configuring all volumes as RAID 0 to avoid parity overhead
options.D: Disabling RAID protection on the volumes that use the cache

questions.answer_text: Battery/flash backup so cached data is not lost on power failure
questions.explanation: Unprotected write-back cache could lose acknowledged writes during power loss.

questions.question: A full backup:

options.A: Copies all selected data every time; slowest to take but simplest and fastest to restore
options.B: Copies only the operating system and settings so that the server can be rebuilt quickly
options.C: Copies only data changed since the last full backup; restore needs the full plus the latest copy
options.D: Copies only data changed since the last backup of any type; fastest to take but slowest to restore

questions.answer_text: Copies all selected data every time; slowest to take but simplest and fastest to restore
questions.explanation: Full backups need the most storage and time.

questions.question: An incremental backup copies:

options.A: All data every time
options.B: Only data changed since the last full backup, ignoring other backups
options.C: Only data changed since the last backup of any type
options.D: Only the database logs

questions.answer_text: Only data changed since the last backup of any type
questions.explanation: Incrementals are fastest and smallest to take, but restore needs the full plus every incremental.

questions.question: A differential backup copies:

options.A: All data every time
options.B: All data changed since the last full backup
options.C: Only data changed since the last incremental backup
options.D: Only system files

questions.answer_text: All data changed since the last full backup
questions.explanation: Restore needs only the full backup plus the latest differential.

questions.question: A full backup is taken on Sunday and incremental backups Monday to Friday. The server crashes on Thursday after Thursday's backup. What is needed to restore?

options.A: Sunday full + Wednesday and Thursday incrementals, since earlier changes are included
options.B: Sunday full + Thursday's incremental backup only
options.C: Thursday's incremental backup only, since it is the latest
options.D: Sunday full + Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday incrementals

questions.answer_text: Sunday full + Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday incrementals
questions.explanation: Each incremental contains only one day's changes, so all are needed in sequence.

questions.question: A full backup is taken on Sunday and differential backups every day. The server crashes on Thursday after Thursday's backup. What is needed to restore?

options.A: Thursday differential only
options.B: Sunday full + all differentials from Monday to Thursday
options.C: Monday differential + Thursday differential
options.D: Sunday full + Thursday differential

questions.answer_text: Sunday full + Thursday differential
questions.explanation: Each differential contains all changes since the full backup.

questions.question: Which backup type gives the FASTEST restoration?

options.A: Incremental backup
options.B: Full backup
options.C: Differential backup
options.D: Transaction log backup chain

questions.answer_text: Full backup
questions.explanation: Restore order of speed: full > full + differential > full + many incrementals.

questions.question: Which statement about the size of differential backups is correct?

options.A: Each differential is smaller than the previous day's differential
options.B: All differentials are about the same size as each daily incremental
options.C: Each differential is larger than the full backup it is based on
options.D: Each differential grows larger every day until the next full backup

questions.answer_text: Each differential grows larger every day until the next full backup
questions.explanation: They keep accumulating all changes since the last full.

questions.question: In Windows file backups, which backup types normally CLEAR the archive bit after copying a file?

options.A: Differential only
options.B: Full and differential
options.C: Full and incremental
options.D: Incremental and differential

questions.answer_text: Full and incremental
questions.explanation: The differential leaves the archive bit set, so it keeps copying everything changed since the full.

questions.question: A 'synthetic full' backup is:

options.A: A full backup built on the backup server by combining the last full with later incrementals, without reading production data again
options.B: A storage snapshot taken on the production array and later copied to tape as a full backup
options.C: A full backup of artificially generated test data that is used only to check that the backup software is working properly after an upgrade
options.D: A full backup taken twice in a row and compared byte by byte to confirm that both copies match

questions.answer_text: A full backup built on the backup server by combining the last full with later incrementals, without reading production data again
questions.explanation: It reduces load on production systems and shortens the backup window.

questions.question: A backup taken while the system or database remains online and available to users is called:

options.A: Warm site backup
options.B: Static backup
options.C: Cold (offline) backup
options.D: Hot (online) backup

questions.answer_text: Hot (online) backup
questions.explanation: Cold backups require the application/database to be shut down.

questions.question: A 'mirror backup' differs from other backups because:

options.A: It keeps an exact copy of the source, so deleted files are also removed from the backup
options.B: It stores only the differences since the last backup, so it is the smallest backup
options.C: It keeps every historical version of every file, so nothing is ever deleted from it
options.D: It is always encrypted and compressed, so it takes less space than other backups

questions.answer_text: It keeps an exact copy of the source, so deleted files are also removed from the backup
questions.explanation: Mirrors protect against hardware loss but not against accidental deletion.

questions.question: Continuous Data Protection (CDP) is used when:

options.A: Storage is extremely limited and only the latest copy can be kept
options.B: Backups are needed only once a year for audit and compliance purposes
options.C: Data rarely changes, so periodic full backups would waste storage
options.D: Near-zero RPO is required, since every change is captured as it happens

questions.answer_text: Near-zero RPO is required, since every change is captured as it happens
questions.explanation: CDP lets you restore to almost any point in time.

questions.question: To keep RPO low for a busy database, which backup should be taken most frequently?

options.A: Transaction log / archived redo log backups
options.B: Full database backups taken every single hour
options.C: Differential backups once a month
options.D: Operating system image backups

questions.answer_text: Transaction log / archived redo log backups
questions.explanation: Frequent log backups allow point-in-time recovery close to the failure time.

questions.question: Restoring a complete system (OS, applications, settings and data) onto new hardware with no pre-installed OS is called:

options.A: Differential restore
options.B: Bare-metal restore
options.C: File-level restore
options.D: Snapshot rollback

questions.answer_text: Bare-metal restore
questions.explanation: Useful after total server failure or disaster.

questions.question: To protect against a single disk failure with no downtime and no data loss, the most suitable option is:

options.A: Disk mirroring (RAID 1)
options.B: Weekly full backup
options.C: Cold site
options.D: Monthly archive

questions.answer_text: Disk mirroring (RAID 1)
questions.explanation: Mirroring gives continuous availability; backups are still needed for logical errors.

questions.question: The 3-2-1 backup rule recommends:

options.A: 3 backups per day, 2 restore tests per week, 1 audit per year
options.B: 3 full backups per week, 2 incrementals per day, 1 monthly archive
options.C: 3 copies of data, on 2 different media types, with 1 copy offsite
options.D: 3 backup servers, 2 data centres, 1 tape library for archives

questions.answer_text: 3 copies of data, on 2 different media types, with 1 copy offsite
questions.explanation: It protects against media failure and site-level disasters.

questions.question: The modern '3-2-1-1-0' backup rule adds which two requirements to 3-2-1?

options.A: One extra full backup every week, and zero incremental backups during the week
options.B: One copy at the DR site, and zero downtime during backups
options.C: One immutable or air-gapped copy, and zero errors after restore verification
options.D: One copy in the public cloud, and zero copies on tape

questions.answer_text: One immutable or air-gapped copy, and zero errors after restore verification
questions.explanation: Immutable/offline copies defend against ransomware that targets backups.

questions.question: The main advantage of keeping a backup copy offsite is:

options.A: Faster restore of individual files for day-to-day recovery requests from users
options.B: No need to encrypt the backup media because they are stored securely
options.C: Protection against disasters like fire or flood that destroy the primary site
options.D: Lower cost than onsite backup because no media are needed

questions.answer_text: Protection against disasters like fire or flood that destroy the primary site
questions.explanation: Onsite copies give fast restores; offsite copies give disaster protection.

questions.question: The main advantage of onsite backup is:

options.A: Automatic compliance with all regulations
options.B: Quick restoration of data for day-to-day recovery
options.C: No need for storage media
options.D: Protection from site-wide disasters like fire and flood

questions.answer_text: Quick restoration of data for day-to-day recovery
questions.explanation: Best practice is to use both onsite and offsite copies.

questions.question: An 'air-gapped' backup is:

options.A: Kept only in the backup server's RAM so that it disappears if the server is attacked
options.B: Stored in a cooled server room with controlled airflow to protect the backup media
options.C: Physically or logically isolated from the production network so attackers cannot reach it
options.D: Transmitted over a dedicated wireless link instead of the production network

questions.answer_text: Physically or logically isolated from the production network so attackers cannot reach it
questions.explanation: Offline tapes or isolated vaults are typical air-gapped copies.

questions.question: Immutable (WORM) backups help against ransomware because:

options.A: They are stored unencrypted, so ransomware cannot recognise them as backups
options.B: They cannot be modified or deleted during the retention period, even by administrators
options.C: They take less storage space because duplicate data is removed before writing
options.D: They are restored much faster than normal backups because they are not compressed

questions.answer_text: They cannot be modified or deleted during the retention period, even by administrators
questions.explanation: WORM = Write Once, Read Many.

questions.question: Sending backup tapes to a secure offsite storage facility on a regular schedule is called:

options.A: Mirroring
options.B: Vaulting
options.C: Tiering
options.D: Deduplication

questions.answer_text: Vaulting
questions.explanation: Tapes in transit and in the vault should be encrypted and tracked.

questions.question: Which is a key advantage of tape for long-term backup?

options.A: Low cost per GB, long shelf life and natural offline (air-gap) protection
options.B: Data can be read directly from the cartridge without any tape drive
options.C: Fastest random access to individual files compared with disk and SSD
options.D: No physical handling, labelling or transport of media is ever required

questions.answer_text: Low cost per GB, long shelf life and natural offline (air-gap) protection
questions.explanation: LTO (Linear Tape-Open) is the common enterprise tape format.

questions.question: Before backing up bank data to a public cloud, which consideration is MOST important?

options.A: The number of free email accounts bundled with the backup service
options.B: Encryption, data residency/localisation and regulatory approval of the provider
options.C: Only the lowest storage price per GB offered by the provider for long-term retention
options.D: The provider's brand popularity among retail customers

questions.answer_text: Encryption, data residency/localisation and regulatory approval of the provider
questions.explanation: Banks must comply with RBI outsourcing and data-localisation requirements.

questions.question: A backup retention policy defines:

options.A: Which users are allowed to log in to the backup server
options.B: Which antivirus product must scan the backup media
options.C: How fast the backup server must complete each job
options.D: How long each type of backup must be kept before deletion

questions.answer_text: How long each type of backup must be kept before deletion
questions.explanation: Retention is decided by business needs, legal and regulatory requirements.

questions.question: In the Grandfather-Father-Son (GFS) rotation scheme:

options.A: Only the latest three backups are kept, named son, father and grandfather
options.B: Daily backups are 'sons', weekly backups 'fathers' and monthly backups 'grandfathers'
options.C: Monthly backups are 'sons', weekly backups 'fathers' and daily backups 'grandfathers'
options.D: Backups are rotated between three data centres named son, father and grandfather

questions.answer_text: Daily backups are 'sons', weekly backups 'fathers' and monthly backups 'grandfathers'
questions.explanation: GFS gives many restore points while reusing media efficiently.

questions.question: Under the PML Rules, banks must preserve records of transactions for at least:

options.A: 2 years from the date of transaction
options.B: 6 months from the date of transaction
options.C: 1 year from the date of transaction
options.D: 5 years from the date of transaction

questions.answer_text: 5 years from the date of transaction
questions.explanation: KYC/identity records are kept for at least 5 years after the business relationship ends.

questions.question: How does an archive differ from a backup?

options.A: A backup moves inactive data to long-term storage for compliance; an archive is a copy for recovering current data
options.B: Archives are overwritten every day, while backups must be kept forever for regulatory purposes
options.C: An archive and a backup are identical, and the terms can be used interchangeably in a retention policy
options.D: An archive moves inactive data to long-term storage for retention/compliance; a backup is a copy for recovering current data

questions.answer_text: An archive moves inactive data to long-term storage for retention/compliance; a backup is a copy for recovering current data
questions.explanation: Archives often become the only copy of old data, so they must be protected too.

questions.question: The 'backup window' is:

options.A: The period during which backups can run without affecting business operations
options.B: The maximum time for which a backup tape can be kept before it must be overwritten and reused
options.C: The main screen of the backup software showing job status
options.D: The time taken to restore a server after a failure

questions.answer_text: The period during which backups can run without affecting business operations
questions.explanation: Incremental, synthetic fulls and snapshots help fit backups into short windows.

questions.question: The best way to make sure backups will actually work during a disaster is to:

options.A: Buy more tapes
options.B: Check that every backup job shows 'completed' in the console
options.C: Perform periodic test restores and verify the data
options.D: Increase retention

questions.answer_text: Perform periodic test restores and verify the data
questions.explanation: A backup is only as good as its last successful restore test.

questions.question: Backup tapes that are sent offsite should be encrypted mainly to:

options.A: Protect customer data if a tape is lost or stolen
options.B: Avoid the need to label tapes before sending them
options.C: Reduce the size so that more data fits on each tape
options.D: Increase the speed at which backups are written

questions.answer_text: Protect customer data if a tape is lost or stolen
questions.explanation: Encryption keys must be stored separately and be available at the DR site.

questions.question: Data backup and recovery software is an essential requirement today mainly because of:

options.A: Falling server costs that make replacement easier than recovery
options.B: Shrinking data volumes that make backups quick to complete
options.C: Faster internet speeds that make cloud backup cheaper and quicker than tape-based backup
options.D: Threats like ransomware, hardware failure, human error and regulatory requirements

questions.answer_text: Threats like ransomware, hardware failure, human error and regulatory requirements
questions.explanation: Without reliable backups, a single incident can cause permanent data loss.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of NIST's five essential characteristics of cloud computing?

options.A: Rapid elasticity
options.B: Broad network access
options.C: Measured service
options.D: Dedicated physical hardware for each customer

questions.answer_text: Dedicated physical hardware for each customer
questions.explanation: The fifth is resource pooling (multi-tenant sharing), the opposite of dedicated hardware.

questions.question: 'Measured service' in cloud computing means:

options.A: Usage is not recorded, so customers pay a flat fee regardless of use
options.B: Service quality is measured only through yearly customer surveys
options.C: Resource usage is metered so customers pay for what they use
options.D: Services are delivered in fixed, pre-measured monthly capacity blocks

questions.answer_text: Resource usage is metered so customers pay for what they use
questions.explanation: Pay-as-you-go billing is based on metering of compute, storage and network.

questions.question: Moving from owning servers to using cloud services mainly converts:

options.A: Variable monthly costs into fixed multi-year asset costs
options.B: Operational expenditure (OpEx) into capital expenditure (CapEx)
options.C: Capital expenditure (CapEx) into operational expenditure (OpEx)
options.D: Software licence costs into hardware purchase costs

questions.answer_text: Capital expenditure (CapEx) into operational expenditure (OpEx)
questions.explanation: There is no large upfront purchase; costs follow usage.

questions.question: Match the cloud concepts: (P) Elasticity (Q) Scalability (R) Reliability | (1) Ability of the system to keep working correctly and recover from failures (2) Automatically adding and removing resources in line with short-term demand (3) Ability to handle growth by adding resources
questions.explanation: Elasticity is dynamic up-and-down scaling; scalability is capacity to grow; reliability is consistent correct operation.

questions.question: A Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) is:

options.A: A logically isolated network section within a public cloud where the customer controls IP ranges, subnets and routing
options.B: A private data centre owned and operated by the bank on its own premises, with no public cloud provider involved at all
options.C: A type of SaaS application that is hosted privately for a single customer by the software vendor
options.D: A VPN client application installed on employees' laptops to connect securely to the office network

questions.answer_text: A logically isolated network section within a public cloud where the customer controls IP ranges, subnets and routing
questions.explanation: Security groups and network ACLs control traffic in and out of the VPC.

questions.question: Cloud 'Availability Zones' within a region are:

options.A: Pricing tiers that offer different discounts based on how much capacity the customer commits
options.B: Physically separate data centres with independent power and networking, used to build highly available applications
options.C: Countries in which the cloud provider is legally allowed to offer its services to banks
options.D: Time zones used by the cloud provider's support teams to provide round-the-clock assistance to customers worldwide

questions.answer_text: Physically separate data centres with independent power and networking, used to build highly available applications
questions.explanation: Spreading workloads across zones protects against a single data-centre failure.

questions.question: In IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service), the provider supplies:

options.A: A managed development platform; the customer only deploys application code
options.B: Virtual servers, storage and networking; the customer manages OS, middleware and applications
options.C: Physical servers shipped to the customer's own data centre for installation and management by the customer
options.D: Ready-to-use applications; the customer only manages users and data

questions.answer_text: Virtual servers, storage and networking; the customer manages OS, middleware and applications
questions.explanation: Examples: AWS EC2, Azure Virtual Machines, Google Compute Engine.

questions.question: PaaS (Platform as a Service) is best described as:

options.A: Ready-made end-user software applications accessed through a web browser
options.B: A managed platform to develop, run and deploy applications without managing the underlying servers
options.C: A dedicated physical server rented by the month from a hosting company
options.D: Renting raw virtual machines, storage and networks on which the customer installs everything

questions.answer_text: A managed platform to develop, run and deploy applications without managing the underlying servers
questions.explanation: Examples: Google App Engine, Azure App Service, Heroku.

questions.question: Microsoft 365, Gmail and Salesforce CRM are examples of:

options.A: PaaS
options.B: IaaS
options.C: On-premise software
options.D: SaaS

questions.answer_text: SaaS
questions.explanation: In SaaS the provider manages everything; the customer just uses the application.

questions.question: Match the service with its model: (P) AWS EC2 (Q) Google App Engine (R) Salesforce CRM | (1) SaaS (2) IaaS (3) PaaS
questions.explanation: EC2 = virtual machines (IaaS); App Engine = platform (PaaS); Salesforce = application (SaaS).

questions.question: In an IaaS deployment, who is responsible for patching the guest operating system of the virtual machines?

options.A: The hardware manufacturer
options.B: The customer
options.C: The cloud provider
options.D: Nobody - it is automatic

questions.answer_text: The customer
questions.explanation: Under the shared responsibility model, the provider secures the infrastructure; the customer secures what runs on it.

questions.question: Even in a SaaS model, which responsibility always remains with the customer (the bank)?

options.A: Its data, and managing user identities and access rights
options.B: Patching the provider's servers
options.C: Physical security of the provider's data centre buildings
options.D: Maintaining the provider's hypervisor

questions.answer_text: Its data, and managing user identities and access rights
questions.explanation: Customers remain accountable for their data, users and access configuration in every model.

questions.question: Under the cloud shared responsibility model, physical security of the data centre is the responsibility of:

options.A: The customer in IaaS, and the provider in SaaS
options.B: The customer in all models
options.C: The cloud service provider in all models
options.D: Shared equally between customer and provider

questions.answer_text: The cloud service provider in all models
questions.explanation: The provider is responsible for 'security OF the cloud'; the customer for 'security IN the cloud'.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a serverless computing service?

options.A: Google Cloud Functions
options.B: Azure Functions
options.C: AWS Lambda
options.D: Amazon EC2

questions.answer_text: Amazon EC2
questions.explanation: EC2 provides virtual machines that the customer must manage; the others run code on events without servers to manage.

questions.question: Serverless computing (Function as a Service) means:

options.A: Applications are deployed only on mobile phones and synchronise with a central database when online
options.B: The customer rents virtual machines by the hour and must manage the OS, patches and scaling
options.C: No physical servers are used anywhere, because the code runs entirely inside users' web browsers and mobile devices
options.D: Code runs on demand in response to events and is billed per execution, with no servers for the customer to manage

questions.answer_text: Code runs on demand in response to events and is billed per execution, with no servers for the customer to manage
questions.explanation: Servers still exist, but the provider manages and scales them automatically.

questions.question: A public cloud is:

options.A: Owned and operated by a provider and shared by many customers over the internet
options.B: Shared only among organisations with common needs, such as government agencies
options.C: Located only inside the bank's own premises and managed by its IT staff
options.D: Dedicated to a single organisation and hosted either on-premise or by a provider

questions.answer_text: Owned and operated by a provider and shared by many customers over the internet
questions.explanation: Examples: AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle Cloud.

questions.question: A private cloud is:

options.A: A combination of public and private clouds with portability of workloads between them
options.B: Infrastructure shared by many unrelated customers over the internet
options.C: A free service offered by public cloud providers to small businesses
options.D: Cloud infrastructure dedicated to a single organisation, on-premise or hosted

questions.answer_text: Cloud infrastructure dedicated to a single organisation, on-premise or hosted
questions.explanation: It gives more control and customisation, but the organisation bears more cost.

questions.question: A hybrid cloud:

options.A: Is shared by a group of banks with common regulatory requirements
options.B: Uses services from two or more public cloud providers, without any private cloud
options.C: Combines private and public clouds, with workloads and data able to move between them
options.D: Uses only on-premise physical servers that are managed like a cloud

questions.answer_text: Combines private and public clouds, with workloads and data able to move between them
questions.explanation: Banks often keep core systems private and use public cloud for less sensitive or bursty workloads.

questions.question: A cloud shared by several organisations with common requirements (for example, banks with similar regulatory needs) is a:

options.A: Personal cloud
options.B: Private cloud
options.C: Community cloud
options.D: Public cloud

questions.answer_text: Community cloud
questions.explanation: Costs are shared while meeting common security and compliance requirements.

questions.question: Using services from two or more different public cloud providers is called:

options.A: Hybrid cloud
options.B: Multi-cloud
options.C: Community cloud
options.D: Cloud bursting

questions.answer_text: Multi-cloud
questions.explanation: Multi-cloud reduces dependency on one provider but increases management complexity.

questions.question: Cloud bursting means:

options.A: Shutting down unused cloud resources automatically to reduce monthly cost
options.B: Splitting a single application across three or more public cloud providers
options.C: Running workloads in a private cloud and overflowing to a public cloud during demand peaks
options.D: Moving all workloads permanently from a public cloud back to the bank's own private cloud

questions.answer_text: Running workloads in a private cloud and overflowing to a public cloud during demand peaks
questions.explanation: It suits seasonal peaks such as festive sales or tax deadlines.

questions.question: Which statement correctly compares public and private clouds?

options.A: Public cloud gives the customer physical control of servers, while private cloud does not
options.B: Private cloud always has lower total cost, while public cloud always offers greater control and isolation
options.C: Private cloud cannot use virtualization, while public cloud depends entirely on it
options.D: Public cloud offers lower upfront cost and high elasticity; private cloud offers greater control and isolation

questions.answer_text: Public cloud offers lower upfront cost and high elasticity; private cloud offers greater control and isolation
questions.explanation: The choice depends on data sensitivity, regulatory needs, cost and scale.

questions.question: Which is a key advantage of public cloud for banks?

options.A: Faster innovation and on-demand scalability without large upfront investment
options.B: Guaranteed zero downtime for all applications hosted in the cloud
options.C: Complete transfer of all regulatory and compliance obligations to the cloud provider
options.D: No need for the bank to implement any security controls of its own

questions.answer_text: Faster innovation and on-demand scalability without large upfront investment
questions.explanation: Regulatory and security responsibilities remain with the bank even when using cloud.

questions.question: As per RBI's April 2018 directive on storage of payment system data, data relating to payment systems operated in India must be:

options.A: Stored only in systems located in India
options.B: Deleted from all systems after 24 hours
options.C: Stored in India with a mandatory copy in the USA
options.D: Stored anywhere, provided it is encrypted

questions.answer_text: Stored only in systems located in India
questions.explanation: This data localisation requirement must be considered when using cloud services.

questions.question: RBI's Master Direction on Outsourcing of Information Technology Services (April 2023), which covers cloud services, came into effect from:

options.A: 1 January 2022
options.B: 1 October 2023
options.C: 1 July 2020
options.D: 1 April 2025

questions.answer_text: 1 October 2023
questions.explanation: It requires due diligence, contractual safeguards, audit rights, exit plans and board oversight for IT outsourcing.

questions.question: A 'right to audit' clause in a cloud contract allows:

options.A: The service provider to audit the bank's branches and internal processes
options.B: The bank and its regulator (RBI) to audit or inspect the service provider
options.C: The bank's customers to audit the provider's data centre security
options.D: The service provider to change prices after giving one month's notice

questions.answer_text: The bank and its regulator (RBI) to audit or inspect the service provider
questions.explanation: Regulators insist on access to information and audit rights for outsourced services.

questions.question: Vendor lock-in in cloud computing means:

options.A: A requirement that all of the bank's applications must run in a single availability zone
options.B: A contract clause that prevents the cloud provider from increasing its prices during the agreed contract term
options.C: A security feature that locks customer accounts after repeated failed login attempts
options.D: Difficulty and high cost in moving from one provider to another due to proprietary services or formats

questions.answer_text: Difficulty and high cost in moving from one provider to another due to proprietary services or formats
questions.explanation: Open standards, portability and an exit strategy reduce lock-in.

questions.question: An exit strategy in a cloud outsourcing contract is important because it:

options.A: Is needed only for SaaS contracts and not for IaaS or PaaS arrangements
options.B: Allows the bank to stop paying the provider immediately whenever service quality drops below the agreed level
options.C: Prevents the provider from ever exiting the contract before its full term ends
options.D: Ensures the bank can move data and services out smoothly if the contract ends or the provider fails

questions.answer_text: Ensures the bank can move data and services out smoothly if the contract ends or the provider fails
questions.explanation: It covers data return/deletion, transition support and timelines.

questions.question: 'Concentration risk' in cloud adoption by the banking sector refers to:

options.A: Many financial institutions depending on the same few cloud providers, creating systemic risk
options.B: Customer data being concentrated in one database table, making queries slow
options.C: Too many virtual machines being placed on a single physical host in the provider's data centre
options.D: Too many users from one branch accessing the cloud at the same time

questions.answer_text: Many financial institutions depending on the same few cloud providers, creating systemic risk
questions.explanation: An outage at a major provider could affect many banks at once.

questions.question: The Government of India's cloud computing initiative (GI Cloud) is known as:

options.A: DigiLocker
options.B: Bharat Net
options.C: Aadhaar
options.D: MeghRaj

questions.answer_text: MeghRaj
questions.explanation: MeitY also empanels cloud service providers for government use.

questions.question: Data residency refers to:

options.A: The length of time for which data must be retained
options.B: The owner of the building that houses the data centre
options.C: The file format in which the data is stored
options.D: The geographic location where data is physically stored

questions.answer_text: The geographic location where data is physically stored
questions.explanation: Residency determines which country's laws apply to the data.

questions.question: The most common cause of data breaches in public cloud environments is:

options.A: Physical theft of servers and disks from the provider's data centres by insiders or contractors
options.B: Use of too many encryption keys by the cloud customer
options.C: Failure of the provider's power supply and cooling systems
options.D: Misconfiguration, such as publicly exposed storage buckets or open security groups

questions.answer_text: Misconfiguration, such as publicly exposed storage buckets or open security groups
questions.explanation: Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) tools continuously check for such misconfigurations.

questions.question: A Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB) is used to:

options.A: Replace the cloud provider's own data centre security controls with the bank's own security controls and staff
options.B: Give visibility and enforce security policies on users' access to cloud services, including detecting shadow IT
options.C: Back up on-premise tape libraries to cloud storage for long-term archival
options.D: Resell cloud services from several providers to customers at a discounted price

questions.answer_text: Give visibility and enforce security policies on users' access to cloud services, including detecting shadow IT
questions.explanation: CASBs sit between users and cloud services, applying DLP, access control and monitoring.

questions.question: Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) tools are mainly used to:

options.A: Manage employee attendance and leave records stored in cloud HR applications
options.B: Continuously detect and fix misconfigurations and compliance violations in cloud accounts
options.C: Encrypt employees' laptops and mobile devices before they are allowed to access any cloud services
options.D: Monitor CCTV cameras at branches using cloud-based video analytics

questions.answer_text: Continuously detect and fix misconfigurations and compliance violations in cloud accounts
questions.explanation: E.g. alerting on unencrypted storage, open ports or excessive permissions.

questions.question: In cloud security, IAM (Identity and Access Management) is used to:

options.A: Assign public IP addresses to virtual machines in the cloud account
options.B: Store backups of cloud databases in a separate region
options.C: Control who can access which cloud resources and what actions they can perform
options.D: Increase the speed of cloud servers by allocating more CPU to important users

questions.answer_text: Control who can access which cloud resources and what actions they can perform
questions.explanation: IAM policies should follow least privilege with MFA for privileged users.

questions.question: Best practice for a cloud account's root/super-admin user is to:

options.A: Use it for all daily administration tasks so that permission errors never occur
options.B: Enable MFA, lock away the credentials and use separate least-privilege accounts for daily work
options.C: Share its credentials among the whole cloud team so that anyone can respond quickly to incidents
options.D: Disable logging for it so that sensitive administrative actions are not recorded

questions.answer_text: Enable MFA, lock away the credentials and use separate least-privilege accounts for daily work
questions.explanation: Compromise of the root account gives full control over all resources and billing.

questions.question: BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) in cloud means:

options.A: The customer generates and controls the encryption keys used to protect its data in the cloud
options.B: The cloud stores data without encryption so that the customer can bring its own tools
options.C: The provider generates and controls all keys, and the customer cannot see or manage them
options.D: Employees bring their own laptops and phones to access the bank's cloud applications

questions.answer_text: The customer generates and controls the encryption keys used to protect its data in the cloud
questions.explanation: BYOK/HYOK give the bank more control over who can decrypt its data.

questions.question: The main security risk of multi-tenancy in public cloud is:

options.A: Each tenant needing much more physical data-centre space than with on-premise servers
options.B: Possible data leakage or interference between tenants sharing the same infrastructure
options.C: Tenants losing internet access whenever another tenant's workload is heavy
options.D: Higher electricity bills charged to each tenant for shared cooling

questions.answer_text: Possible data leakage or interference between tenants sharing the same infrastructure
questions.explanation: Providers use strong logical isolation, and customers add encryption and access controls.

questions.question: Which ISO standard provides guidance specifically for protecting personal data (PII) in public clouds?

options.A: ISO/IEC 27018
options.C: ISO/IEC 27017
options.D: ISO 9001

questions.answer_text: ISO/IEC 27018
questions.explanation: ISO 27017 covers cloud security controls; 27018 covers PII protection in public cloud.

questions.question: In Docker, the difference between an image and a container is:

options.A: A container is a read-only template; an image is a running instance of a container
options.B: An image and a container are the same thing, just named differently in tools
options.C: An image is a read-only template; a container is a running instance of an image
options.D: An image is a full virtual machine; a container is a backup of that machine

questions.answer_text: An image is a read-only template; a container is a running instance of an image
questions.explanation: Many containers can be started from the same image.

questions.question: Kubernetes is mainly used for:

options.A: Orchestrating containers: scheduling, scaling, self-healing and rolling updates
options.B: Designing relational database schemas for cloud applications
options.C: Encrypting email traffic between cloud applications and users
options.D: Writing and compiling Java microservices into container images for deployment to the cloud

questions.answer_text: Orchestrating containers: scheduling, scaling, self-healing and rolling updates
questions.explanation: Originally developed by Google, it is now a CNCF project.

questions.question: In Kubernetes, the smallest deployable unit that can hold one or more containers is a:

options.A: Pod
options.B: Node
options.C: Namespace
options.D: Cluster

questions.answer_text: Pod
questions.explanation: Containers in a pod share network and storage.

questions.question: What does a liveness probe in Kubernetes do?

options.A: Removes the pod from the load balancer until ready
options.B: Restarts the container if it fails the health check
options.C: Restarts the whole physical node running the pod
options.D: Scales out the deployment by adding more pods

questions.answer_text: Restarts the container if it fails the health check
questions.explanation: It detects hung applications and lets Kubernetes heal them automatically.

questions.question: In Kubernetes, a readiness probe is used to:

options.A: Add or remove worker nodes based on cluster load
options.B: Delete old container images that are no longer used
options.C: Decide whether a pod should receive traffic from the service
options.D: Restart the container whenever it fails its health check

questions.answer_text: Decide whether a pod should receive traffic from the service
questions.explanation: A pod that is starting up or temporarily overloaded is removed from load balancing until ready.

questions.question: A container registry (e.g. Docker Hub, Harbor, Amazon ECR) is used to:

options.A: Run virtual machines on demand
options.B: Assign IP addresses to running pods
options.C: Store database backups and archives
options.D: Store and distribute container images

questions.answer_text: Store and distribute container images
questions.explanation: Private registries with image scanning help prevent vulnerable images reaching production.

questions.question: The availability and reliability of a cloud service or application are formally defined in the:

options.A: Business Impact Analysis (BIA)
options.B: Request for Change
options.C: Service Level Agreement (SLA)
options.D: Non-disclosure agreement

questions.answer_text: Service Level Agreement (SLA)
questions.explanation: The SLA states measurable targets like uptime %, response and resolution times.

questions.question: The main purpose of an SLA is to:

options.A: Define expected service levels, responsibilities and remedies between provider and customer
options.B: Describe the internal design, architecture and source code of the service being provided
options.C: Record the passwords and access rights of users of the service
options.D: Approve changes to the service before they are deployed to production

questions.answer_text: Define expected service levels, responsibilities and remedies between provider and customer
questions.explanation: Clear SLAs avoid disputes and drive service quality.

questions.question: If a cloud provider fails to meet the uptime promised in its SLA, the customer is typically compensated through:

options.A: Automatic contract termination
options.B: Nothing
options.C: Service credits
options.D: Free hardware

questions.answer_text: Service credits
questions.explanation: Service credits are usually a percentage of the monthly fee.

questions.question: During due diligence before selecting a cloud provider, a bank should assess:

options.A: Only the price per GB of storage and per hour of compute, since all providers offer the same security
options.B: Security certifications, financial stability, data location, audit rights and exit support
options.C: Only the number of free trial credits offered to new customers
options.D: Only the provider's brand popularity and marketing material

questions.answer_text: Security certifications, financial stability, data location, audit rights and exit support
questions.explanation: Third-party risk management continues throughout the contract, not just at selection.

questions.question: A SOC 2 Type II report from a cloud provider shows:

options.A: The provider's revenue, profit and financial health for the most recent financial year
options.B: Only the design of the provider's controls at a single point in time, without any testing of how they operate
options.C: That the provider's controls were operating effectively over a period of time, as tested by an independent auditor
options.D: The list of patents and intellectual property owned by the provider in cloud technology

questions.answer_text: That the provider's controls were operating effectively over a period of time, as tested by an independent auditor
questions.explanation: Type I reports on control design at a point in time; Type II tests operating effectiveness over a period.

questions.question: A DDoS attack differs from a simple DoS attack because it:

options.A: Comes from a single powerful computer with a fast connection
options.B: Comes from many distributed compromised systems at the same time
options.C: Targets only the database rather than the web server
options.D: Steals passwords from the server instead of flooding it

questions.answer_text: Comes from many distributed compromised systems at the same time
questions.explanation: Distributed attacks are harder to block because traffic arrives from thousands of sources.

questions.question: DDoS attacks are typically carried out using:

options.A: Malicious insiders logging in from the branch network
options.B: A single high-bandwidth server owned by the attacker
options.C: Stolen digital certificates of the target website
options.D: A botnet of compromised computers and IoT devices

questions.answer_text: A botnet of compromised computers and IoT devices
questions.explanation: Malware such as Trojans is used to recruit machines into the botnet, which the attacker controls via C2 servers.

questions.question: Which of the following is an APPLICATION-layer (Layer 7) DDoS attack?

options.A: TCP SYN flood on the internet banking web server
options.B: UDP flood on random ports
options.C: HTTP GET/POST flood on the login page
options.D: ICMP ping flood on the router

questions.answer_text: HTTP GET/POST flood on the login page
questions.explanation: Layer 7 floods look like real user requests, so WAFs and bot detection are needed.

questions.question: In a Smurf attack, the attacker:

options.A: Sends a large number of TCP SYN packets to the victim without ever completing the three-way handshake
options.B: Sends ICMP echo requests to a broadcast address with the victim's spoofed IP, so many hosts reply to the victim
options.C: Sends specially crafted overlapping IP fragments that crash the victim when it tries to reassemble them
options.D: Sends small spoofed DNS queries to open resolvers so that large responses are returned to the victim

questions.answer_text: Sends ICMP echo requests to a broadcast address with the victim's spoofed IP, so many hosts reply to the victim
questions.explanation: Disabling directed broadcasts on routers prevents Smurf amplification.

questions.question: In a DNS amplification attack:

options.A: The attacker deletes the victim's DNS records so that the website disappears
options.B: The attacker changes records in a resolver's cache to redirect users to a fake site
options.C: The attacker registers a look-alike domain name to host a phishing website
options.D: Small spoofed queries to open DNS resolvers produce large responses sent to the victim

questions.answer_text: Small spoofed queries to open DNS resolvers produce large responses sent to the victim
questions.explanation: Amplification uses the victim's spoofed IP and the size difference between request and response.

questions.question: Which measure is most effective against large volumetric DDoS attacks on internet banking?

options.A: Adding more RAM and CPU to the internet banking web server only
options.B: Increasing the minimum password length for all customer logins
options.C: Upstream DDoS scrubbing services / CDN with anycast absorbing traffic
options.D: Running updated antivirus on all branch and office PCs

questions.answer_text: Upstream DDoS scrubbing services / CDN with anycast absorbing traffic
questions.explanation: Volumetric attacks can saturate the link before traffic reaches the bank's own firewall.

questions.question: Amazon Web Services protects customer applications against DDoS mainly using:

options.A: AWS Lambda functions that automatically restart failed servers
options.B: Amazon RDS read replicas in other regions
options.C: AWS Shield together with CloudFront, Route 53 and AWS WAF
options.D: Amazon S3 Glacier together with AWS Backup

questions.answer_text: AWS Shield together with CloudFront, Route 53 and AWS WAF
questions.explanation: Shield Standard is automatic; Shield Advanced adds detection, response support and cost protection.

questions.question: In a Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attack, the attacker:

options.A: Floods the target server with traffic until it stops responding
options.B: Secretly intercepts and possibly alters communication between two parties
options.C: Guesses the user's password offline using a stolen hash file
options.D: Steals a backup tape from the vault and reads the customer data on it offline

questions.answer_text: Secretly intercepts and possibly alters communication between two parties
questions.explanation: Both parties believe they are talking directly to each other.

questions.question: Which is the BEST protection against MITM attacks on internet banking sessions?

options.A: TLS with proper certificate validation (plus HSTS)
options.B: Changing the internet banking URL every month
options.C: Using longer usernames together with security questions
options.D: Disabling the browser cache and cookies

questions.answer_text: TLS with proper certificate validation (plus HSTS)
questions.explanation: If certificate warnings are ignored, MITM becomes possible, so users must be educated too.

questions.question: ARP spoofing (ARP poisoning) works by:

options.A: Changing records on the DNS server so that the bank's domain resolves to the attacker's IP
options.B: Forging the sender address in emails so that they appear to come from the bank
options.C: Capturing the Wi-Fi handshake and cracking the network password offline
options.D: Sending fake ARP replies so that victims map the gateway's IP to the attacker's MAC address

questions.answer_text: Sending fake ARP replies so that victims map the gateway's IP to the attacker's MAC address
questions.explanation: Traffic then flows through the attacker, enabling sniffing or MITM on the LAN.

questions.question: Which switch feature helps prevent ARP spoofing on a LAN?

options.A: Spanning Tree Protocol (STP)
options.B: Link aggregation (LACP)
options.C: Port mirroring (SPAN)
options.D: Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI)

questions.answer_text: Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI)
questions.explanation: DAI validates ARP packets against the DHCP snooping binding table.

questions.question: An attacker inserts packets with a forged source IP address to hide their identity or impersonate another host. This is:

options.A: IP spoofing
options.B: Port scanning
options.C: Packet sniffing
options.D: Phishing

questions.answer_text: IP spoofing
questions.explanation: Ingress/egress filtering blocks packets with impossible source addresses.

questions.question: DNS cache poisoning redirects users to a fake website by:

options.A: Flooding the bank's web server with fake requests
options.B: Registering a domain name that looks like the bank's
options.C: Breaking the TLS encryption used by the bank website
options.D: Inserting false records into a DNS resolver's cache

questions.answer_text: Inserting false records into a DNS resolver's cache
questions.explanation: DNSSEC adds digital signatures to DNS records to prevent forged responses.

questions.question: Which set of email authentication standards helps detect forged (spoofed) sender domains?

options.A: RAID, LVM and SAN
options.B: FTP, SFTP and TFTP
options.C: SPF, DKIM and DMARC
options.D: HTTP, HTML and CSS

questions.answer_text: SPF, DKIM and DMARC
questions.explanation: SPF lists allowed sending servers, DKIM signs mail, DMARC sets policy and reporting.

questions.question: Stealing a valid session cookie/token to take over a logged-in user's session is called:

options.A: Salami attack
options.B: Session hijacking
options.C: Brute force
options.D: Dumpster diving

questions.answer_text: Session hijacking
questions.explanation: HTTPS, HttpOnly/Secure cookies and session timeouts reduce the risk.

questions.question: In a replay attack, the attacker:

options.A: Modifies DNS records so that users are sent to a fake copy of the website
options.B: Captures a valid transmission (e.g. an authentication message) and re-sends it later
options.C: Floods the server with requests until it can no longer respond to genuine users
