options.D: Guesses one-time passwords repeatedly until the correct one is accepted

questions.answer_text: Captures a valid transmission (e.g. an authentication message) and re-sends it later
questions.explanation: Nonces, timestamps and one-time tokens make replayed messages invalid.

questions.question: Packet sniffing means:

options.A: Capturing and inspecting network packets as they travel over the network
options.B: Dropping suspicious packets before they reach the internal network
options.C: Compressing packets so that the network carries more data
options.D: Encrypting packets so that only the intended receiver can read them

questions.answer_text: Capturing and inspecting network packets as they travel over the network
questions.explanation: Tools: Wireshark, tcpdump. Unencrypted protocols expose passwords to sniffers.

questions.question: Sniffing tools are called a 'double-edged sword' because:

options.A: They can both encrypt and decrypt the packets that they capture from the network
options.B: Administrators use them to troubleshoot and monitor, while attackers use them to steal unencrypted data
options.C: They can capture traffic in both directions, inbound as well as outbound, on the same interface
options.D: They work on both Windows and Linux operating systems with the same features

questions.answer_text: Administrators use them to troubleshoot and monitor, while attackers use them to steal unencrypted data
questions.explanation: Using encrypted protocols makes sniffed data useless to attackers.

questions.question: Identifying the open ports and the services running on a target host (e.g. using Nmap) is called:

options.A: Phishing / social engineering
options.B: Salting and key stretching of password hashes
options.C: Port scanning / service enumeration
options.D: Defacement / vandalism

questions.answer_text: Port scanning / service enumeration
questions.explanation: Ethical hackers do this during reconnaissance to understand the attack surface.

questions.question: Passive scanning (passive reconnaissance) means:

options.A: Sending probe packets to every port of the target to see which ones respond
options.B: Exploiting a discovered vulnerability to confirm that it is real
options.C: Gathering information without directly sending probes to the target, e.g. monitoring traffic or using public sources
options.D: Running a full port scan only at night so that it is not noticed by the administrators or by the SOC monitoring team

questions.answer_text: Gathering information without directly sending probes to the target, e.g. monitoring traffic or using public sources
questions.explanation: It is hard to detect because the target sees no unusual traffic.

questions.question: Eavesdropping and traffic analysis are examples of ____ attacks, while modifying data and DoS are ____ attacks.

options.A: Physical; logical
options.B: Internal; external
options.C: Active; passive
options.D: Passive; active

questions.answer_text: Passive; active
questions.explanation: Passive attacks threaten confidentiality and are hard to detect; encryption is the main defence.

questions.question: A brute-force attack is one in which the attacker:

options.A: Floods the login server with requests so that real users cannot log in to their accounts
options.B: Steals the user's laptop and reads the passwords saved in the browser
options.C: Sends a fake email that tricks the user into revealing the password
options.D: Tries every possible password or key combination until the correct one is found

questions.answer_text: Tries every possible password or key combination until the correct one is found
questions.explanation: Long passwords, account lockout and MFA defeat brute force.

questions.question: A Trojan horse is malware that:

options.A: Displays unwanted advertisements but causes no other harm
options.B: Encrypts the user's files and demands a ransom payment
options.C: Replicates itself across networks to other computers without any user action
options.D: Appears to be legitimate software but performs hidden malicious actions

questions.answer_text: Appears to be legitimate software but performs hidden malicious actions
questions.explanation: Unlike worms, Trojans do not self-replicate; they rely on users running them.

questions.question: Malware that self-replicates and spreads across networks without any user action is a:

options.A: Worm
options.B: Adware
options.C: Trojan horse
options.D: Logic bomb

questions.answer_text: Worm
questions.explanation: Worms like WannaCry exploited unpatched network services to spread.

questions.question: A rootkit is dangerous mainly because it:

options.A: Slows down the browser by running hidden cryptocurrency mining scripts in the background
options.B: Gives privileged access while hiding its presence from the OS and security tools
options.C: Deletes itself after one use so that it leaves no trace at all
options.D: Shows unwanted pop-up advertisements in the user's web browser

questions.answer_text: Gives privileged access while hiding its presence from the OS and security tools
questions.explanation: Rootkits may require OS reinstallation to remove.

questions.question: Spyware is malware that:

options.A: Secretly collects information about the user's activities and sends it to an attacker
options.B: Spreads automatically to other computers by exploiting network services
options.C: Encrypts the user's files and then demands payment in cryptocurrency for the decryption key
options.D: Floods the network with traffic until other systems stop responding

questions.answer_text: Secretly collects information about the user's activities and sends it to an attacker
questions.explanation: Keyloggers are a common type of spyware used to steal banking credentials.

questions.question: Ransomware makes data files unusable by:

options.A: Deleting the operating system so that the computer cannot boot
options.B: Compressing them into a password-protected archive file
options.C: Moving them to the recycle bin and emptying it after a delay
options.D: Encrypting them and demanding payment for the decryption key

questions.answer_text: Encrypting them and demanding payment for the decryption key
questions.explanation: Offline/immutable backups and patching are the key defences.

questions.question: Malicious code inserted into a program that activates only when a specific condition occurs (e.g. a date or an employee's removal from payroll) is a:

options.A: Worm
options.B: Spyware
options.C: Adware
options.D: Logic bomb

questions.answer_text: Logic bomb
questions.explanation: Often planted by insiders, so code reviews and change control matter.

questions.question: A polymorphic virus is hard to detect because it:

options.A: Always encrypts itself with AES-256, so antivirus software can never read or analyse its code
options.B: Changes its code/signature each time it infects, evading signature-based antivirus
options.C: Carries a valid digital certificate, so antivirus treats it as trusted
options.D: Infects only the BIOS, which antivirus software is not allowed to scan

questions.answer_text: Changes its code/signature each time it infects, evading signature-based antivirus
questions.explanation: Behaviour-based detection (EDR) helps catch such malware.

questions.question: Malware that installs a hidden way to bypass normal authentication for later remote access is called a:

options.A: Honeypot
options.B: Firewall
options.C: Backdoor
options.D: Sandbox

questions.answer_text: Backdoor
questions.explanation: Remote Access Trojans (RATs) typically open backdoors.

questions.question: Siphoning very small amounts of money from many accounts into another account so that each loss goes unnoticed is called a:

options.A: Teardrop attack
options.B: Smurf attack
options.C: Salami attack
options.D: Watering hole attack

questions.answer_text: Salami attack
questions.explanation: Reconciliation and anomaly monitoring help detect it.

questions.question: Phishing carried out over a voice phone call is called ____, and over SMS is called ____.

options.A: Vishing; smishing
options.B: Whaling; pharming
options.C: Spoofing; spamming
options.D: Smishing; vishing

questions.answer_text: Vishing; smishing
questions.explanation: Spear phishing targets specific people; whaling targets senior executives.

questions.question: Unsolicited bulk email is called:

options.A: Spam
options.B: Phishing
options.C: Spoofing
options.D: Vishing

questions.answer_text: Spam
questions.explanation: Spam filters and content filters block such mail; phishing is spam with malicious intent.

questions.question: An Advanced Persistent Threat (APT) is best described as:

options.A: A one-time, high-volume DDoS attack that stops as soon as the target goes offline
options.B: A random virus that spreads through USB drives and infects any computer that it reaches in the network
options.C: A prolonged, targeted and stealthy attack, often by a well-resourced group, aiming to stay undetected
options.D: An automated password-guessing attack against many unrelated websites at once

questions.answer_text: A prolonged, targeted and stealthy attack, often by a well-resourced group, aiming to stay undetected
questions.explanation: APTs move laterally over months; detection needs strong monitoring and threat hunting.

questions.question: The main difference between an IDS and an IPS is:

options.A: IDS detects and alerts; IPS sits inline and can block malicious traffic
options.B: IPS detects and alerts; IDS sits inline and can block malicious traffic
options.C: IDS encrypts suspicious traffic; IPS decrypts it for inspection
options.D: IDS is always a hardware appliance; IPS is always software on hosts

questions.answer_text: IDS detects and alerts; IPS sits inline and can block malicious traffic
questions.explanation: 'Prevention is better than cure' - an IPS can stop an attack in real time.

questions.question: Signature-based detection is limited because it:

options.A: Generates far too many alerts for normal, legitimate user behaviour
options.B: Does not need any updates once it has been installed
options.C: Cannot detect new (zero-day) attacks that have no known signature
options.D: Cannot detect any attack that uses a well-known exploit

questions.answer_text: Cannot detect new (zero-day) attacks that have no known signature
questions.explanation: Anomaly-based detection can catch unknown attacks but produces more false positives.

questions.question: Anomaly-based intrusion detection works by:

options.A: Scanning files on disk for known virus patterns every night
options.B: Building a baseline of normal behaviour and alerting on significant deviations
options.C: Blocking all traffic that does not come from a trusted IP address
options.D: Matching traffic only against a database of known attack signatures from the vendor

questions.answer_text: Building a baseline of normal behaviour and alerting on significant deviations
questions.explanation: Tuning the baseline reduces false positives.

questions.question: A HIDS (Host-based IDS) differs from a NIDS (Network-based IDS) because a HIDS:

options.A: Monitors activity, logs and file integrity on an individual host
options.B: Is installed only on routers at the internet perimeter
options.C: Monitors all traffic flowing on an entire network segment through a span port
options.D: Blocks traffic inline before it reaches any host

questions.answer_text: Monitors activity, logs and file integrity on an individual host
questions.explanation: NIDS sees network traffic; HIDS sees what happens on the server, including encrypted traffic after decryption.

questions.question: In intrusion detection, a 'false positive' is:

options.A: A real attack that the IDS failed to detect or report
options.B: A real attack that was correctly detected
options.C: Legitimate activity wrongly flagged as an attack
options.D: An alert generated by a disabled sensor

questions.answer_text: Legitimate activity wrongly flagged as an attack
questions.explanation: A false negative (missed attack) is generally more dangerous.

questions.question: A honeypot is:

options.A: A decoy system designed to attract attackers so their methods can be studied and they are diverted
options.B: A hardened production server that hosts the bank's most sensitive databases
options.C: A filter that blocks known malicious IP addresses at the internet gateway
options.D: A system that collects and correlates logs from all the servers in the data centre to raise alerts

questions.answer_text: A decoy system designed to attract attackers so their methods can be studied and they are diverted
questions.explanation: Any interaction with a honeypot is suspicious, giving high-quality alerts.

questions.question: A SIEM (Security Information and Event Management) system:

options.A: Collects and correlates logs from many sources to detect and alert on security incidents
options.B: Encrypts hard disks on servers and laptops to protect data at rest
options.C: Backs up security logs to tape for long-term retention only
options.D: Inspects and blocks malicious traffic inline at the network perimeter before it reaches servers

questions.answer_text: Collects and correlates logs from many sources to detect and alert on security incidents
questions.explanation: SIEM is the core tool of a Security Operations Centre (SOC).

questions.question: How does SOAR differ from SIEM?

options.A: SOAR and SIEM are two names for the same product used by different vendors
options.B: SIEM sits inline and blocks malicious traffic; SOAR only generates compliance reports
options.C: SOAR mainly collects, stores and correlates logs; SIEM automates and orchestrates incident response using playbooks
options.D: SOAR automates and orchestrates incident response using playbooks; SIEM mainly collects, correlates and alerts

questions.answer_text: SOAR automates and orchestrates incident response using playbooks; SIEM mainly collects, correlates and alerts
questions.explanation: SOAR = Security Orchestration, Automation and Response.

questions.question: The main security benefit of network segmentation is that it:

options.A: Makes every system reachable from every other system
options.B: Limits an attacker's lateral movement and contains the impact of a breach
options.C: Increases the internet bandwidth available to each department and branch
options.D: Removes the need for firewalls between different zones

questions.answer_text: Limits an attacker's lateral movement and contains the impact of a breach
questions.explanation: E.g. CBS servers, ATM network, user LAN and DMZ in separate zones.

questions.question: Implementing VLANs instead of one flat LAN is advantageous because VLANs:

options.A: Increase broadcast traffic so that devices can discover each other more quickly
options.B: Need separate physical switches for each department, which isolates their traffic completely from others
options.C: Logically separate traffic into different broadcast domains, improving security and performance
options.D: Remove the need for IP addresses because devices communicate using VLAN IDs

questions.answer_text: Logically separate traffic into different broadcast domains, improving security and performance
questions.explanation: Inter-VLAN traffic must pass through a router/firewall where rules can be applied.

questions.question: A 'VLAN hopping' attack allows an attacker to:

options.A: Encrypt traffic in the VLAN so that the network team cannot monitor it
options.B: Send traffic into a VLAN they are not assigned to, e.g. by switch spoofing or double tagging
options.C: Increase the bandwidth of their own VLAN by taking unused capacity away from other VLANs on the switch
options.D: Delete VLANs from the switch remotely by sending a large number of ping packets

questions.answer_text: Send traffic into a VLAN they are not assigned to, e.g. by switch spoofing or double tagging
questions.explanation: Disabling auto-trunking (DTP) and not using the native VLAN for users prevent it.

questions.question: Micro-segmentation differs from traditional segmentation because it:

options.A: Applies fine-grained security policies down to individual workloads or applications
options.B: Uses only physical firewalls placed between different office buildings
options.C: Groups all servers into one large zone with a single shared policy
options.D: Divides the network only at the internet perimeter into an inside zone and an outside zone

questions.answer_text: Applies fine-grained security policies down to individual workloads or applications
questions.explanation: Common in virtualized/cloud data centres and a key part of Zero Trust.

questions.question: Zero Trust security follows the principle:

options.A: Trust but verify
options.B: Never trust, always verify
options.C: Verify once, trust forever
options.D: Trust everything inside the firewall

questions.answer_text: Never trust, always verify
questions.explanation: No user or device is trusted automatically because of its network location.

questions.question: Which set lists the core principles of Zero Trust?

options.A: Perimeter firewall only, open internal network
options.B: Trust internal users, block external users, log nothing
options.C: Single sign-on only, no MFA, flat network
options.D: Verify explicitly, use least-privilege access, assume breach

questions.answer_text: Verify explicitly, use least-privilege access, assume breach
questions.explanation: Every access request is authenticated, authorised and continuously evaluated.

questions.question: NIST Special Publication 800-207 describes:

options.A: Business continuity planning
options.B: Zero Trust Architecture
options.C: Password guidelines only
options.D: Cloud computing definition

questions.answer_text: Zero Trust Architecture
questions.explanation: It defines components such as the Policy Decision Point and Policy Enforcement Point.

questions.question: Device compliance and endpoint security posture checks before allowing network access are enforced using:

options.A: NAC (Network Access Control)
options.B: DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration)
options.C: NTP (Network Time Protocol)
options.D: DNS (Domain Name System)

questions.answer_text: NAC (Network Access Control)
questions.explanation: NAC checks things like antivirus status and patches, and can quarantine non-compliant devices.

questions.question: A laptop without the latest antivirus updates is connected to the bank LAN and is automatically placed in a restricted remediation VLAN. This is done by:

options.A: A forward proxy server
options.B: A RAID controller
options.C: Network Access Control (NAC)
options.D: A load balancer

questions.answer_text: Network Access Control (NAC)
questions.explanation: Once updated and compliant, the device is moved to the normal network.

questions.question: A VPN secures remote access by:

options.A: Hiding the user's screen from people sitting nearby in public places
options.B: Increasing the speed of the user's internet connection through compression and local caching of data
options.C: Removing the need for the user to log in with a password or OTP
options.D: Creating an encrypted tunnel over a public network between the user and the organisation

questions.answer_text: Creating an encrypted tunnel over a public network between the user and the organisation
questions.explanation: MFA should be required for VPN logins.

questions.question: In IPsec, which protocol provides encryption (confidentiality) of the payload?

options.A: ESP (Encapsulating Security Payload)
options.B: AH (Authentication Header)
options.C: IKE (Internet Key Exchange)
options.D: GRE (Generic Routing Encapsulation)

questions.answer_text: ESP (Encapsulating Security Payload)
questions.explanation: AH provides integrity and authentication but no encryption; IKE negotiates keys.

questions.question: Which wireless security protocol is currently the strongest?

options.A: WPA2-TKIP
options.B: WPA
options.C: WEP
options.D: WPA3

questions.answer_text: WPA3
questions.explanation: WEP is completely broken; WPA2-AES is acceptable; WPA3 is the newest.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a network security best practice?

options.A: Sending all network device logs to a central SIEM for correlation
options.B: Disabling unused switch ports
options.C: Leaving SNMP community string as 'public' for easy monitoring
options.D: Using SSH instead of Telnet for device management

questions.answer_text: Leaving SNMP community string as 'public' for easy monitoring
questions.explanation: Default SNMP community strings let attackers read (or change) device configuration; use SNMPv3.

questions.question: Data Loss Prevention (DLP) is vital for a bank because it:

options.A: Replaces antivirus software by scanning all files for known malware signatures
options.B: Backs up sensitive data automatically to a secure offsite location every day
options.C: Speeds up the network by compressing large email attachments and file transfers sent to external parties
options.D: Detects and blocks sensitive data like account or card numbers from leaving through email, USB or web

questions.answer_text: Detects and blocks sensitive data like account or card numbers from leaving through email, USB or web
questions.explanation: DLP enforces data classification policies on endpoints, network and cloud.

questions.question: Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) improves on traditional antivirus by:

options.A: Removing the need to patch endpoints because attacks are blocked at the network
options.B: Continuously monitoring endpoint behaviour, detecting suspicious activity and enabling investigation and isolation
options.C: Scanning files for known virus signatures once a week during off-peak hours, without providing any real-time protection
options.D: Blocking all internet access from endpoints so that no malware can be downloaded

questions.answer_text: Continuously monitoring endpoint behaviour, detecting suspicious activity and enabling investigation and isolation
questions.explanation: EDR can isolate an infected machine remotely to stop ransomware spread.

questions.question: A firewall is primarily used to:

options.A: Allow or block network traffic between zones based on defined security rules
options.B: Store backups of servers and restore them after a failure
options.C: Speed up internet connections by caching frequently used web content for all users
options.D: Assign IP addresses automatically to hosts on the network

questions.answer_text: Allow or block network traffic between zones based on defined security rules
questions.explanation: It enforces the organisation's network access policy at zone boundaries.

questions.question: A packet-filtering firewall makes decisions based on:

options.A: The full content of web pages and files, including scanning attachments for malware and data leakage patterns
options.B: The state of each TCP session, allowing return traffic only for established connections
options.C: Packet header information such as source/destination IP, port and protocol, checking each packet independently
options.D: The identity of the logged-in user obtained from Active Directory for every connection

questions.answer_text: Packet header information such as source/destination IP, port and protocol, checking each packet independently
questions.explanation: Simple packet filters are stateless and work at Layers 3 and 4.

questions.question: Which type of firewall keeps track of the state of network connections and allows return traffic only for established sessions?

options.A: Personal firewall without rules
options.B: Circuit-level gateway
options.C: Stateful inspection firewall
options.D: Stateless packet filter

questions.answer_text: Stateful inspection firewall
questions.explanation: It maintains a state table of active connections.

questions.question: A stateless packet filter that must allow web browsing from inside to the internet requires:

options.A: No rules at all, because web traffic is always allowed by default
options.B: Only one outbound rule, since return traffic is allowed automatically
options.C: Only DNS rules, since browsing depends mainly on name resolution
options.D: Explicit rules for both the outgoing requests and the returning responses

questions.answer_text: Explicit rules for both the outgoing requests and the returning responses
questions.explanation: Stateful firewalls automatically allow the return traffic of permitted connections.

questions.question: An application-level gateway (proxy firewall):

options.A: Works only at the physical layer, blocking traffic by disconnecting the network cable
options.B: Works at Layer 7, terminating the client connection and inspecting application content before forwarding
options.C: Forwards packets without inspecting their content, checking only the source and destination IP addresses
options.D: Filters traffic only on MAC addresses, without looking at IP addresses or content

questions.answer_text: Works at Layer 7, terminating the client connection and inspecting application content before forwarding
questions.explanation: It offers deep inspection but adds latency.

questions.question: A circuit-level gateway (e.g. SOCKS) works mainly by:

options.A: Inspecting HTTP request content for SQL injection and cross-site scripting patterns
options.B: Validating the TCP session setup at the session layer without inspecting packet contents
options.C: Filtering frames based on the source and destination MAC addresses only
options.D: Encrypting all traffic between the client and the server using TLS

questions.answer_text: Validating the TCP session setup at the session layer without inspecting packet contents
questions.explanation: Once the session is valid, packets flow without further content checks.

questions.question: A Next-Generation Firewall (NGFW) adds which capabilities to traditional stateful inspection?

options.A: Application awareness, integrated IPS, user identity and TLS inspection
options.B: Faster packet routing using dynamic routing protocols such as OSPF
options.C: Physical access control for the data centre doors and racks
options.D: Network address translation and DHCP services for internal hosts

questions.answer_text: Application awareness, integrated IPS, user identity and TLS inspection
questions.explanation: NGFWs can allow or block specific applications regardless of port.

questions.question: A Web Application Firewall (WAF) mainly protects against:

options.A: ARP spoofing and MAC flooding attacks carried out by insiders on the internal LAN switches
options.B: Power failures and voltage fluctuations in the data centre
options.C: Application-layer attacks on web apps like SQL injection and cross-site scripting
options.D: Disk crashes and data corruption on web servers

questions.answer_text: Application-layer attacks on web apps like SQL injection and cross-site scripting
questions.explanation: It inspects HTTP/HTTPS requests and responses, often using OWASP rule sets.

questions.question: iptables/firewalld on Linux and Windows Defender Firewall are examples of:

options.A: Network hardware firewalls
options.B: Web application firewalls
options.C: Cloud access brokers
options.D: Host-based firewalls

questions.answer_text: Host-based firewalls
questions.explanation: Host firewalls add a layer of protection on each server (defense in depth).

questions.question: In Linux iptables, which chain handles packets destined for the local server itself?

options.A: FORWARD
options.B: PREROUTING
options.C: OUTPUT
options.D: INPUT

questions.answer_text: INPUT
questions.explanation: OUTPUT handles locally generated packets; FORWARD handles packets routed through the host.

questions.question: Unified Threat Management (UTM) appliances are popular for small offices because they:

options.A: Combine firewall, VPN, IPS, antivirus and web filtering in one device
options.B: Need no configuration or updates once they are installed
options.C: Provide large storage capacity for branch backups
options.D: Replace all servers in the branch with a single appliance that runs every application

questions.answer_text: Combine firewall, VPN, IPS, antivirus and web filtering in one device
questions.explanation: Consolidation reduces cost and administration for small sites.

questions.question: Which of the following can a perimeter firewall alone NOT protect against?

options.A: An employee clicking a phishing link and entering credentials on a fake site
options.B: Access from the internet to services that are not published
options.C: Unsolicited inbound connections from the internet to ports that are closed on the firewall
options.D: Traffic coming from IP addresses that are on the block list

questions.answer_text: An employee clicking a phishing link and entering credentials on a fake site
questions.explanation: Firewalls must be complemented by awareness, email security, MFA and endpoint controls.

questions.question: The 'implicit deny' principle in firewall rule sets means:

options.A: The first rule always denies
options.B: All traffic is allowed unless it is explicitly denied by a rule
options.C: Any traffic not explicitly permitted by a rule is denied
options.D: Only ICMP is denied

questions.answer_text: Any traffic not explicitly permitted by a rule is denied
questions.explanation: Default-deny is the secure baseline; only required flows are opened.

questions.question: Firewall and router ACL rules are generally processed:

options.A: Bottom-up, last match wins
options.B: Randomly
options.C: Only the most specific rule regardless of order
options.D: Top-down, and the first matching rule is applied

questions.answer_text: Top-down, and the first matching rule is applied
questions.explanation: Rule order matters; specific rules must be placed above general ones.

questions.question: A firewall has Rule 1: 'Permit any to any' and Rule 2: 'Deny source 10.1.1.5 to any'. What happens to traffic from 10.1.1.5?

options.A: It is denied, because Rule 2 is more specific
options.B: It is logged by Rule 2 but forwarded by Rule 1
options.C: It is permitted, because Rule 1 matches first
options.D: It is dropped by the implicit deny at the end

questions.answer_text: It is permitted, because Rule 1 matches first
questions.explanation: Rule 2 is 'shadowed' and never takes effect; it should be placed above Rule 1.

questions.question: A firewall rule that can never be matched because an earlier, broader rule already covers all its traffic is called a:

options.A: Shadowed rule
options.B: Implicit rule
options.C: Egress rule
options.D: Stateful rule

questions.answer_text: Shadowed rule
questions.explanation: Periodic rule-base reviews find shadowed, redundant and unused rules.

questions.question: In Cisco IOS, a standard IP ACL (numbers 1-99) filters traffic based on:

options.A: MAC address only
options.B: Source and destination IP, protocol and ports
options.C: Source IP address only
options.D: URL only

questions.answer_text: Source IP address only
questions.explanation: Extended ACLs (100-199) can match source, destination, protocol and port numbers.

questions.question: As a general guideline, where should standard and extended ACLs be placed?

options.A: Both always on the internet router
options.B: Standard ACLs close to the destination; extended ACLs close to the source
options.C: Both only on the core switch
options.D: Standard ACLs close to the source; extended close to the destination

questions.answer_text: Standard ACLs close to the destination; extended ACLs close to the source
questions.explanation: Standard ACLs only know the source, so placing them near the source could block too much.

questions.question: In a Cisco ACL, the wildcard mask 0.0.0.255 used with 192.168.5.0 matches:

options.A: All addresses from 192.168.5.0 to 192.168.5.255
options.B: Only the single host address 192.168.5.255
options.C: All addresses from 192.168.0.0 to 192.168.255.255
options.D: Only the network address 192.168.5.0

questions.answer_text: All addresses from 192.168.5.0 to 192.168.5.255
questions.explanation: In wildcard masks, 0 = must match, 255 = any value; it is the inverse of the subnet mask.

questions.question: Branch users (10.10.0.0/16) need to access the CBS application server 172.16.5.10 over HTTPS only. Which rule best follows least privilege?

options.A: Permit IP from 10.10.0.0/16 to 172.16.0.0/12 on all ports
options.B: Permit TCP from 10.10.0.0/16 to 172.16.5.10 port 443
options.C: Permit TCP from any to 172.16.5.10 any port
options.D: Permit any from 10.10.0.0/16 to any

questions.answer_text: Permit TCP from 10.10.0.0/16 to 172.16.5.10 port 443
questions.explanation: Restrict source, destination and service to exactly what is needed.

questions.question: An 'any-any-allow' rule in a firewall is risky because it:

options.A: Slows down DNS resolution because every query has to be inspected twice
options.B: Permits all traffic between all sources and destinations, defeating the purpose of the firewall
options.C: Disables firewall logging automatically for all the traffic it matches
options.D: Blocks all traffic between all zones, causing an immediate outage of every application in the bank

questions.answer_text: Permits all traffic between all sources and destinations, defeating the purpose of the firewall
questions.explanation: Such rules are top audit findings and should be removed or narrowed.

questions.question: Ingress filtering at the internet router means:

options.A: Blocking all outgoing email from internal users to external domains in order to prevent the leakage of confidential customer data to outsiders
options.B: Allowing every incoming packet from the internet so that no legitimate customer traffic is ever dropped
options.C: Blocking incoming packets with invalid or spoofed source addresses, such as private or internal IP ranges arriving from the internet
options.D: Filtering only the wireless traffic that enters the network through guest Wi-Fi access points

questions.answer_text: Blocking incoming packets with invalid or spoofed source addresses, such as private or internal IP ranges arriving from the internet
questions.explanation: Packets claiming to come from inside should never arrive on the external interface.

questions.question: Egress filtering helps an organisation mainly by:

options.A: Blocking all inbound traffic from the internet, which stops every type of external attack from reaching the bank's servers
options.B: Assigning public IP addresses to internal hosts so that they can be reached from the internet
options.C: Increasing upload speed for users by prioritising outbound traffic over inbound traffic
options.D: Restricting outbound traffic, which limits data exfiltration and malware communicating with command-and-control servers

questions.answer_text: Restricting outbound traffic, which limits data exfiltration and malware communicating with command-and-control servers
questions.explanation: Servers should only reach the specific external destinations they need.

questions.question: Network Address Translation (NAT) is mainly used to:

options.A: Translate private internal IP addresses to public IP addresses for internet communication
options.B: Translate domain names into IP addresses for users who are browsing websites on the internet
options.C: Translate IP addresses into MAC addresses for delivery on the local network
options.D: Encrypt traffic leaving the internal network for the internet

questions.answer_text: Translate private internal IP addresses to public IP addresses for internet communication
questions.explanation: NAT conserves public IPv4 addresses and hides internal addressing.

questions.question: Which NAT type maps one private IP permanently to one public IP, commonly used to publish an internal server?

options.A: Dynamic NAT
options.B: Twice NAT only
options.C: Static NAT
options.D: PAT (NAT overload)

questions.answer_text: Static NAT
questions.explanation: Inbound connections to that public IP always reach the same internal host.

questions.question: PAT (Port Address Translation / NAT overload) allows:

options.A: Only one internal host at a time to access the internet
options.B: NAT to work without any router or firewall in the path
options.C: Each internal host to get its own dedicated public IP address from the ISP's pool
options.D: Many internal hosts to share a single public IP, distinguished by port numbers

questions.answer_text: Many internal hosts to share a single public IP, distinguished by port numbers
questions.explanation: This is how most offices and homes connect to the internet.

questions.question: Dynamic NAT differs from static NAT in that it:

options.A: Uses a single public IP shared by all hosts through ports
options.B: Assigns public addresses from a pool to internal hosts as needed
options.C: Translates addresses without using any public IPs at all
options.D: Uses a fixed one-to-one mapping between private and public IPs

questions.answer_text: Assigns public addresses from a pool to internal hosts as needed
questions.explanation: Mappings are temporary and released when not in use.

questions.question: From a security point of view, a side benefit of NAT is that it:

options.A: Prevents phishing emails from reaching internal users
options.B: Encrypts all traffic between internal hosts and the internet
options.C: Replaces the firewall completely for all internet-facing traffic of the bank
options.D: Hides internal IP addresses and network structure from external parties

questions.answer_text: Hides internal IP addresses and network structure from external parties
questions.explanation: NAT is not a security control by itself; firewall rules are still required.

questions.question: Which of the following is a known problem caused by NAT?

options.A: It prevents the use of TCP, so only UDP traffic can pass through NAT
options.B: It makes IPv4 addresses longer, so that older network devices can no longer process them
options.C: It breaks end-to-end addressing and can interfere with protocols like IPsec AH
options.D: It disables DNS resolution for hosts that sit behind the NAT device

questions.answer_text: It breaks end-to-end addressing and can interfere with protocols like IPsec AH
questions.explanation: AH protects the IP header, which NAT modifies; NAT-Traversal with ESP is used instead.

questions.question: A DMZ (Demilitarized Zone) in network design is:

options.A: A wireless guest network provided to visitors in branches and offices
options.B: The most protected internal network segment, which hosts the core banking database servers and the payment HSMs
options.C: An area of the data centre where no network cabling is allowed, for physical security
options.D: A separate network segment that hosts public-facing servers between the internet and the internal network

questions.answer_text: A separate network segment that hosts public-facing servers between the internet and the internal network
questions.explanation: If a DMZ server is compromised, the internal network is still protected by the firewall.

questions.question: Which of the following should NOT be placed in the DMZ?

options.A: Public internet banking web server
options.B: Core banking database server
options.C: Outbound mail relay server
options.D: Reverse proxy for internet banking

questions.answer_text: Core banking database server
questions.explanation: Sensitive databases belong in the most protected internal zone, reachable only from approved app servers.

questions.question: A 'three-legged' firewall design means:

options.A: A single firewall managed jointly by three administrators from different teams
options.B: Three separate DMZ networks created on one switch using VLANs
options.C: Three separate firewalls placed in series between the internet and the internal network
options.D: One firewall with three interfaces connecting the internet, the DMZ and the internal network

questions.answer_text: One firewall with three interfaces connecting the internet, the DMZ and the internal network
questions.explanation: It is cheaper; a dual-firewall (screened subnet) design gives stronger separation.

questions.question: In a dual-firewall DMZ design, using firewalls from two different vendors is recommended because:

options.A: Two different vendors together always cost less than two from the same vendor
options.B: Regulators require two vendors for every firewall pair in the data centre
options.C: Using two vendors removes the need to write separate rules for each layer
options.D: A vulnerability in one vendor's product is less likely to compromise both layers

questions.answer_text: A vulnerability in one vendor's product is less likely to compromise both layers
questions.explanation: This applies the defense-in-depth principle to the perimeter.

questions.question: Which traffic flow is generally acceptable in a standard DMZ design?

options.A: Internet to DMZ web server on port 443; DMZ web server to internal app server on a specific port only
options.B: Internet directly to the internal database server on port 1521, for faster response to customer queries
options.C: Internet to DMZ on all ports, and DMZ to internal network on all ports for simplicity
options.D: DMZ web server to any internal server on any port, since the DMZ is already protected

questions.answer_text: Internet to DMZ web server on port 443; DMZ web server to internal app server on a specific port only
questions.explanation: Every flow is narrowly defined; direct internet-to-internal access is denied.

questions.question: A bastion host is:

options.A: A normal user desktop used by administrators to browse the internet
options.B: A test server with no operating system used for staging new applications
options.C: A specially hardened system exposed to the internet, often in the DMZ, designed to withstand attack
options.D: A backup server kept inside the vault with no network connection at all, used for disaster recovery

questions.answer_text: A specially hardened system exposed to the internet, often in the DMZ, designed to withstand attack
questions.explanation: Jump servers used to administer internal systems are also hardened bastion hosts.

questions.question: In firewall zoning, the default principle is that traffic from a LOWER-trust zone to a HIGHER-trust zone is:

options.A: Denied unless specifically permitted
options.B: Always permitted by default
options.C: Permitted only outside business hours
options.D: Permitted if the traffic is encrypted

questions.answer_text: Denied unless specifically permitted
questions.explanation: Zones (internet, DMZ, internal, CBS, management) are assigned trust levels.

questions.question: For effective firewall logging and monitoring, logs should be:

options.A: Kept only on the firewall's local disk and overwritten every day, to save storage space on the firewall appliance in the data centre
options.B: Sent to a central SIEM with accurate NTP time, reviewed for denied and critical allowed traffic, and retained as per policy
options.C: Disabled completely during business hours so that the firewall's performance is not affected by logging
options.D: Printed every week and filed in the data centre so that auditors can review them during inspections

questions.answer_text: Sent to a central SIEM with accurate NTP time, reviewed for denied and critical allowed traffic, and retained as per policy
questions.explanation: Correlating firewall logs with other sources helps detect attacks.

questions.question: Periodic firewall rule-base review is done mainly to:

options.A: Remove unused, redundant, shadowed or overly permissive rules
options.B: Add more rules so that every application has its own rule
options.C: Reset the administrator passwords of the firewall
options.D: Decide whether the firewall vendor should be changed

questions.answer_text: Remove unused, redundant, shadowed or overly permissive rules
questions.explanation: Rule bloat increases risk and makes audits difficult.

questions.question: New rules or changes to production firewall rules should be implemented:

options.A: Only by the firewall vendor's support team, without involving the bank's staff
options.B: Directly by any administrator as soon as a user requests it over the phone
options.C: Quietly without logging, so that attackers do not learn about the new rules
options.D: Through the formal change management process with documented business justification

questions.answer_text: Through the formal change management process with documented business justification
questions.explanation: Every rule should be traceable to an approved request and an owner.

questions.question: Firewalls deployed in an active-passive high-availability pair need state synchronisation so that:

options.A: Old logs are deleted from both firewalls so that storage is not exhausted
options.B: The passive firewall can also be used for general internet browsing by staff
options.C: Existing sessions continue without dropping if the active firewall fails over
options.D: Both firewalls block all traffic until an administrator confirms the failover

questions.answer_text: Existing sessions continue without dropping if the active firewall fails over
questions.explanation: Without state sync, all established connections would reset at failover.

questions.question: Enabling TLS/SSL inspection on an NGFW allows detection of threats in encrypted traffic, but requires:

options.A: Disabling HTTPS on all internal and external websites so that all web traffic can be inspected by the firewall in clear text
options.B: Deploying the firewall's CA certificate to clients and handling privacy-sensitive categories (e.g. banking/health) carefully
options.C: Using only HTTP/1.0 for browsing, because newer HTTP versions cannot be decrypted by firewalls
options.D: Removing all existing firewall rules so that decrypted traffic is not blocked accidentally

questions.answer_text: Deploying the firewall's CA certificate to clients and handling privacy-sensitive categories (e.g. banking/health) carefully
questions.explanation: The firewall acts as a trusted MITM, decrypting and re-encrypting traffic.

questions.question: A forward proxy server in an organisation mainly:

options.A: Acts as an intermediary for users' web requests, providing filtering, caching and logging
options.B: Assigns IP addresses and DNS settings to users' computers
options.C: Hosts the bank's public website and handles incoming customer requests from the internet
options.D: Stores database backups and replicates them to the DR site

questions.answer_text: Acts as an intermediary for users' web requests, providing filtering, caching and logging
questions.explanation: It can block malicious or non-business sites and hide internal client IPs.

questions.question: A reverse proxy differs from a forward proxy because it:

options.A: Sits in front of users and handles their outgoing web requests to the internet on their behalf (filtering, caching)
options.B: Sits in front of servers and handles incoming client requests on their behalf (load balancing, TLS termination)
options.C: Cannot be used with HTTPS because it is unable to terminate or forward encrypted connections
options.D: Works only for email traffic, relaying messages between internal and external mail servers

questions.answer_text: Sits in front of servers and handles incoming client requests on their behalf (load balancing, TLS termination)
questions.explanation: Examples: Nginx, HAProxy, F5 in front of web/application servers.

questions.question: Arrange the classic SDLC phases in order: (1) Testing (2) Design (3) Requirement analysis (4) Maintenance (5) Development/Coding (6) Deployment
questions.explanation: Requirements -> Design -> Coding -> Testing -> Deployment -> Maintenance.

questions.question: The cost of fixing a defect generally:

options.A: Decreases the later in the SDLC it is found
options.B: Stays the same in every phase of the SDLC
options.C: Becomes zero once the software is deployed
options.D: Increases the later in the SDLC it is found

questions.answer_text: Increases the later in the SDLC it is found
questions.explanation: A requirement error found in production can cost many times more than one found during analysis.

questions.question: Development and unit testing of individual modules take place in which SDLC phase?

options.A: Feasibility study and planning phase
options.B: Implementation / coding phase
options.C: Maintenance phase
options.D: Requirement analysis phase

questions.answer_text: Implementation / coding phase
questions.explanation: Developers write code and test their own units before integration.

questions.question: The Waterfall model is most suitable when:

options.A: The project is highly experimental
options.B: Requirements change every week
options.C: The customer wants a new working version of the product every two weeks
options.D: Requirements are clear, stable and well documented at the start

questions.answer_text: Requirements are clear, stable and well documented at the start
questions.explanation: Each phase is completed before the next begins, so late changes are costly.

questions.question: A major drawback of the Waterfall model is that:

options.A: It needs almost no documentation, so knowledge is lost when staff leave
options.B: It forces customers to review working software every two weeks
options.C: It has too many short iterations, which makes planning and budgeting difficult
options.D: Working software and defects appear late, and changes are hard to accommodate

questions.answer_text: Working software and defects appear late, and changes are hard to accommodate
questions.explanation: Testing happens only after coding is finished.

questions.question: In the V-model:

options.A: Each development phase has a corresponding testing phase planned in parallel
options.B: There are no separate testing phases; developers test while coding
options.C: Testing is carried out only once, after the software has been deployed
options.D: Coding starts first and requirements are written after the code is ready

questions.answer_text: Each development phase has a corresponding testing phase planned in parallel
questions.explanation: It is also called the Verification and Validation model.

questions.question: In the V-model, user acceptance testing is planned against which phase?

options.A: Low-level/module design
options.B: Deployment
options.C: Requirement analysis
options.D: Coding

questions.answer_text: Requirement analysis
questions.explanation: Unit testing maps to module design, integration testing to architecture design, system testing to system design.

questions.question: The Spiral model, proposed by Barry Boehm, is mainly characterised by:

options.A: A single linear pass through each phase without any iteration
options.B: No formal planning at all, with all the team's effort going directly into coding
options.C: Risk analysis in each iterative cycle, suiting large high-risk projects
options.D: Fixed two-week sprints with daily stand-up meetings

questions.answer_text: Risk analysis in each iterative cycle, suiting large high-risk projects
questions.explanation: Each loop: objectives -> risk analysis -> development/test -> planning the next iteration.

questions.question: The Big Bang model of software development:

options.A: Has a matching testing phase planned for every design phase, as in the V-model
options.B: Puts almost all resources into coding with little planning; suitable only for small or experimental projects
options.C: Is the most structured model, with detailed documentation and formal sign-off at the end of every single phase
options.D: Requires detailed risk analysis in every cycle, making it ideal for large high-risk projects

questions.answer_text: Puts almost all resources into coding with little planning; suitable only for small or experimental projects
questions.explanation: Its main disadvantage is high risk and uncertainty for large or complex projects.

questions.question: Prototyping in software development is mainly done during which stage?

options.A: Requirement gathering and analysis, to clarify user needs
options.B: Deployment, to train users on the live system
options.C: Decommissioning, to archive the old system
options.D: Maintenance, to fix defects reported by users after go-live

questions.answer_text: Requirement gathering and analysis, to clarify user needs
questions.explanation: A quick model helps users see and refine what they want before full development.

questions.question: Rapid Application Development (RAD) emphasises:

options.A: Writing all components from scratch to avoid dependence on libraries
options.B: Quick development through prototyping, reusable components and strong user involvement
options.C: Minimal user involvement until the final acceptance test at the end
options.D: Very long planning phases, with all requirements fully frozen before any design work starts

questions.answer_text: Quick development through prototyping, reusable components and strong user involvement
questions.explanation: It shortens delivery time for projects that can be modularised.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four values of the Agile Manifesto?

options.A: Customer collaboration over contract negotiation
options.B: Individuals and interactions over processes and tools
options.C: Working software over comprehensive documentation
options.D: Following a plan over responding to change

questions.answer_text: Following a plan over responding to change
questions.explanation: The actual value is 'Responding to change over following a plan'.

questions.question: In Scrum, a sprint is:

options.A: A time-boxed iteration, usually 1 to 4 weeks, delivering a usable increment
options.B: A prioritised list of all features required in the product
options.C: The final testing phase carried out after all development is done
options.D: A daily 15-minute meeting in which developers plan the work for the next 24 hours

questions.answer_text: A time-boxed iteration, usually 1 to 4 weeks, delivering a usable increment
questions.explanation: Sprints have fixed length; scope is agreed at sprint planning.

questions.question: In Scrum, who is responsible for prioritising the Product Backlog to maximise value?

options.A: Developers
options.B: Product Owner
options.C: Scrum Master
options.D: Project sponsor

questions.answer_text: Product Owner
questions.explanation: The Product Owner represents business/customer interests.

questions.question: The main role of a Scrum Master is to:

options.A: Own the product backlog and approve the project budget
options.B: Assign tasks to developers and evaluate their performance
options.C: Facilitate Scrum events, coach the team and remove impediments
options.D: Write most of the code and review all pull requests

questions.answer_text: Facilitate Scrum events, coach the team and remove impediments
questions.explanation: The Scrum Master is a servant-leader, not a traditional project manager.

questions.question: The Daily Scrum (stand-up) meeting is time-boxed to:

options.A: 4 hours
options.B: 1 full day
options.C: 15 minutes
options.D: 1 hour

questions.answer_text: 15 minutes
questions.explanation: Developers inspect progress towards the sprint goal and plan the next 24 hours.

questions.question: The Scrum event in which the team reflects on how to improve its own way of working is the:

options.A: Sprint Retrospective
options.B: Sprint Review
options.C: Backlog Refinement
options.D: Sprint Planning

questions.answer_text: Sprint Retrospective
questions.explanation: Sprint Review inspects the product increment with stakeholders; Retrospective inspects the process.

questions.question: Which is the standard format of an Agile user story?

options.A: The system shall <function> within <time> under <load>
options.B: As a <type of user>, I want <goal> so that <benefit>
options.C: Module <ID> must handle <input> and return <output>
options.D: Given <context>, when <action>, then <expected result>

questions.answer_text: As a <type of user>, I want <goal> so that <benefit>
questions.explanation: Example: As a customer, I want to block my debit card in the app so that I can prevent misuse.

questions.question: Kanban mainly focuses on:

options.A: Completing the entire design before any coding starts
options.B: Visualising work on a board and limiting work in progress (WIP)
options.C: Working in fixed-length sprints with a sprint review at the end
options.D: Writing detailed documentation before any coding begins

questions.answer_text: Visualising work on a board and limiting work in progress (WIP)
questions.explanation: Limiting WIP improves flow and exposes bottlenecks.

questions.question: DevOps is best described as:

options.A: A programming language designed for writing deployment scripts that run on both Windows and Linux servers in production and test environments
options.B: A database tool that automatically tunes queries and indexes in production environments
options.C: A network security device that blocks unauthorised deployments to production servers
options.D: A culture and set of practices that unify development and operations to deliver software faster and more reliably through automation

questions.answer_text: A culture and set of practices that unify development and operations to deliver software faster and more reliably through automation
questions.explanation: Key practices: CI/CD, infrastructure as code, monitoring and collaboration.

questions.question: Continuous Integration (CI) means:

options.A: Developers integrate all of their code only once, at the end of the project, just before user acceptance testing
options.B: Operations staff take over development once the application goes live
options.C: Developers merge code into a shared repository frequently, triggering automated builds and tests
options.D: Testers run manual integration tests once a year before the annual release

questions.answer_text: Developers merge code into a shared repository frequently, triggering automated builds and tests
questions.explanation: Frequent integration catches conflicts and bugs early.

questions.question: What is the difference between Continuous Delivery and Continuous Deployment?

options.A: Continuous Deployment only deploys to test environments and never reaches production systems
options.B: Continuous Delivery does not use automated tests, while Continuous Deployment depends on them
options.C: In Continuous Delivery, release to production needs a manual approval; in Continuous Deployment, every passing change goes to production automatically
options.D: In Continuous Deployment, release to production needs a manual approval; in Continuous Delivery, every passing change goes to production automatically

questions.answer_text: In Continuous Delivery, release to production needs a manual approval; in Continuous Deployment, every passing change goes to production automatically
questions.explanation: Regulated environments like banks commonly use Continuous Delivery with a manual gate.

questions.question: Jenkins is widely used as a:

options.A: Relational database
options.B: Hypervisor
options.C: Web browser
options.D: CI/CD automation server

questions.answer_text: CI/CD automation server
questions.explanation: Others include GitLab CI, GitHub Actions and Azure DevOps.

questions.question: 'Shift left' in DevSecOps means:

options.A: Bringing security activities earlier into the development lifecycle
options.B: Delaying security fixes until the next major version
options.C: Testing security only after the application has gone live
options.D: Moving security reviews to the end, just before production release

questions.answer_text: Bringing security activities earlier into the development lifecycle
questions.explanation: Finding vulnerabilities during design and coding is cheaper than after release.

questions.question: Which statement about SAST and DAST is correct?

options.A: SAST tests the running application from outside; DAST analyses source code without running it
options.B: SAST analyses source code without running it; DAST tests the running application from outside
options.C: Both SAST and DAST require full access to the application's source code
options.D: Both SAST and DAST are purely manual techniques performed by penetration testers

questions.answer_text: SAST analyses source code without running it; DAST tests the running application from outside
questions.explanation: SAST is white-box; DAST is black-box. Both are used in a secure SDLC.

questions.question: Software Composition Analysis (SCA) tools are used to:

options.A: Test the running application from outside by sending malicious requests
options.B: Measure the application's response time and throughput under load
options.C: Identify open-source libraries in an application and their known vulnerabilities and licences
options.D: Analyse the application's own source code for insecure coding patterns, without running the application

questions.answer_text: Identify open-source libraries in an application and their known vulnerabilities and licences
questions.explanation: Log4Shell showed how one vulnerable library can affect thousands of applications.

questions.question: 'The system must support 5,000 concurrent users with response time under 2 seconds' is an example of a:

options.A: Test case
options.B: Non-functional requirement
options.C: Functional requirement of the system
options.D: Business rule only

questions.answer_text: Non-functional requirement
questions.explanation: Non-functional requirements cover performance, security, availability, usability, etc.

questions.question: The document that formally captures what the software must do is the:

options.A: Test Summary Report (TSR) of the release cycle
options.B: Software Requirements Specification (SRS)
options.C: High-Level Design document (HLD)
options.D: Release notes for the version

questions.answer_text: Software Requirements Specification (SRS)
questions.explanation: The SRS is the basis for design, testing and acceptance.

questions.question: A Requirement Traceability Matrix (RTM) is used to:

options.A: Track the time each developer spends on each requirement for billing
options.B: Map each requirement to design elements and test cases to ensure full coverage
options.C: List the servers and IP addresses on which each requirement is deployed
options.D: Record the priority and business owner of each requirement only

questions.answer_text: Map each requirement to design elements and test cases to ensure full coverage
questions.explanation: It shows which requirements are tested and helps assess impact of changes.

questions.question: In MoSCoW prioritisation, the letters stand for:

options.A: Minimum, Optimal, Standard, Critical, Worst
options.B: Model, Object, System, Code, Workflow
options.C: Must have, Should have, Could have, Won't have (this time)
options.D: Mandatory, Optional, Secondary, Conditional, Waived (this time)

questions.answer_text: Must have, Should have, Could have, Won't have (this time)
questions.explanation: It helps teams agree scope when time or budget is limited.

questions.question: Good software design aims for:

options.A: High cohesion and high coupling, so modules work closely together
options.B: Low cohesion within modules and high coupling between modules
options.C: One large module containing all functions to avoid any coupling
options.D: High cohesion within modules and low coupling between modules

questions.answer_text: High cohesion within modules and low coupling between modules
questions.explanation: Loosely coupled, cohesive modules are easier to change, test and reuse.

questions.question: High-Level Design (HLD) differs from Low-Level Design (LLD) in that HLD:

options.A: Is written after testing to document what was built; LLD is written before coding
options.B: Covers only database tables and indexes; LLD covers user interface screens
options.C: Describes overall architecture, modules and their interactions; LLD details internal logic of each module
options.D: Contains the actual source code of each module, while LLD describes only the overall architecture of the system

questions.answer_text: Describes overall architecture, modules and their interactions; LLD details internal logic of each module
questions.explanation: LLD is detailed enough for developers to code directly.

questions.question: Which UML diagram shows the interactions between objects in time sequence?

options.A: Class diagram
options.B: Sequence diagram
options.C: Deployment diagram
options.D: Use case diagram

questions.answer_text: Sequence diagram
questions.explanation: Use case = user goals; class = static structure; deployment = physical nodes.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a secure coding practice?

options.A: Validating all user inputs on the server side
options.B: Keeping secrets in a vault instead of in the source code repository
options.C: Encoding output before displaying it in the browser
options.D: Using parameterised queries for database access
options.E: Showing detailed error messages and stack traces to end users

questions.answer_text: Showing detailed error messages and stack traces to end users
questions.explanation: Detailed errors reveal internal structure useful to attackers; log them internally instead.

questions.question: Hard-coding database passwords in application source code is risky because:

options.A: Anyone with access to the code or repository can see and misuse the credentials
options.B: It makes the application slower because the password is checked at every call
options.C: Compilers reject source code that contains string literals for passwords
options.D: It forces the database to use weaker encryption for the connection

questions.answer_text: Anyone with access to the code or repository can see and misuse the credentials
questions.explanation: Secrets should be stored in a vault or secure configuration with access control.

questions.question: The most effective defence against SQL injection in application code is:

options.A: Using parameterised queries / prepared statements
options.B: Using long and complex table names
options.C: Hiding the login page behind a CAPTCHA and an IP whitelist
options.D: Enforcing HTTPS on all application pages

questions.answer_text: Using parameterised queries / prepared statements
questions.explanation: User input is treated strictly as data, never as part of the SQL command.

questions.question: In the STRIDE threat model, 'R' stands for:

options.A: Rootkit
options.B: Ransomware
options.C: Replication
options.D: Repudiation

questions.answer_text: Repudiation
questions.explanation: STRIDE = Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service, Elevation of privilege.

questions.question: In STRIDE, which threat is countered mainly by strong authentication?

options.A: Information disclosure
options.B: Denial of service
options.C: Tampering
options.D: Spoofing

questions.answer_text: Spoofing
questions.explanation: Tampering -> integrity controls; Repudiation -> logging/signatures; Info disclosure -> encryption; Elevation -> authorisation.

questions.question: Threat modelling in a secure SDLC is best performed during the:

options.A: Maintenance phase only
options.B: After go-live only
options.C: Decommissioning phase
options.D: Design phase

questions.answer_text: Design phase
questions.explanation: Design-stage threat modelling finds architectural flaws before code is written.

questions.question: SonarQube is an example of a tool used for:

options.A: Container orchestration and scaling
options.B: Load and performance testing of web apps
options.C: Network traffic monitoring and alerting
options.D: Static code quality and security analysis

questions.answer_text: Static code quality and security analysis
questions.explanation: It flags bugs, code smells and security hotspots in source code.

questions.question: Arrange the testing levels in the order they are normally performed:

options.A: System -> Unit -> Integration -> Acceptance
options.B: Acceptance -> System -> Integration -> Unit
options.C: Integration -> Unit -> Acceptance -> System
options.D: Unit -> Integration -> System -> Acceptance

questions.answer_text: Unit -> Integration -> System -> Acceptance
questions.explanation: Testing moves from the smallest components to the complete system validated by users.

questions.question: Testing in which the tester has access to the internal code and logic is called:

options.A: Beta testing
options.B: White-box testing
options.C: Black-box testing
options.D: Acceptance testing

questions.answer_text: White-box testing
questions.explanation: Black-box testing checks behaviour against requirements without knowing the code.

questions.question: Alpha testing and beta testing differ in that:

options.A: Alpha is done by internal users at the developer's site; beta is done by real users in their own environment before full release
options.B: Both alpha and beta testing are done only after the product has been withdrawn from the market
options.C: Beta is done by internal users at the developer's site; alpha is done by real users in their own environment before release
options.D: Alpha testing is done only by customers after release, while beta testing is done only by developers before release

questions.answer_text: Alpha is done by internal users at the developer's site; beta is done by real users in their own environment before full release
questions.explanation: Both help find issues before general availability.

questions.question: User Acceptance Testing (UAT) is performed by:

options.A: Developers to confirm that each unit of code works exactly as designed in the LLD
options.B: Business/end users to confirm the system meets their requirements before go-live
options.C: Hardware vendors to confirm that servers meet specifications
options.D: The database administrator to confirm that backups are working

questions.answer_text: Business/end users to confirm the system meets their requirements before go-live
questions.explanation: UAT sign-off is usually a prerequisite for production deployment.

questions.question: Re-testing existing features after a code change to make sure nothing else broke is called:

options.A: Regression testing
options.B: Load testing
options.C: Smoke testing
options.D: Alpha testing

questions.answer_text: Regression testing
questions.explanation: Automated regression suites make frequent releases safe.

questions.question: Smoke testing is:

options.A: A quick set of basic tests to check that a new build's critical functions work before deeper testing
options.B: A test carried out by real users in their own environment before the final release
options.C: A test that checks how the system behaves when it is pushed far beyond its expected peak load
options.D: Exhaustive testing of every feature and every input combination before the system is released

questions.answer_text: A quick set of basic tests to check that a new build's critical functions work before deeper testing
questions.explanation: If the smoke test fails, the build is rejected without wasting time on detailed testing.

questions.question: An input field accepts ages from 18 to 60. Using boundary value analysis, which set of test values is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Errors cluster at the edges, so values just inside and outside each boundary are tested.

questions.question: Equivalence partitioning means:

options.A: Testing only invalid inputs, since valid inputs are already covered by developers
options.B: Dividing inputs into groups expected to behave the same and testing one value from each group
options.C: Testing the values just inside and just outside each boundary of an input range to find edge errors
options.D: Testing every possible input value one by one to make sure nothing is missed

questions.answer_text: Dividing inputs into groups expected to behave the same and testing one value from each group
questions.explanation: It reduces the number of test cases while keeping coverage.

questions.question: What is the difference between load testing and stress testing?

options.A: Both load and stress testing are manual reviews of design documents
options.B: Both load and stress testing check only the look and feel of the user interface
options.C: Load testing checks behaviour at expected peak load; stress testing pushes beyond limits to find the breaking point
options.D: Stress testing checks behaviour at expected peak load; load testing pushes beyond limits to find the breaking point

questions.answer_text: Load testing checks behaviour at expected peak load; stress testing pushes beyond limits to find the breaking point
questions.explanation: Stress testing also checks how gracefully the system fails and recovers.

questions.question: Selenium and Apache JMeter are commonly used for:

options.A: Performance/load testing and UI test automation respectively
options.B: UI test automation and performance/load testing respectively
options.C: Static code analysis and dependency scanning respectively
options.D: Database backup and source code version control respectively

questions.answer_text: UI test automation and performance/load testing respectively
questions.explanation: Automation tools speed up regression and performance testing.

questions.question: In defect management, 'severity' and 'priority' differ in that:

options.A: Severity is the technical impact of the defect; priority is how urgently it should be fixed
options.B: Priority is the technical impact of the defect; severity is how urgently it should be fixed
options.C: Severity and priority always have the same value for every defect
options.D: Severity is decided by the customer only; priority is decided by the code

questions.answer_text: Severity is the technical impact of the defect; priority is how urgently it should be fixed
questions.explanation: A spelling mistake in the bank's name on the home page: low severity but high priority.

questions.question: Quality Assurance (QA) differs from Quality Control (QC) because QA:

options.A: Is done only by customers after release, while QC is done only by developers
options.B: Focuses on inspecting the finished product to find defects, while QC focuses on improving the processes
options.C: Focuses on improving processes to prevent defects; QC focuses on inspecting the product to find defects
options.D: Is concerned only with documentation, while QC is concerned only with hardware

questions.answer_text: Focuses on improving processes to prevent defects; QC focuses on inspecting the product to find defects
questions.explanation: QA is process-oriented and proactive; QC is product-oriented and reactive.

questions.question: Test-Driven Development (TDD) means:

options.A: Letting end users do all the testing during user acceptance testing
options.B: Writing all the code first and adding automated tests only after the project ends
options.C: Skipping unit tests and relying only on system testing before release
options.D: Writing an automated test first, then writing code to make it pass, then refactoring

questions.answer_text: Writing an automated test first, then writing code to make it pass, then refactoring
questions.explanation: Cycle: Red (failing test) -> Green (pass) -> Refactor.

questions.question: Modifying an application so that it works on a new operating system version or meets a new regulatory requirement is:

options.A: Corrective maintenance
options.B: Adaptive maintenance
options.C: Preventive maintenance
options.D: Perfective maintenance

questions.answer_text: Adaptive maintenance
questions.explanation: Corrective = fixing bugs; Perfective = enhancements/performance; Preventive = reducing future problems.

questions.question: 'Technical debt' refers to:

options.A: The cost of training developers on new tools and technologies introduced in a project
options.B: The amount of money that a bank owes to software vendors for licences and annual support contracts
options.C: The loans taken by the IT department to buy new hardware and infrastructure
options.D: The future cost of rework caused by choosing quick or easy solutions now instead of better ones

questions.answer_text: The future cost of rework caused by choosing quick or easy solutions now instead of better ones
questions.explanation: Unmanaged technical debt slows future changes and increases defects.

questions.question: In the Capability Maturity Model (CMM), the highest level (Level 5) is called:

options.A: Defined
options.B: Managed
options.C: Initial
options.D: Optimizing

questions.answer_text: Optimizing
questions.explanation: Levels: 1 Initial, 2 Repeatable/Managed, 3 Defined, 4 Quantitatively Managed, 5 Optimizing.

questions.question: At CMM Level 1 (Initial), software processes are:

options.A: Fully optimised through continuous, data-driven process improvement
options.B: Standardised and documented across the organisation
options.C: Ad hoc and chaotic, with success depending on individual effort
options.D: Quantitatively measured and controlled using metrics

questions.answer_text: Ad hoc and chaotic, with success depending on individual effort
questions.explanation: Higher levels add repeatability, standardisation, measurement and optimisation.

questions.question: In web development, HTML, CSS and JavaScript are mainly used for:

options.A: Structure, presentation/styling and interactivity respectively
options.B: Structure, data storage and encryption respectively
options.C: Presentation/styling, structure and interactivity respectively
options.D: Database access, server logic and network routing respectively

questions.answer_text: Structure, presentation/styling and interactivity respectively
questions.explanation: HTML defines content structure; CSS styles it; JavaScript adds behaviour.

questions.question: Which of the following is a semantic HTML5 element?

options.A: <span>
options.C: <article>
options.D: <div>

questions.answer_text: <article>
questions.explanation: Semantic tags (<header>, <nav>, <article>, <section>, <footer>) describe meaning, helping accessibility and SEO.

questions.question: Which HTML form method sends form data in the request body rather than in the URL?

options.A: HEAD
options.B: GET
options.C: OPTIONS
options.D: POST

questions.answer_text: POST
questions.explanation: GET appends data to the URL (visible in logs/history), so it must not be used for passwords.

questions.question: In the CSS box model, what is the order of layers from the inside out?

options.A: Content, padding, border, margin
options.B: Margin, border, padding, content
options.C: Padding, content, border, margin
options.D: Content, margin, border, padding

questions.answer_text: Content, padding, border, margin
questions.explanation: Padding is inside the border; margin is the space outside it.

questions.question: In CSS, which symbols select an element by id and by class respectively?

options.A: # for id and . for class
options.B: . for id and # for class
options.C: id= for id and class= for class
options.D: @ for id and $ for class

questions.answer_text: # for id and . for class
questions.explanation: Example: #header { } targets id='header'; .btn { } targets class='btn'.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a valid value of the CSS 'border-style' property?

options.A: dotted
options.B: double
options.C: bold
