options.D: solid

questions.answer_text: bold
questions.explanation: Other valid values include groove, ridge, inset, outset, none and hidden.

questions.question: In CSS specificity, which selector type has the HIGHEST priority (ignoring !important)?

options.A: Inline style attribute
options.B: Element (tag) selector
options.C: ID selector
options.D: Class selector

questions.answer_text: Inline style attribute
questions.explanation: Order: inline > ID > class/attribute/pseudo-class > element.

questions.question: Which JavaScript event fires when an input field loses focus?

options.A: onclick
options.B: onblur
options.C: onload
options.D: onfocus

questions.answer_text: onblur
questions.explanation: onblur is often used to validate a field after the user leaves it.

questions.question: Which JavaScript function converts the string '42' into an integer?

options.A: String()
options.B: toString()
options.C: toFixed()
options.D: parseInt()

questions.answer_text: parseInt()
questions.explanation: parseFloat() converts to a decimal number; Number() is another option.

questions.question: In JavaScript, what is the difference between '==' and '==='?

options.A: '===' assigns a value to a variable; '==' compares two values
options.B: '===' compares both value and type; '==' converts types before comparing
options.C: '==' compares both value and type; '===' converts types before comparing
options.D: There is no difference; both compare values in the same way

questions.answer_text: '===' compares both value and type; '==' converts types before comparing
questions.explanation: '5' == 5 is true, but '5' === 5 is false.

questions.question: The DOM (Document Object Model) is:

options.A: A web server module that renders pages before sending them
options.B: A CSS framework used for building responsive page layouts
options.C: A tree-structured representation of an HTML page that scripts can read and modify
options.D: A database used by web servers to store HTML pages and the session data of logged-in users

questions.answer_text: A tree-structured representation of an HTML page that scripts can read and modify
questions.explanation: JavaScript uses DOM methods like getElementById to change page content dynamically.

questions.question: AJAX / Fetch API allows a web page to:

options.A: Run JavaScript only on the server instead of in the browser, for better security
options.B: Exchange data with the server asynchronously without reloading the whole page
options.C: Encrypt the data stored in the server's database
options.D: Block pop-up windows and advertisements on the page

questions.answer_text: Exchange data with the server asynchronously without reloading the whole page
questions.explanation: Used for live balance updates, auto-complete and similar features.

questions.question: React, developed by Meta, is known for:

options.A: Running as a server operating system for web hosting
options.B: Storing data in tables with SQL queries and transactions
options.C: Styling pages using only CSS, without any JavaScript
options.D: Building UIs from reusable components using a virtual DOM

questions.answer_text: Building UIs from reusable components using a virtual DOM
questions.explanation: Angular (Google, TypeScript-based) and Vue are other popular UI frameworks.

questions.question: Responsive web design means:

options.A: The layout adapts to different screen sizes such as mobile, tablet and desktop
options.B: The site replies automatically to customer emails and chat messages within minutes
options.C: The server always responds to every request within one second
options.D: The page avoids images and scripts so that it loads quickly

questions.answer_text: The layout adapts to different screen sizes such as mobile, tablet and desktop
questions.explanation: Achieved using flexible grids and CSS media queries (frameworks like Bootstrap help).

questions.question: A Single Page Application (SPA):

options.A: Loads a separate HTML page from the server for every click, refreshing the whole screen
options.B: Contains all its code on a single page and cannot call any external APIs
options.C: Loads one HTML page and updates content dynamically via JavaScript without full page reloads
options.D: Works only offline after installation and cannot connect to any server

questions.answer_text: Loads one HTML page and updates content dynamically via JavaScript without full page reloads
questions.explanation: SPAs feel faster but need careful handling of security tokens and SEO.

questions.question: Server-side processing in a web application refers to:

options.A: Animations and visual effects running inside the user's browser using JavaScript
options.B: CSS styling and layout calculations done by the browser
options.C: Image rendering and video playback on the user's screen
options.D: Business logic, database access and authentication executed on the server

questions.answer_text: Business logic, database access and authentication executed on the server
questions.explanation: Back-end technologies include Java (Spring), .NET, Node.js, Python (Django), PHP.

questions.question: Node.js is:

options.A: A JavaScript runtime for server-side applications using an event-driven, non-blocking I/O model
options.B: A CSS framework for building responsive layouts with a grid system and ready-made components
options.C: A browser plugin that runs JavaScript faster by compiling it into native machine code
options.D: A relational database that stores data in tables and supports SQL queries and transactions

questions.answer_text: A JavaScript runtime for server-side applications using an event-driven, non-blocking I/O model
questions.explanation: It is built on Chrome's V8 JavaScript engine.

questions.question: Java is called platform-independent because:

options.A: It is an interpreted scripting language that runs only inside web browsers
options.B: Source code compiles to bytecode that runs on any system with a Java Virtual Machine (JVM)
options.C: It needs no runtime environment, so programs run directly on any operating system
options.D: Source code compiles directly to machine code that runs on every processor architecture

questions.answer_text: Source code compiles to bytecode that runs on any system with a Java Virtual Machine (JVM)
questions.explanation: 'Write once, run anywhere' - the JVM is platform-specific, the bytecode is not.

questions.question: Which pair correctly lists a web server and an application server?

options.A: Oracle Database (web server); MySQL (application server)
options.B: Tomcat / WebLogic (web server); Apache HTTP Server / Nginx (application server)
options.C: Apache HTTP Server / Nginx (web server); Tomcat / WebLogic (application server)
options.D: Chrome (web server); Firefox (application server)

questions.answer_text: Apache HTTP Server / Nginx (web server); Tomcat / WebLogic (application server)
questions.explanation: Web servers serve HTTP/static content; application servers run business logic components.

questions.question: HTTP is called a stateless protocol because:

options.A: Each request is independent; the server does not remember previous requests by itself
options.B: It stores every request permanently on the server for later reference
options.C: It cannot carry any data in requests other than the URL being requested
options.D: It cannot run over TCP, so it must use UDP for every single request and response it sends

questions.answer_text: Each request is independent; the server does not remember previous requests by itself
questions.explanation: Cookies, sessions and tokens are used to maintain state across requests.

questions.question: What is the difference between cookies and sessions?

options.A: Sessions are stored in the user's browser; cookie data is stored on the server and identified by a cookie ID
options.B: Cookies are always encrypted by the browser, while session data is always stored in plain text
options.C: Cookies are stored in the user's browser; session data is stored on the server and identified by a session ID
options.D: Both cookies and sessions are stored only in the application's database and never in the browser

questions.answer_text: Cookies are stored in the user's browser; session data is stored on the server and identified by a session ID
questions.explanation: Sensitive data should be kept server-side, not in cookies.

questions.question: Which HTTP method is NOT idempotent (repeating it may create duplicate effects)?

options.A: POST
options.B: GET
options.C: PUT
options.D: DELETE

questions.answer_text: POST
questions.explanation: Repeating a POST could create two payments; payment APIs use idempotency keys to prevent this.

questions.question: Match the HTTP status codes: (P) 201 (Q) 403 (R) 404 (S) 503 | (1) Not Found (2) Service Unavailable (3) Created (4) Forbidden
questions.explanation: 2xx success, 3xx redirection, 4xx client error, 5xx server error.

questions.question: HTTP status 401 differs from 403 in that:

options.A: Both mean that the requested page has permanently moved to a new URL
options.B: 401 means an internal server error; 403 means the requested page was not found
options.C: 401 means the user is authenticated but not allowed; 403 means the user is not authenticated
options.D: 401 means the user is not authenticated; 403 means the user is authenticated but not allowed

questions.answer_text: 401 means the user is not authenticated; 403 means the user is authenticated but not allowed
questions.explanation: 401 Unauthorized asks for valid credentials; 403 Forbidden refuses even with credentials.

questions.question: An API returns HTTP 429. This indicates:

options.A: Moved permanently - the resource has a new URL
options.B: Too many requests - the client has exceeded the rate limit
options.C: Internal server error - the server failed unexpectedly
options.D: Created - the requested resource was created successfully

questions.answer_text: Too many requests - the client has exceeded the rate limit
questions.explanation: Rate limiting protects APIs from abuse and overload.

questions.question: JSON is often preferred over XML for web APIs because it is:

options.A: Required by the HTTP protocol for all API responses
options.B: Always encrypted during transmission, unlike XML
options.C: Lighter, less verbose and natively easy to parse in JavaScript
options.D: Able to define strict schemas and namespaces, which XML cannot do

questions.answer_text: Lighter, less verbose and natively easy to parse in JavaScript
questions.explanation: XML is still used in SOAP, ISO 20022 messages and many legacy integrations.

questions.question: In a 3-tier web architecture, the three tiers are:

options.A: Development, Testing, Production
options.B: Front-end, Middleware, Network
options.C: Presentation, Application (business logic), Data
options.D: Client tier, Load balancer tier, Web server tier

questions.answer_text: Presentation, Application (business logic), Data
questions.explanation: Each tier can be scaled and secured independently.

questions.question: A key security advantage of 3-tier architecture is that:

options.A: The database is not directly exposed to users; only the application tier can reach it
options.B: No firewall is needed between tiers because each tier is on its own server
options.C: Users connect directly to the database, which removes one network hop and a point of failure
options.D: All three tiers run on one server, which reduces the attack surface

questions.answer_text: The database is not directly exposed to users; only the application tier can reach it
questions.explanation: Typical placement: web tier in DMZ, app tier internal, DB tier in the most restricted zone.

questions.question: Microservices architecture builds an application as:

options.A: A collection of database stored procedures called directly by the user interface
options.B: One large program in which all business functions are built and deployed as a single unit
options.C: A set of front-end components that share one back-end server and one database
options.D: A set of small, independently deployable services, each owning a specific business capability

questions.answer_text: A set of small, independently deployable services, each owning a specific business capability
questions.explanation: Services communicate via APIs or messaging.

questions.question: Microservices are considered highly scalable mainly because:

options.A: All services share a single server, so resources are pooled
options.B: They always run on mainframes with very large capacity
options.C: Each service can be scaled independently based on its own load
options.D: They avoid network calls between services entirely

questions.answer_text: Each service can be scaled independently based on its own load
questions.explanation: E.g. only the payment service is scaled up during salary-day peaks.

questions.question: Compared with microservices, a monolithic application:

options.A: Is deployed as one unit, so even a small change requires rebuilding and redeploying the whole application
options.B: Is always more scalable than microservices because all components share the same memory
options.C: Is made of many small services that are deployed independently and communicate with each other over APIs
options.D: Cannot use a database, so all data must be stored in files on the application server

questions.answer_text: Is deployed as one unit, so even a small change requires rebuilding and redeploying the whole application
questions.explanation: Monoliths are simpler to start with; microservices add operational complexity.

questions.question: In microservices, the circuit breaker pattern is used to:

options.A: Encrypt all messages exchanged between services
options.B: Stop calling a failing service for a while to prevent cascading failures
options.C: Cut electrical power to servers that are overheating in the data centre racks
options.D: Merge small services back into a single monolith

questions.answer_text: Stop calling a failing service for a while to prevent cascading failures
questions.explanation: After a timeout, it lets a few test calls through ('half-open') to check recovery.

questions.question: An API Gateway in a microservices architecture provides:

options.A: DNS resolution for internet domain names used by the services
options.B: Physical storage for container images, service configuration files and secrets used by backend services
options.C: A single entry point handling routing, authentication, rate limiting and logging for backend services
options.D: Replication of each service's database to the DR site in real time

questions.answer_text: A single entry point handling routing, authentication, rate limiting and logging for backend services
questions.explanation: It shields internal services from direct exposure.

questions.question: A service mesh (e.g. Istio) in microservices mainly handles:

options.A: Hardware provisioning of servers and storage for the Kubernetes cluster in the data centre
options.B: User interface rendering for single-page applications using a virtual DOM and reusable front-end components
options.C: Service-to-service communication concerns such as mutual TLS, retries and traffic routing via sidecar proxies
options.D: Database indexing and query optimisation for services that share a single relational database

questions.answer_text: Service-to-service communication concerns such as mutual TLS, retries and traffic routing via sidecar proxies
questions.explanation: It moves networking and security logic out of application code.

questions.question: The OWASP Top 10 is:

options.A: A certification that every web application must pass before it is allowed to go live
options.B: An awareness document listing the most critical web application security risks
options.C: A firewall product that blocks the ten most common attacks
options.D: A ranking of the ten fastest and most popular web servers

questions.answer_text: An awareness document listing the most critical web application security risks
questions.explanation: OWASP = Open Worldwide Application Security Project, a non-profit community.

questions.question: In the OWASP Top 10 (2021), which risk is ranked #1?

options.A: Injection
options.B: Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
options.C: Cryptographic Failures
options.D: Broken Access Control

questions.answer_text: Broken Access Control
questions.explanation: Injection moved down to #3 in the 2021 list.

questions.question: A logged-in customer changes 'account=1001' to 'account=1002' in the URL and sees another customer's statement. This is an example of:

options.A: SQL injection through the account number parameter in the URL
options.B: Cross-site scripting (reflected XSS)
options.C: Broken access control (insecure direct object reference)
options.D: Session fixation after login

questions.answer_text: Broken access control (insecure direct object reference)
questions.explanation: The server must check that the requested object belongs to the logged-in user.

questions.question: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) is an attack where:

options.A: DNS records are changed so that users reach a fake website
options.B: Malicious SQL commands are injected into a login form and then executed on the database
options.C: A web server is flooded with requests until it stops responding
options.D: Malicious scripts are injected into a trusted website and run in other users' browsers

questions.answer_text: Malicious scripts are injected into a trusted website and run in other users' browsers
questions.explanation: XSS can steal session cookies or modify page content.

questions.question: Which type of XSS is stored permanently on the server (e.g. in a comment or profile field) and affects every user who views that page?

options.A: Stored (persistent) XSS
options.B: Blind SQL injection
options.C: Reflected XSS
options.D: DOM-based XSS only

questions.answer_text: Stored (persistent) XSS
questions.explanation: Reflected XSS comes from a crafted link and affects only the user who clicks it.

questions.question: The main defences against XSS are:

options.A: Long and complex passwords with periodic expiry
options.B: Context-aware output encoding and a Content Security Policy (CSP)
options.C: Disabling HTTPS so that the WAF can inspect all incoming request traffic
options.D: Adding database indexes on all user input columns

questions.answer_text: Context-aware output encoding and a Content Security Policy (CSP)
questions.explanation: Input validation helps, but encoding output is the key control.

questions.question: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) tricks a logged-in user's browser into sending unwanted requests. It is prevented mainly by:

options.A: Using GET requests for fund transfers
options.B: Anti-CSRF tokens and SameSite cookies
options.C: Increasing the session timeout
options.D: Disabling all cookies in the browser

questions.answer_text: Anti-CSRF tokens and SameSite cookies
questions.explanation: The attacker's site cannot read the unique token, so forged requests fail.

questions.question: Entering ' OR '1'='1 in a login form to bypass authentication is an example of:

options.A: SQL injection
options.B: Cross-site scripting
options.C: Clickjacking
options.D: Phishing

questions.answer_text: SQL injection
questions.explanation: Parameterised queries prevent it.

questions.question: Which HTTP response header helps prevent clickjacking by stopping the page from being loaded inside a frame on another site?

options.A: X-Frame-Options (or CSP frame-ancestors)
options.B: Accept-Encoding (or Content-Encoding)
options.C: Content-Type (or X-Content-Type-Options)
options.D: Cache-Control (or Expires)

questions.answer_text: X-Frame-Options (or CSP frame-ancestors)
questions.explanation: Clickjacking overlays an invisible frame to trick users into clicking.

questions.question: HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) instructs browsers to:

options.A: Save the user's password securely in the browser's password manager
options.B: Disable JavaScript on pages loaded over HTTP
options.C: Always connect to the site using HTTPS, refusing plain HTTP
options.D: Cache all pages of the site for faster loading

questions.answer_text: Always connect to the site using HTTPS, refusing plain HTTP
questions.explanation: It prevents SSL-stripping attacks that downgrade users to HTTP.

questions.question: Setting the 'HttpOnly' flag on a session cookie:

options.A: Prevents JavaScript from reading the cookie, reducing theft via XSS
options.B: Sends the cookie only over plain HTTP and never over an HTTPS connection
options.C: Encrypts the cookie value so that it cannot be read
options.D: Makes the cookie permanent so that it never expires

questions.answer_text: Prevents JavaScript from reading the cookie, reducing theft via XSS
questions.explanation: 'Secure' sends the cookie only over HTTPS; 'SameSite' limits cross-site sending (CSRF).

questions.question: Issuing a new session ID immediately after a user logs in protects against:

options.A: DNS spoofing
options.B: Brute force on the database
options.C: Session fixation
options.D: SQL injection

questions.answer_text: Session fixation
questions.explanation: Otherwise an attacker could plant a known session ID before login and reuse it.

questions.question: CAPTCHA is used on login and registration pages mainly to:

options.A: Speed up loading of the login page
options.B: Encrypt the password before it is sent to the server
options.C: Store the user's language preferences
options.D: Distinguish human users from automated bots

questions.answer_text: Distinguish human users from automated bots
questions.explanation: It reduces credential stuffing, spam registrations and scraping.

questions.question: In a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) attack, the attacker:

options.A: Injects malicious scripts into web pages that then run in other users' browsers
options.B: Steals session cookies by sniffing traffic on an unencrypted public Wi-Fi network
options.C: Makes the server send requests to internal or unintended resources using an attacker-supplied URL
options.D: Tricks the user's browser into sending forged requests to a site where the user is logged in

questions.answer_text: Makes the server send requests to internal or unintended resources using an attacker-supplied URL
questions.explanation: SSRF can expose cloud metadata services and internal systems.

questions.question: REST APIs typically:

options.A: Use only XML envelopes described by a WSDL contract
options.B: Work only over FTP and SMTP rather than HTTP
options.C: Require the server to keep a permanent session for each connected client application
options.D: Use standard HTTP methods on resources identified by URIs and are stateless

questions.answer_text: Use standard HTTP methods on resources identified by URIs and are stateless
questions.explanation: Responses are commonly in JSON.

questions.question: Statelessness in REST means:

options.A: The API contract never changes once it has been published to clients
options.B: Each request contains all information needed to process it; the server keeps no client session state
options.C: Requests cannot include headers, so authentication is passed in the URL
options.D: The server stores each client's full session state in its memory between consecutive requests from that client

questions.answer_text: Each request contains all information needed to process it; the server keeps no client session state
questions.explanation: Statelessness makes REST services easy to scale horizontally.

questions.question: SOAP web services are characterised by:

options.A: JSON-only messages, flexible contracts and no formal security standards of any kind
options.B: Binary messages over UDP with no contract describing the operations
options.C: Plain-text messages that can be used only within mobile applications
options.D: XML-based message envelopes, strict contracts (WSDL) and standards like WS-Security

questions.answer_text: XML-based message envelopes, strict contracts (WSDL) and standards like WS-Security
questions.explanation: SOAP is heavier than REST but still common in enterprise/banking integrations.

questions.question: OAuth 2.0 is mainly used for:

options.A: Encrypting all the data stored on hard disks, so that stolen laptops and servers do not expose any confidential customer information
options.B: Signing software releases so that users can verify that the code has not been tampered with
options.C: Authenticating users with biometrics so that passwords are no longer needed for any application
options.D: Delegated authorisation - letting an application access resources on a user's behalf via access tokens without sharing the password

questions.answer_text: Delegated authorisation - letting an application access resources on a user's behalf via access tokens without sharing the password
questions.explanation: OpenID Connect adds an identity (authentication) layer on top of OAuth 2.0.

questions.question: A JSON Web Token (JWT) consists of:

options.A: Username and password in plain text
options.B: Header, payload (claims) and signature
options.C: A session cookie and a CAPTCHA
options.D: Only an encrypted password

questions.answer_text: Header, payload (claims) and signature
questions.explanation: The signature lets the server verify the token has not been altered.

questions.question: In the OWASP API Security Top 10 (2023), the top risk where an API returns objects without checking that the caller owns them is:

options.A: Unrestricted Resource Consumption
options.B: Server-Side Request Forgery
options.C: Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA)
options.D: Security Misconfiguration of the API gateway

questions.answer_text: Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA)
questions.explanation: Every object access must be authorised against the caller's identity.

questions.question: GraphQL differs from REST mainly because it:

options.A: Cannot return JSON, so responses are always in XML format
options.B: Lets the client request exactly the fields it needs from a single endpoint
options.C: Uses only SOAP envelopes and WSDL contracts for every request and response
options.D: Requires a separate endpoint for every field of every object

questions.answer_text: Lets the client request exactly the fields it needs from a single endpoint
questions.explanation: It reduces over-fetching and multiple round trips.

questions.question: A Content Delivery Network (CDN) improves website performance by:

options.A: Compressing the CPU instructions of the web server for faster execution
options.B: Storing a copy of the bank's database inside users' browsers for much faster access
options.C: Disabling images and scripts on pages to reduce the data sent
options.D: Caching content on edge servers close to users, reducing latency and origin load

questions.answer_text: Caching content on edge servers close to users, reducing latency and origin load
questions.explanation: CDNs also help absorb DDoS traffic.

questions.question: Which load-balancing algorithm sends each new request to the server with the fewest active connections?

options.A: Random
options.B: IP hash
options.C: Round robin
options.D: Least connections

questions.answer_text: Least connections
questions.explanation: Round robin rotates requests in order regardless of current load.

questions.question: 'Sticky sessions' on a load balancer mean:

options.A: Users cannot log out until their session times out
options.B: All backend servers share a single session file on disk
options.C: Requests from the same user are always sent to the same backend server
options.D: User sessions never expire, even after the browser is closed by the user

questions.answer_text: Requests from the same user are always sent to the same backend server
questions.explanation: Simple but limits balancing; shared session stores (e.g. Redis) are an alternative.

questions.question: Redis is commonly used in web applications as:

options.A: A web browser engine for rendering HTML pages
options.B: A relational database used to store core banking transactions
options.C: An in-memory key-value store for caching and session data
options.D: A Type 1 hypervisor for running virtual machines

questions.answer_text: An in-memory key-value store for caching and session data
questions.explanation: Keeping hot data in memory greatly reduces response time and database load.

questions.question: Database connection pooling improves web application performance because:

options.A: Data is stored in the browser so that the database is called less often
options.B: Connections are reused instead of being opened and closed for every request
options.C: Transactions are disabled so that queries do not wait for commits
options.D: More database tables are created so that each request uses its own table

questions.answer_text: Connections are reused instead of being opened and closed for every request
questions.explanation: Opening a database connection is expensive.

questions.question: Minifying CSS/JavaScript and enabling gzip/Brotli compression improve performance by:

options.A: Reducing the size of files sent to the browser
options.B: Encrypting the files sent to the browser
options.C: Increasing server CPU usage for each request
options.D: Adding more features to each page

questions.answer_text: Reducing the size of files sent to the browser
questions.explanation: Smaller payloads load faster, especially on mobile networks.

questions.question: Which DNS record type maps a domain name to an IPv4 address?

options.A: CNAME record
options.B: A record
options.C: AAAA record
options.D: MX record

questions.answer_text: A record
questions.explanation: AAAA = IPv6, MX = mail server, CNAME = alias to another name.

questions.question: RBI asked Indian banks in 2025 to migrate their websites to which exclusive domain to help customers recognise genuine bank sites and curb phishing?

options.A: .rbi.org
options.B: .gov.in
options.C: .bank.com
options.D: .bank.in

questions.answer_text: .bank.in
questions.explanation: IDRBT acts as the registrar; '.fin.in' was announced for other financial sector entities.

questions.question: When you type a bank's URL in a browser, which sequence happens first to last?

options.A: DNS resolution -> TCP connection -> TLS handshake -> HTTP request -> page rendering
options.B: TLS handshake -> DNS resolution -> TCP connection -> HTTP request -> rendering
options.C: HTTP request -> DNS resolution -> TLS handshake -> TCP connection -> rendering
options.D: TCP connection -> DNS resolution -> HTTP request -> TLS handshake -> rendering

questions.answer_text: DNS resolution -> TCP connection -> TLS handshake -> HTTP request -> page rendering
questions.explanation: The IP must be known before connecting; TLS is set up on the TCP connection before HTTP data is sent.

questions.question: In shared web hosting:

options.A: No server is used at all
options.B: Each website gets its own dedicated physical server in the data centre
options.C: Many websites share the same server and its resources
options.D: The website runs only on the user's PC

questions.answer_text: Many websites share the same server and its resources
questions.explanation: VPS gives a virtual slice with dedicated resources; dedicated hosting gives a whole server.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between AI, Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL)?

options.A: AI, ML and DL are separate, unrelated fields
options.B: AI is a subset of ML, which is a subset of DL
options.C: DL is a subset of ML, which is a subset of AI
options.D: ML is a subset of DL, which is a subset of AI

questions.answer_text: DL is a subset of ML, which is a subset of AI
questions.explanation: Deep learning uses multi-layer neural networks, a specific ML technique.

questions.question: Training a model on past loan records labelled 'defaulted' or 'repaid' is an example of:

options.A: Reinforcement learning
options.B: Unsupervised learning
options.C: Rule-based programming
options.D: Supervised learning

questions.answer_text: Supervised learning
questions.explanation: Supervised learning learns from input-output pairs (labelled data).

questions.question: Grouping customers into segments based on spending behaviour without any predefined labels is:

options.A: Reinforcement learning (reward-based)
options.B: Unsupervised learning (clustering)
options.C: Supervised learning (classification)
options.D: Supervised learning (regression)

questions.answer_text: Unsupervised learning (clustering)
questions.explanation: K-means is a popular clustering algorithm.

questions.question: In reinforcement learning, an agent learns by:

options.A: Studying a large set of labelled examples that are provided by human experts
options.B: Taking actions and receiving rewards or penalties from the environment
options.C: Grouping unlabelled data into clusters of similar records
options.D: Copying the decision rules written by domain experts

questions.answer_text: Taking actions and receiving rewards or penalties from the environment
questions.explanation: Used in robotics, game playing and also in RLHF for LLMs.

questions.question: Predicting whether a transaction is 'fraud' or 'genuine' is a ____ problem, while predicting a customer's next-month balance is a ____ problem.

options.A: Clustering; classification
options.B: Classification; regression
options.C: Regression; clustering
options.D: Regression; classification

questions.answer_text: Classification; regression
questions.explanation: Classification predicts categories; regression predicts continuous numbers.

questions.question: Which algorithm is commonly used for clustering?

options.A: K-means
options.B: Naive Bayes
options.C: Linear regression
options.D: Logistic regression

questions.answer_text: K-means
questions.explanation: Logistic regression and Naive Bayes are classification methods; linear regression predicts numbers.

questions.question: A model shows 99% accuracy on training data but only 70% on new data. This is called:

options.A: Data labelling
options.B: Normalisation
options.C: Underfitting
options.D: Overfitting

questions.answer_text: Overfitting
questions.explanation: The model memorised training data instead of learning general patterns.

questions.question: Which technique helps reduce overfitting?

options.A: Using more training data, regularisation and cross-validation
options.B: Adding more irrelevant features
options.C: Removing the test set
options.D: Training for many more epochs on the same small training data set

questions.answer_text: Using more training data, regularisation and cross-validation
questions.explanation: Simpler models and early stopping also help.

questions.question: Why is data split into training and test sets?

options.A: To make the training process run faster on large data
options.B: To reduce the storage space needed for the training data
options.C: To evaluate how well the model performs on unseen data
options.D: To keep sensitive data away from auditors and reviewers

questions.answer_text: To evaluate how well the model performs on unseen data
questions.explanation: Testing on training data gives an overly optimistic view of performance.

questions.question: In a fraud detection model, 'recall' measures:

options.A: The proportion of flagged transactions that were really frauds
options.B: The speed of the model
options.C: Overall accuracy on all transactions
options.D: The proportion of actual frauds that the model correctly caught

questions.answer_text: The proportion of actual frauds that the model correctly caught
questions.explanation: Precision = flagged frauds that are truly fraud. High recall means fewer missed frauds.

questions.question: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are best suited for:

options.A: Tabular data, such as joining relational database tables
options.B: Image data, such as cheque image or signature verification
options.C: Long text sequences, such as translating customer emails
options.D: Network data, such as routing packets between branches

questions.answer_text: Image data, such as cheque image or signature verification
questions.explanation: CNNs learn spatial patterns like edges and shapes.

questions.question: RNNs and LSTMs were designed mainly to handle:

options.A: Sequential data such as text and time series
options.B: Static images such as scanned cheques
options.C: Relational tables with fixed schemas
options.D: Encryption keys and digital certificates

questions.answer_text: Sequential data such as text and time series
questions.explanation: Transformers have largely replaced them for language tasks.

questions.question: Which language is NOT commonly used for AI/ML development?

options.A: COBOL
options.B: R
options.C: Python
options.D: Julia

questions.answer_text: COBOL
questions.explanation: Python dominates AI/ML with libraries like TensorFlow, PyTorch and scikit-learn.

questions.question: The Turing Test evaluates:

options.A: Whether a neural network has been trained on enough labelled data
options.B: Whether a machine's conversational behaviour is indistinguishable from a human's
options.C: Whether an encryption algorithm can resist attacks from a quantum computer
options.D: Whether a computer can solve mathematical problems faster than a human

questions.answer_text: Whether a machine's conversational behaviour is indistinguishable from a human's
questions.explanation: Proposed by Alan Turing in 1950.

questions.question: GPT in ChatGPT stands for:

options.A: Guided Probabilistic Translator
options.B: Generative Pre-trained Transformer
options.C: Graph-based Predictive Technology
options.D: General Purpose Text-generator

questions.answer_text: Generative Pre-trained Transformer
questions.explanation: The model is pre-trained on large text corpora and generates text.

questions.question: The Transformer architecture behind modern LLMs was introduced in the 2017 paper:

options.A: Deep Residual Learning
options.B: ImageNet Classification with Deep CNNs
options.C: Attention Is All You Need
options.D: Playing Atari with Deep RL

questions.answer_text: Attention Is All You Need
questions.explanation: Its key idea is self-attention, which relates every token to every other token in the input.

questions.question: A Large Language Model (LLM) generates text by:

options.A: Copying the most relevant web page it finds through a live internet search
options.B: Running SQL queries on internal databases to fetch the correct answer
options.C: Looking up the closest matching answer in a fixed table of stored responses
options.D: Predicting the next token repeatedly based on patterns learned from huge text data

questions.answer_text: Predicting the next token repeatedly based on patterns learned from huge text data
questions.explanation: Because it predicts plausible text, it can also produce plausible-sounding errors.

questions.question: In LLMs, a 'token' is:

options.A: A digital coin used to pay for each request made to the model
options.B: A security credential used to authenticate users to the AI application
options.C: A network packet that carries the prompt from the user to the server
options.D: A unit of text such as a word or part of a word that the model processes

questions.answer_text: A unit of text such as a word or part of a word that the model processes
questions.explanation: Pricing and context limits of LLMs are measured in tokens.

questions.question: The 'context window' of an LLM refers to:

options.A: The number of users who can chat with the model at the same time
options.B: The maximum number of tokens (input plus output) the model can consider at once
options.C: The size of the chat window that is displayed to the user in the banking application
options.D: The maximum time the model is allowed to take before it must answer

questions.answer_text: The maximum number of tokens (input plus output) the model can consider at once
questions.explanation: Content beyond the context window is not seen by the model.

questions.question: Lowering the 'temperature' setting of an LLM makes its output:

options.A: More focused and deterministic
options.B: Longer
options.C: More random, varied and creative
options.D: Encrypted

questions.answer_text: More focused and deterministic
questions.explanation: Higher temperature increases randomness; low temperature suits factual tasks.

questions.question: An LLM 'hallucination' is:

options.A: A crash of the model server during a long-running request
options.B: A confident-sounding output that is false or fabricated
options.C: An image generated instead of the requested text
options.D: An answer that is correct but takes too long

questions.answer_text: A confident-sounding output that is false or fabricated
questions.explanation: Grounding with RAG, citations and human review reduce the risk.

questions.question: A foundation model is:

options.A: A large model pre-trained on broad data that can be adapted to many downstream tasks
options.B: A small model trained only on a single bank's own data for one narrowly defined task
options.C: A rule-based expert system built from rules written by domain experts
options.D: The database schema that stores the training data used by an AI system

questions.answer_text: A large model pre-trained on broad data that can be adapted to many downstream tasks
questions.explanation: Examples include GPT, Claude, Gemini and Llama families.

questions.question: A multimodal AI model can:

options.A: Understand and reply in more than one natural language, but only in written text form
options.B: Run on more than one type of device such as phones and servers
options.C: Process and generate more than one type of data such as text, images and audio
options.D: Serve more than one user at a time in the same conversation

questions.answer_text: Process and generate more than one type of data such as text, images and audio
questions.explanation: E.g. reading a scanned document image and answering questions about it.

questions.question: 'Agentic AI' refers to AI systems that:

options.A: Only classify inputs into fixed categories without ever taking any action on them
options.B: Answer a single question per request with no access to tools
options.C: Plan multi-step tasks and take actions using tools or APIs with some autonomy
options.D: Run entirely without a model by following hand-written rules

questions.answer_text: Plan multi-step tasks and take actions using tools or APIs with some autonomy
questions.explanation: Agents raise new governance needs: permissions, approvals and audit of actions taken.

questions.question: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) improves LLM answers by:

options.A: Removing the system prompt so that the model is not limited by instructions
options.B: Increasing the temperature so that the model explores more possible answers
options.C: Retraining the entire model from scratch every day on the latest internal documents
options.D: Retrieving relevant documents from a knowledge base and giving them to the model as context

questions.answer_text: Retrieving relevant documents from a knowledge base and giving them to the model as context
questions.explanation: It grounds answers in current, internal data (e.g. bank circulars) and reduces hallucination.

questions.question: Embeddings in AI are:

options.A: Encrypted forms of user passwords that are stored inside the model's weights
options.B: Numerical vectors that represent the meaning of text, images or other data
options.C: HTML tags that embed AI widgets inside web pages
options.D: Specialised hardware chips embedded in AI servers

questions.answer_text: Numerical vectors that represent the meaning of text, images or other data
questions.explanation: Similar meanings produce vectors that are close to each other.

questions.question: A vector database differs from a traditional relational database because it:

options.A: Cannot be queried directly and is used only to back up the AI model's weights
options.B: Stores only numeric data in rows and columns and finds matching rows only by exact primary key matches
options.C: Does not support any kind of indexing, so every search scans all stored records
options.D: Stores embeddings and finds items by similarity (nearest neighbour search) rather than exact matches

questions.answer_text: Stores embeddings and finds items by similarity (nearest neighbour search) rather than exact matches
questions.explanation: Used in RAG to fetch passages semantically related to a user's question.

questions.question: Which measure is most commonly used to compare how similar two text embeddings are?

options.A: Cosine similarity
options.B: Hamming parity
options.C: Checksum
options.D: Round robin

questions.answer_text: Cosine similarity
questions.explanation: It measures the angle between vectors, ignoring their length.

questions.question: Fine-tuning an LLM means:

options.A: Further training a pre-trained model on domain-specific examples to specialise its behaviour
options.B: Increasing the context window so that the model can read longer documents
options.C: Deleting part of the model's original training data to remove unwanted behaviour
options.D: Writing more detailed prompts with worked examples so that the model behaves as the bank requires

questions.answer_text: Further training a pre-trained model on domain-specific examples to specialise its behaviour
questions.explanation: Fine-tuning changes model weights; prompting and RAG do not.

questions.question: LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) is popular because it:

options.A: Removes the need for any real training data by generating synthetic examples automatically for every new task
options.B: Encrypts the model's weights so that they cannot be copied or stolen by attackers
options.C: Stores document embeddings so that relevant passages can be retrieved for each query
options.D: Fine-tunes a model by training small added low-rank matrices instead of all weights, saving compute and memory

questions.answer_text: Fine-tunes a model by training small added low-rank matrices instead of all weights, saving compute and memory
questions.explanation: It is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) technique.

questions.question: RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback) is used to:

options.A: Compress the model so that it can run on smaller hardware such as branch PCs and mobile phones
options.B: Speed up GPU training by distributing work across many machines
options.C: Align model responses with human preferences using ratings from human reviewers
options.D: Translate model outputs into multiple languages automatically

questions.answer_text: Align model responses with human preferences using ratings from human reviewers
questions.explanation: It helps make models more helpful and less harmful.

questions.question: Prompt engineering refers to:

options.A: Configuring firewall rules that control which users can access an AI model
options.B: Writing database triggers that call an AI model whenever a table is updated
options.C: Designing the hardware and GPU clusters on which large AI models are trained and later served to users
options.D: Designing and refining the input instructions to get accurate and useful outputs from an AI model

questions.answer_text: Designing and refining the input instructions to get accurate and useful outputs from an AI model
questions.explanation: Clear instructions, context, examples and output format improve results.

questions.question: Giving an LLM a few solved examples inside the prompt before asking a new question is called:

options.A: Zero-shot prompting
options.B: Fine-tuning
options.C: Few-shot prompting
options.D: Pre-training

questions.answer_text: Few-shot prompting
questions.explanation: Zero-shot gives only the instruction with no examples.

questions.question: Asking the model to 'think step by step' before giving its final answer is known as:

options.A: Chain-of-thought prompting
options.B: Few-shot prompting with examples
options.C: Prompt injection
options.D: Temperature scaling

questions.answer_text: Chain-of-thought prompting
questions.explanation: It often improves performance on reasoning and arithmetic tasks.

questions.question: A 'system prompt' in an LLM application is used to:

options.A: Store the user's password so that they do not need to log in again
options.B: Set overall instructions, role and constraints that apply to the whole conversation
options.C: Display the chat user interface and format the model's responses
options.D: Restart the model server automatically whenever the conversation becomes too long for its memory

questions.answer_text: Set overall instructions, role and constraints that apply to the whole conversation
questions.explanation: E.g. 'You are a bank customer-service assistant; never reveal account data without authentication.'

questions.question: Prompt injection is an attack in which:

options.A: Malicious instructions hidden in user input or documents override the AI system's intended instructions
options.B: Training data is copied from the provider's storage and sold to competitors
options.C: The model's GPUs are overloaded with very long prompts until they overheat
options.D: An attacker floods the model server with requests until legitimate users can no longer get any answers from it

questions.answer_text: Malicious instructions hidden in user input or documents override the AI system's intended instructions
questions.explanation: Indirect prompt injection hides instructions in web pages or files the model reads.

questions.question: Crafting prompts specifically to make an AI model bypass its safety rules is called:

options.A: Jailbreaking
options.B: Embedding
options.C: Overfitting
options.D: Fine-tuning

questions.answer_text: Jailbreaking
questions.explanation: Guardrails, output filtering and monitoring help reduce jailbreak risk.

questions.question: Deliberately corrupting a model's training data to influence its behaviour is called:

options.A: Data masking
options.B: Data mining
options.C: Data poisoning
options.D: Data scrubbing

questions.answer_text: Data poisoning
questions.explanation: Controls on data sources and integrity checks of training data are needed.

questions.question: 'Model drift' means:

options.A: A model becomes faster over time as it caches frequently asked questions
options.B: A model is moved from one server to another during a data-centre migration
options.C: A model's performance degrades over time because real-world data patterns change
options.D: A model's weights are encrypted and slowly lose precision over time

questions.answer_text: A model's performance degrades over time because real-world data patterns change
questions.explanation: Continuous monitoring and periodic retraining/validation address drift.

questions.question: The biggest data-protection risk of staff pasting customer details into a public GenAI chatbot is:

options.A: The chatbot's answer may be too short to be useful for the customer
options.B: Confidential customer data may be stored or used by an external provider, causing a data breach
options.C: The browser may crash if large amounts of text are pasted into the chat
options.D: The chatbot may respond slowly when many staff members use it at the same time during peak hours

questions.answer_text: Confidential customer data may be stored or used by an external provider, causing a data breach
questions.explanation: Banks should use approved, enterprise AI tools with data protection agreements.

questions.question: AI bias in a credit-scoring model mainly arises from:

options.A: Biased or unrepresentative training data leading to unfair outcomes for certain groups
options.B: Hosting the model on too few servers, which delays credit decisions
options.C: Serving the model over HTTPS, which changes the input data in transit
options.D: Running the model on servers with too little RAM, which causes random errors in the scores

questions.answer_text: Biased or unrepresentative training data leading to unfair outcomes for certain groups
questions.explanation: Fairness testing and diverse data reduce discriminatory outcomes.

questions.question: Deepfakes pose a risk to banks mainly because they can be used to:

options.A: Impersonate customers or executives in video KYC or voice-based fraud
options.B: Speed up loan processing by generating supporting documents automatically
options.C: Encrypt customer data using AI-generated keys
options.D: Improve network security by simulating attacker behaviour

questions.answer_text: Impersonate customers or executives in video KYC or voice-based fraud
questions.explanation: Liveness detection and multi-factor verification help counter deepfakes.

questions.question: Explainable AI (XAI) is particularly important in banking because:

options.A: It is required only for image-generation models used in marketing
options.B: It removes the need for training data because decisions are rule-based
options.C: It makes the models run much faster by removing all input features that are hard to explain
options.D: Decisions like loan rejection must be explainable to customers, auditors and regulators

questions.answer_text: Decisions like loan rejection must be explainable to customers, auditors and regulators
questions.explanation: Techniques like SHAP and LIME show which factors influenced a prediction.

questions.question: 'Human-in-the-loop' in AI systems means:

options.A: A human types every answer manually while the AI only records the conversation
options.B: No human is involved at any stage, so decisions are fully automated
options.C: A human reviews or approves AI outputs before important decisions are acted upon
options.D: The AI system monitors humans and approves their decisions before execution

questions.answer_text: A human reviews or approves AI outputs before important decisions are acted upon
questions.explanation: Recommended for high-impact decisions such as credit and fraud blocking.

questions.question: Which of the following is a core element of AI governance in a bank?

options.A: Allowing any team to deploy any AI tool quickly without any central review, testing or approval process
options.B: Maintaining an inventory of AI models with risk classification, validation and ongoing monitoring
options.C: Avoiding documentation of models so that competitors cannot learn about them
options.D: Using AI only for marketing campaigns so that regulatory risk is avoided

questions.answer_text: Maintaining an inventory of AI models with risk classification, validation and ongoing monitoring
questions.explanation: Model risk management covers development, validation, approval, monitoring and retirement.

questions.question: RBI's FREE-AI framework (August 2025) stands for:

options.A: Framework for Regulation of Emerging and Experimental Artificial Intelligence
options.B: Fair, Reliable, Explainable and Ethical AI
options.C: Framework for Responsible and Ethical Enablement of Artificial Intelligence
options.D: Financial Risk Evaluation and Estimation using AI

questions.answer_text: Framework for Responsible and Ethical Enablement of Artificial Intelligence
questions.explanation: It sets out principles ('Sutras') and recommendations for AI adoption by regulated entities.

questions.question: Under the EU AI Act's risk-based approach, AI systems used for creditworthiness assessment of individuals are classified as:

options.A: Not regulated
options.B: Unacceptable (banned)
options.C: High-risk
options.D: Minimal risk

questions.answer_text: High-risk
questions.explanation: High-risk systems need risk management, data governance, transparency and human oversight.

questions.question: A Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) consists of:

options.A: A retriever that finds documents and a generator that writes answers from them
options.B: Two identical networks that share weights and compare pairs of inputs
options.C: An encoder that compresses data and a decoder that reconstructs it from a latent space
options.D: A generator that creates fake samples and a discriminator that tries to detect them

questions.answer_text: A generator that creates fake samples and a discriminator that tries to detect them
questions.explanation: They train against each other until generated data looks realistic.

questions.question: In generative AI, VAE stands for:

options.A: Validated AI Environment
options.B: Virtual Analytics Engine
options.C: Variational Auto-Encoder
options.D: Vector Attention Encoder

questions.answer_text: Variational Auto-Encoder
questions.explanation: VAEs learn a compressed latent space from which new samples can be generated.

questions.question: Diffusion models (e.g. Stable Diffusion) generate images by:

options.A: Starting from random noise and removing noise step by step guided by the prompt
options.B: Compressing existing photos and blending them together into one image
options.C: Searching the internet for matching images and copying the closest match that it finds
options.D: Drawing the image pixel by pixel from left to right using fixed rules

questions.answer_text: Starting from random noise and removing noise step by step guided by the prompt
questions.explanation: They learned to reverse a process of gradually adding noise to training images.

questions.question: Which of the following is a major challenge for Natural Language Processing (NLP) in Indian banking?

options.A: Ambiguity, context and code-mixed multilingual text (e.g. Hinglish)
options.B: Too few languages being used by Indian customers
options.C: NLP systems being able to process only numeric data
options.D: A complete lack of digital text data in Indian banks for training models

questions.answer_text: Ambiguity, context and code-mixed multilingual text (e.g. Hinglish)
questions.explanation: Sarcasm, spelling variations and domain jargon also reduce NLP accuracy.

questions.question: Using ML to flag a card transaction that is very different from the customer's usual pattern (location, amount, time) is an example of:

options.A: Data compression
options.B: Anomaly detection
options.C: Image classification
options.D: Machine translation

questions.answer_text: Anomaly detection
questions.explanation: Real-time anomaly detection is widely used for fraud prevention.

questions.question: MuleHunter.AI, announced by RBI in December 2024, is an AI model meant to:

options.A: Generate personalised marketing content for bank customers
options.B: Detect mule bank accounts used to route fraud proceeds
options.C: Process and route UPI transactions between banks
options.D: Price government securities in the primary auction

questions.answer_text: Detect mule bank accounts used to route fraud proceeds
questions.explanation: It was developed by the Reserve Bank Innovation Hub (RBIH) and piloted with banks.

questions.question: An AI chatbot on a bank's website mainly helps by:

options.A: Answering common customer queries 24x7 and routing complex cases to human agents
options.B: Replacing all branch and call-centre staff with fully automated responses
options.C: Storing customer passwords so that they can be reminded when forgotten
options.D: Approving all loan applications automatically without any human review

questions.answer_text: Answering common customer queries 24x7 and routing complex cases to human agents
questions.explanation: Chatbots reduce call-centre load and improve response times.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the commonly cited 5 Vs of Big Data?

options.A: Volume
options.B: Veracity
options.C: Velocity
options.D: Variety

questions.answer_text: Vulnerability
questions.explanation: The 5 Vs: Volume, Velocity, Variety, Veracity and Value.

questions.question: In Big Data, 'Veracity' refers to:

options.A: The different formats and types of data collected
options.B: The speed at which data is generated and arrives
options.C: The trustworthiness, accuracy and quality of the data
options.D: The total size of data stored by the organisation

questions.answer_text: The trustworthiness, accuracy and quality of the data
questions.explanation: Poor-quality data leads to wrong insights, so cleansing and validation are essential.

questions.question: The continuous flow of millions of UPI transactions per minute mainly illustrates which V of Big Data?

options.A: Veracity
options.B: Velocity
options.C: Value
options.D: Variety

questions.answer_text: Velocity
questions.explanation: Velocity is the speed of data generation and the need to process it quickly.

questions.question: 'Variety' in Big Data refers to:

options.A: The total amount of data stored across all the systems
options.B: Different types of data - structured, semi-structured and unstructured
options.C: The speed at which data is generated and must be processed by the bank's systems
options.D: The accuracy and trustworthiness of the data being collected

questions.answer_text: Different types of data - structured, semi-structured and unstructured
questions.explanation: Banks handle tables, JSON/XML messages, emails, call recordings, images and logs.

questions.question: JSON and XML documents are examples of:

options.A: Unstructured data
options.B: Binary data only
options.C: Structured data
options.D: Semi-structured data

questions.answer_text: Semi-structured data
questions.explanation: They have tags/keys giving some structure but no fixed relational schema.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of unstructured data?

options.A: A table of account balances
options.B: A CSV file of transactions
options.C: A relational table of branch codes
options.D: Customer call-centre voice recordings

questions.answer_text: Customer call-centre voice recordings
questions.explanation: Images, video, audio, emails and free text are unstructured.

questions.question: The 'Value' dimension of Big Data emphasises that:

options.A: Data must always be priced and sold to generate revenue for the bank
options.B: Data must be stored forever because its value can never be predicted
options.C: Only numeric data has value, while text and images should be discarded
options.D: Data is useful only when it produces meaningful business insights or benefits

questions.answer_text: Data is useful only when it produces meaningful business insights or benefits
questions.explanation: Collecting data without extracting value only adds cost and risk.

questions.question: Apache Hadoop is:

options.A: An open-source framework for distributed storage and processing of very large data sets on clusters of commodity hardware
options.B: A network security appliance that inspects large volumes of traffic in real time on enterprise networks
options.C: A programming language created specifically for writing statistical and machine learning programs
options.D: A commercial relational database from Oracle designed for very large OLTP workloads on expensive high-end clustered servers

questions.answer_text: An open-source framework for distributed storage and processing of very large data sets on clusters of commodity hardware
questions.explanation: Core components: HDFS (storage), YARN (resource management) and MapReduce (processing).

questions.question: In HDFS, which node stores the file system metadata (file names, block locations)?

options.A: Secondary storage node
options.B: Edge node
options.C: DataNode
options.D: NameNode

questions.answer_text: NameNode
questions.explanation: DataNodes store the actual data blocks and report to the NameNode.

questions.question: The default HDFS block size in Hadoop 2.x/3.x is:

options.A: 4 KB
options.B: 128 MB
options.C: 64 KB
options.D: 1 GB

questions.answer_text: 128 MB
questions.explanation: Large blocks reduce metadata and suit big sequential reads (it was 64 MB in Hadoop 1.x).

questions.question: The default replication factor of data blocks in HDFS is:
questions.explanation: Copies are spread across nodes (and racks) so the failure of a node does not lose data.

questions.question: HDFS is best suited for:

options.A: Data that must be stored only in RAM for the fastest possible access
options.B: Very large files written once and read many times in large sequential scans
options.C: Millions of tiny files that are updated randomly many times a second by many users
options.D: Low-latency OLTP transactions such as ATM withdrawals and transfers

questions.answer_text: Very large files written once and read many times in large sequential scans
questions.explanation: Many small files overload the NameNode's memory with metadata.

questions.question: A 600 MB file is being loaded into HDFS. After 200 MB is written, another client tries to read the file. What happens?

options.A: The reader receives a corrupted copy of the whole file, because HDFS mixes old and new blocks while a write is in progress
options.B: The read is always rejected with an error until the upload finishes, because HDFS locks every file against all readers while it is still being written by a client
options.C: The reader immediately sees the complete 600 MB file, because HDFS reserves and pre-fills all blocks before the upload starts
options.D: The reader can see the blocks already completely written, but data still being written is not guaranteed to be visible until flushed or the file is closed

questions.answer_text: The reader can see the blocks already completely written, but data still being written is not guaranteed to be visible until flushed or the file is closed
questions.explanation: HDFS follows a single-writer, multiple-reader model with relaxed visibility for files under construction.

questions.question: YARN in Hadoop is responsible for:

options.A: Running SQL-like queries on Hadoop data
options.B: Storing and replicating data blocks on DataNodes
options.C: Importing tables from relational databases
options.D: Cluster resource management and job scheduling

questions.answer_text: Cluster resource management and job scheduling
questions.explanation: YARN = Yet Another Resource Negotiator.

questions.question: What is the correct order of phases in a MapReduce job?

options.A: Reduce -> Map -> Shuffle
options.B: Sort -> Map -> Reduce -> Shuffle
options.C: Map -> Shuffle and Sort -> Reduce
options.D: Shuffle -> Reduce -> Map

questions.answer_text: Map -> Shuffle and Sort -> Reduce
questions.explanation: Map produces key-value pairs; shuffle groups them by key; reduce aggregates each group.

questions.question: Apache Spark is usually much faster than classic MapReduce because it:

options.A: Runs on a single powerful machine instead of a cluster, avoiding network overhead
options.B: Processes data in memory instead of writing intermediate results to disk
options.C: Stores data on tape, which is faster for large sequential reads
options.D: Avoids parallel processing, which removes coordination overhead

questions.answer_text: Processes data in memory instead of writing intermediate results to disk
questions.explanation: Spark also supports SQL, streaming and machine learning libraries.

questions.question: Which tool provides a SQL-like query language (HiveQL) on data stored in Hadoop?

options.A: Apache Sqoop
options.B: Apache ZooKeeper
options.C: Apache Hive
options.D: Apache Flume

questions.answer_text: Apache Hive
questions.explanation: Hive acts as a data warehouse layer on top of HDFS.

questions.question: HBase is:

options.A: A workflow scheduler that chains Hadoop jobs into pipelines
options.B: A tool that collects log data from servers and moves it into HDFS
options.C: A SQL query engine that converts HiveQL queries into batch MapReduce or Tez jobs on HDFS
options.D: A column-oriented NoSQL database on top of HDFS for real-time random read/write

questions.answer_text: A column-oriented NoSQL database on top of HDFS for real-time random read/write
questions.explanation: It is modelled on Google's Bigtable.

questions.question: Data transfer between relational databases (RDBMS) and Hadoop is done using:

options.A: Apache Pig
options.B: Apache Kafka
options.C: Apache Sqoop
options.D: Apache Flume

questions.answer_text: Apache Sqoop
questions.explanation: Sqoop = 'SQL to Hadoop'; it imports/exports tables in bulk.

questions.question: Apache Flume is mainly used to:

options.A: Transfer tables in bulk between relational databases and HDFS
options.B: Run SQL-like queries over data stored in the Hadoop cluster
options.C: Collect, aggregate and move large volumes of log/event data into HDFS
options.D: Coordinate configuration and leader election for distributed services

questions.answer_text: Collect, aggregate and move large volumes of log/event data into HDFS
questions.explanation: Sqoop handles RDBMS data; Flume handles streaming log data.

questions.question: Apache Kafka is best described as:

options.A: A distributed event-streaming platform for publishing and subscribing to real-time data streams
options.B: A relational database designed for storing customer and account master data with full ACID support
options.C: A compression utility that reduces the size of files stored in HDFS
options.D: A business intelligence tool for building dashboards and management reports

questions.answer_text: A distributed event-streaming platform for publishing and subscribing to real-time data streams
questions.explanation: Banks use Kafka for real-time transaction feeds, fraud alerts and CDC pipelines.

questions.question: Apache ZooKeeper in the Hadoop ecosystem provides:

options.A: Coordination services like configuration, naming, synchronisation and leader election
options.B: Masking of sensitive data before it is loaded
options.C: Storage of HDFS data blocks with three-way replication across racks for fault tolerance
options.D: Visual dashboards for monitoring cluster health

questions.answer_text: Coordination services like configuration, naming, synchronisation and leader election
questions.explanation: Many distributed systems (HBase, older Kafka) depend on it.

questions.question: Which Hadoop ecosystem tool is a workflow scheduler for managing Hadoop jobs?

options.A: Apache HBase
options.B: Apache Hive
options.C: Apache Sqoop
options.D: Apache Oozie

questions.answer_text: Apache Oozie
questions.explanation: Oozie chains MapReduce, Hive, Pig and Sqoop jobs into workflows.

questions.question: End-of-day interest calculation over all accounts is ____ processing, while blocking a suspicious card transaction within milliseconds needs ____ processing.

options.A: Stream; batch
options.B: Manual; batch
options.C: Real-time; manual
options.D: Batch; stream (real-time)

questions.answer_text: Batch; stream (real-time)
questions.explanation: Stream processing tools include Kafka Streams, Spark Streaming and Flink.

questions.question: The Lambda architecture for Big Data combines:

options.A: A batch layer for complete accurate views and a speed layer for real-time views
options.B: Two relational databases kept in sync using synchronous replication
options.C: Only a speed layer that processes every event in real time with no batch views
options.D: Only a batch layer that recomputes all views once a day with no real-time layer

questions.answer_text: A batch layer for complete accurate views and a speed layer for real-time views
questions.explanation: A serving layer merges results; Kappa architecture uses only streaming.

questions.question: Which of the following matches the NoSQL database type with an example correctly?

options.A: Document - Neo4j; Graph - MongoDB; Key-value - Cassandra; Column - Redis
options.B: Document - Redis; Key-value - MongoDB; Graph - Cassandra; Column - Neo4j
options.C: All four are relational databases
options.D: Document - MongoDB; Key-value - Redis; Column-family - Cassandra; Graph - Neo4j

questions.answer_text: Document - MongoDB; Key-value - Redis; Column-family - Cassandra; Graph - Neo4j
questions.explanation: NoSQL databases trade rigid schemas and joins for scalability and flexibility.

questions.question: A graph database is particularly useful in banking for:

options.A: Storing scanned images of cheques and KYC documents
options.B: Generating monthly account statements for customers
options.C: Detecting fraud rings by analysing relationships between accounts, devices and people
options.D: Calculating daily interest accruals on millions of savings accounts in the end-of-day batch

questions.answer_text: Detecting fraud rings by analysing relationships between accounts, devices and people
questions.explanation: Graph queries easily follow links like shared phone numbers or beneficiaries.

questions.question: According to the CAP theorem, during a network partition a distributed database must choose between:

options.A: Capacity and Partition tolerance
options.B: Consistency and Availability
options.C: Cost and Performance
options.D: Compression and Archiving

questions.answer_text: Consistency and Availability
questions.explanation: Partition tolerance is unavoidable in distributed systems, so the trade-off is C vs A.

questions.question: The four characteristics of a data warehouse (as defined by Bill Inmon) are:

options.A: Subject-oriented, integrated, time-variant and non-volatile
options.B: Volatile, transactional, real-time and fully normalised to 3NF
options.C: Encrypted, compressed, replicated and mirrored
options.D: Fast, cheap, small and simple

questions.answer_text: Subject-oriented, integrated, time-variant and non-volatile
questions.explanation: Non-volatile: data is loaded and read, not updated by daily transactions.

questions.question: How does OLTP differ from OLAP?

options.A: OLTP and OLAP are two names for the same type of system used by different vendors
options.B: OLAP handles many short day-to-day transactions; OLTP runs complex analytical queries on historical data
options.C: OLTP handles many short day-to-day transactions; OLAP runs complex analytical queries on historical data
options.D: OLTP is used only for management reporting, while OLAP is used for ATM and branch transactions

questions.answer_text: OLTP handles many short day-to-day transactions; OLAP runs complex analytical queries on historical data
questions.explanation: CBS is an OLTP system; the data warehouse supports OLAP.

questions.question: A data lake typically:

options.A: Is an in-memory cache that holds only the most recent data for fast dashboard queries
options.B: Stores only cleaned, structured data that must fit a fixed schema before loading (schema-on-write)
options.C: Stores raw data in its native format and applies structure only when data is read (schema-on-read)
options.D: Can store only structured data from relational systems and not images, logs or documents

questions.answer_text: Stores raw data in its native format and applies structure only when data is read (schema-on-read)
questions.explanation: Without governance, a data lake can become a 'data swamp'.

questions.question: A data lakehouse is an architecture that:

options.A: Replaces both data lakes and warehouses with spreadsheets shared among business users across departments
options.B: Combines the low-cost, flexible storage of a data lake with warehouse features like ACID transactions and schema management
options.C: Keeps raw data only in its native format with no schema management or transaction support of any kind
options.D: Stores only structured OLTP data in a relational database and copies it to a data lake once a year for long-term archival purposes

questions.answer_text: Combines the low-cost, flexible storage of a data lake with warehouse features like ACID transactions and schema management
questions.explanation: Open table formats such as Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg and Hudi enable lakehouses.

questions.question: In ELT (as opposed to ETL):

options.A: Data is only extracted from sources and reports are run directly against the extracts
options.B: Raw data is loaded into the target first and transformed there using the target platform's compute
options.C: Data is transformed on a separate server first and only the cleaned data is loaded into the target
options.D: No transformation is done at all, so the target always contains only raw source data

questions.answer_text: Raw data is loaded into the target first and transformed there using the target platform's compute
questions.explanation: ELT suits scalable cloud warehouses and data lakes.

questions.question: A data mart is:

options.A: The complete enterprise data warehouse covering all subjects
options.B: An OLTP database used for daily customer transactions
options.C: A subset of data focused on a specific business area or department
options.D: A marketplace where organisations buy and sell data

questions.answer_text: A subset of data focused on a specific business area or department
questions.explanation: Dependent data marts are fed from the central DWH; independent ones draw directly from sources.

questions.question: MOLAP differs from ROLAP in that MOLAP:

options.A: Queries relational tables directly, while ROLAP stores pre-aggregated data in multidimensional cubes for fast queries
options.B: Stores pre-aggregated data in multidimensional cubes for fast queries, while ROLAP queries relational tables directly
options.C: Is used only for OLTP processing, while ROLAP is used only for analytical processing
options.D: Cannot aggregate data at all, so every query is answered from detailed transaction records

questions.answer_text: Stores pre-aggregated data in multidimensional cubes for fast queries, while ROLAP queries relational tables directly
questions.explanation: MOLAP is faster for fixed analyses; ROLAP scales better to large detailed data. HOLAP combines both.

questions.question: In OLAP, moving from yearly totals to quarterly and then monthly figures is called:

options.A: Roll-up
options.B: Pivot
options.C: Slice
options.D: Drill-down

questions.answer_text: Drill-down
questions.explanation: Roll-up aggregates to a higher level; slice selects one value of a dimension; dice selects a sub-cube.

questions.question: Data scrubbing (data cleansing) means:

options.A: Detecting and correcting inaccurate, incomplete or duplicate data
options.B: Compressing data to reduce storage costs
options.C: Encrypting sensitive data before loading it
options.D: Deleting all records that are older than the bank's defined retention period

questions.answer_text: Detecting and correcting inaccurate, incomplete or duplicate data
questions.explanation: It is a key step in ETL before loading into a warehouse.

questions.question: How is data mining different from a data warehouse?

options.A: A data warehouse stores integrated historical data; data mining discovers hidden patterns from such data
options.B: Data mining stores integrated historical data; a data warehouse discovers hidden patterns from it
options.C: A data warehouse and data mining are the same activity described with different names
options.D: Data mining deletes old data from the warehouse to keep it small and fast

questions.answer_text: A data warehouse stores integrated historical data; data mining discovers hidden patterns from such data
questions.explanation: Data mining uses techniques like classification, clustering and association rules.

questions.question: Finding that customers who take a home loan often also buy home insurance is an example of:

options.A: Association rule mining (market basket analysis)
options.B: Linear regression on loan amounts
options.C: Clustering of customers by age group
