options.D: Classification of loans into default/non-default

questions.answer_text: Association rule mining (market basket analysis)
questions.explanation: Banks use such insights for cross-selling.

questions.question: Which is a typical use of data mining in banking?

options.A: Configuring routers and switches in the bank's network
options.B: Predicting customer churn and identifying cross-sell opportunities
options.C: Assigning IP addresses to branch computers automatically using DHCP
options.D: Printing passbooks and account statements for customers

questions.answer_text: Predicting customer churn and identifying cross-sell opportunities
questions.explanation: Other uses: credit scoring, fraud detection, customer segmentation.

questions.question: Match the type of analytics with the question it answers: (P) Descriptive (Q) Diagnostic (R) Predictive (S) Prescriptive | (1) What will happen? (2) What should we do? (3) What happened? (4) Why did it happen?
questions.explanation: Value and complexity increase from descriptive to prescriptive analytics.

questions.question: Business Intelligence (BI) refers to:

options.A: Monitoring of network devices and servers for performance problems
options.B: Tools and processes that turn data into reports, dashboards and insights for decision-making
options.C: Recruitment of highly skilled analysts for the bank's strategy, planning and research departments
options.D: Encryption of business data before it is shared with external partners

questions.answer_text: Tools and processes that turn data into reports, dashboards and insights for decision-making
questions.explanation: Examples of BI tools: Power BI, Tableau, Qlik, Oracle BI.

questions.question: Web usage mining analyses:

options.A: The HTML and JavaScript source code of web pages for quality issues
options.B: The network cables and switches that connect web servers to the internet
options.C: Web server logs and clickstream data to discover how users navigate a website
options.D: Only the hyperlink structure between web pages to rank their importance

questions.answer_text: Web server logs and clickstream data to discover how users navigate a website
questions.explanation: It helps improve website design and personalisation.

questions.question: Data governance is best described as:

options.A: A technique for compressing data so that it takes less space in the data warehouse
options.B: The purchase of additional storage capacity whenever data volumes grow beyond the current limits of the systems
options.C: A type of database designed for storing policies and regulatory documents
options.D: The policies, roles, standards and processes for managing data quality, security, privacy and ownership

questions.answer_text: The policies, roles, standards and processes for managing data quality, security, privacy and ownership
questions.explanation: Good governance is essential for regulatory reporting and analytics trust.

questions.question: Data lineage refers to:

options.A: Measuring the speed at which data moves between two systems
options.B: Tracking where data originated and how it has been transformed and moved across systems
options.C: Recording the family history of customers for relationship-based marketing and cross-selling
options.D: Maintaining the physical order of rows inside a database table

questions.answer_text: Tracking where data originated and how it has been transformed and moved across systems
questions.explanation: Lineage helps in audits, impact analysis and root-cause analysis of data errors.

questions.question: Metadata is:

options.A: Extremely large data sets that cannot fit on a single server
options.B: Data that has been encrypted for secure storage
options.C: Data about data, such as its definition, source, format and owner
options.D: Data that has been deleted but can still be recovered

questions.answer_text: Data about data, such as its definition, source, format and owner
questions.explanation: A data catalogue stores metadata so users can find and understand data.

questions.question: A data steward is responsible for:

options.A: Writing and maintaining the operating system of database servers
options.B: Selling the organisation's data to third parties at the best price
options.C: Physically guarding the data centre and controlling entry of staff and visitors to server rooms
options.D: Ensuring the quality, definitions and proper use of data in a specific business domain

questions.answer_text: Ensuring the quality, definitions and proper use of data in a specific business domain
questions.explanation: Data owners are accountable; stewards handle day-to-day data quality management.

questions.question: A blockchain is best described as:

options.A: A backup format in which transaction tapes are chained together for long-term archival
options.B: A central database owned by one bank in which records can be freely edited by administrators
options.C: A distributed, append-only ledger where blocks of transactions are linked using cryptographic hashes
options.D: A network of firewalls that block transactions coming from unknown or blacklisted sources

questions.answer_text: A distributed, append-only ledger where blocks of transactions are linked using cryptographic hashes
questions.explanation: Copies of the ledger are kept by many nodes, and consensus decides which blocks are added.

questions.question: The first block of a blockchain is called the:

options.A: Genesis block
options.B: Root block
options.C: Master block
options.D: Origin hash

questions.answer_text: Genesis block
questions.explanation: Bitcoin's genesis block was mined in January 2009.

questions.question: Altering a transaction in an old block is easily detected because:

options.A: Each block stores the hash of the previous block, so changing one block breaks all following links
options.B: Each block is printed and stored on paper by every participant for later physical verification
options.C: Old blocks are deleted daily, so any change would have to be made within a single day
options.D: Each block is encrypted with the user's password, so only that user can change old records

questions.answer_text: Each block stores the hash of the previous block, so changing one block breaks all following links
questions.explanation: An attacker would have to recompute all subsequent blocks and out-pace the honest network.

questions.question: Blockchain is considered trustworthy without a central authority mainly because of:

options.A: A single trusted administrator who approves every block before it is added
options.B: Decentralised copies, cryptographic hashing and consensus among participants
options.C: Strong passwords and two-factor authentication for every participant
options.D: Daily backups of the ledger kept by a central clearing house

questions.answer_text: Decentralised copies, cryptographic hashing and consensus among participants
questions.explanation: Trust shifts from an intermediary to the protocol and the network.

questions.question: How does Proof of Stake (PoS) differ from Proof of Work (PoW)?

options.A: PoS uses more electricity than PoW because every node must validate every transaction twice
options.B: PoS requires validators to solve harder cryptographic puzzles than PoW miners, using more computing power
options.C: PoS selects validators based on the cryptocurrency they lock up as stake, using far less energy than PoW mining
options.D: PoS has no validators at all; blocks are added automatically by the network after a fixed time

questions.answer_text: PoS selects validators based on the cryptocurrency they lock up as stake, using far less energy than PoW mining
questions.explanation: Ethereum switched from PoW to PoS in September 2022 ('The Merge').

questions.question: In Proof of Work mining, the miner repeatedly changes which value until the block hash meets the difficulty target?

options.A: Nonce
options.B: Merkle root
options.C: Genesis hash
options.D: Public key

questions.answer_text: Nonce
questions.explanation: Finding a valid nonce requires massive trial-and-error hashing.

questions.question: A Merkle tree in a blockchain block is used to:

options.A: Store the private keys of all the users whose transactions are recorded in that block
options.B: Encrypt the contents of the block so that only participants can read them
options.C: Efficiently summarise and verify all transactions in the block with a single root hash
options.D: Randomly choose which miner or validator will create the next block

questions.answer_text: Efficiently summarise and verify all transactions in the block with a single root hash
questions.explanation: A transaction's inclusion can be proved with a short Merkle path.

questions.question: A smart contract is:

options.A: A legal agreement signed digitally on paper and stored as a PDF in a shared folder
options.B: An insurance policy that covers losses from cryptocurrency theft
options.C: A service level agreement between a bank and its cloud service provider
options.D: Self-executing code stored on a blockchain that runs automatically when conditions are met

questions.answer_text: Self-executing code stored on a blockchain that runs automatically when conditions are met
questions.explanation: Used for automated escrow, trade finance and token transfers.

questions.question: Hyperledger Fabric is preferred by banks for consortium use cases because it is:

options.A: A permissioned blockchain where participants are known and access is controlled
options.B: A relational database with a blockchain-style user interface on top
options.C: A public permissionless network where anyone can join and mine anonymously
options.D: A mining pool that shares Bitcoin rewards among member banks

questions.answer_text: A permissioned blockchain where participants are known and access is controlled
questions.explanation: Permissioned networks offer privacy, governance and higher throughput.

questions.question: A '51% attack' on a blockchain means:

options.A: Transaction fees on the network increase by 51% whenever demand for block space is high
options.B: Half of the blocks in the chain are deleted automatically when the ledger becomes too large
options.C: More than half of the network's users lose their private keys and can no longer access their funds
options.D: An entity controlling the majority of mining/validating power can rewrite recent history or double-spend

questions.answer_text: An entity controlling the majority of mining/validating power can rewrite recent history or double-spend
questions.explanation: Large, decentralised networks make this very expensive.

questions.question: How is Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) related to blockchain?

options.A: DLT always requires mining, whereas blockchain never does
options.B: They are completely unrelated technologies used for different purposes
options.C: Blockchain is one type of DLT that organises records into a chain of blocks
options.D: DLT is one type of blockchain that does not use cryptographic hashing

questions.answer_text: Blockchain is one type of DLT that organises records into a chain of blocks
questions.explanation: Other DLTs (e.g. DAG-based) do not use a chain of blocks.

questions.question: Bitcoin uses which hash function for mining and block linking?

options.A: AES-128
options.B: RSA
options.C: MD5
options.D: SHA-256

questions.answer_text: SHA-256
questions.explanation: Bitcoin was proposed by the pseudonymous Satoshi Nakamoto in 2008; supply is capped at 21 million.

questions.question: Which banking use case is commonly cited for blockchain?

options.A: Counting and sorting cash at branches at the end of each business day
options.B: Resetting forgotten internet banking passwords for retail customers
options.C: Printing passbooks and account statements at branches for walk-in customers on demand at the counter
options.D: Trade finance documentation (letters of credit) shared among banks, exporters and importers

questions.answer_text: Trade finance documentation (letters of credit) shared among banks, exporters and importers
questions.explanation: Shared, tamper-evident records reduce paperwork, delays and fraud like duplicate financing.

questions.question: The Internet of Things (IoT) refers to:

options.A: Physical devices with sensors and connectivity that collect and exchange data over networks
options.B: A new version of the Internet Protocol designed to replace IPv6 addressing
options.C: Online shopping websites that sell connected gadgets to consumers
options.D: Smartphones and tablets used by customers to access internet and mobile banking applications

questions.answer_text: Physical devices with sensors and connectivity that collect and exchange data over networks
questions.explanation: Examples: smart meters, connected ATMs, wearables, vehicle trackers.

questions.question: MQTT is widely used in IoT because it is:

options.A: A lightweight embedded database engine that runs on sensors and gateways
options.B: A video compression codec used for streaming camera feeds from devices
options.C: A lightweight publish/subscribe messaging protocol suited to low-bandwidth, unreliable networks
options.D: A heavy XML-based protocol that guarantees delivery using full two-phase commit transaction support

questions.answer_text: A lightweight publish/subscribe messaging protocol suited to low-bandwidth, unreliable networks
questions.explanation: MQTT runs over TCP (port 1883, or 8883 with TLS) via a broker.

questions.question: CoAP (Constrained Application Protocol) differs from HTTP in that it:

options.A: Is designed for constrained IoT devices and runs over UDP
options.B: Requires a graphical user interface on each device
options.C: Runs only over TCP and uses large text-based headers
options.D: Is used only for exchanging email between IoT devices

questions.answer_text: Is designed for constrained IoT devices and runs over UDP
questions.explanation: CoAP uses REST-like methods with very small overhead.

questions.question: The Mirai botnet (2016) was able to launch huge DDoS attacks mainly because:

options.A: Many IoT devices used default or weak passwords
options.B: Internet routers were configured to block all traffic
options.C: IoT devices had far more memory than normal PCs
options.D: All the infected devices used IPv6 addresses

questions.answer_text: Many IoT devices used default or weak passwords
questions.explanation: Changing default credentials and patching firmware are basic IoT security steps.

questions.question: NFC (Near Field Communication), used in contactless card and phone payments, works over a range of about:

options.A: 100 metres
options.B: A few centimetres
options.C: 1 kilometre
options.D: 10 metres

questions.answer_text: A few centimetres
questions.explanation: The short range makes accidental or remote reading harder.

questions.question: A 'digital twin' is:

options.A: A virtual model of a physical object or process, updated with real-time data for monitoring and simulation
options.B: A backup copy of a production database kept on a second, identical server at the DR site for disaster recovery
options.C: A duplicate bank account opened fraudulently using a customer's stolen identity
options.D: A pair of identical user accounts created for the same employee in two applications

questions.answer_text: A virtual model of a physical object or process, updated with real-time data for monitoring and simulation
questions.explanation: Used for predictive maintenance, e.g. of data-centre cooling systems.

questions.question: Cloud-native applications are typically built using:

options.A: Single monolithic programs deployed on mainframes
options.B: Desktop applications installed on each user's PC
options.C: Microservices, containers, CI/CD and dynamic orchestration
options.D: Manual deployments on dedicated physical servers in the data centre

questions.answer_text: Microservices, containers, CI/CD and dynamic orchestration
questions.explanation: They are designed to scale, recover and update rapidly in cloud environments.

questions.question: Kubernetes is hosted and governed by which foundation?

options.A: Open Worldwide Application Security Project
options.B: Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF)
options.C: Information Systems Audit and Control Association
options.D: Apache Software Foundation (ASF)

questions.answer_text: Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF)
questions.explanation: CNCF is part of the Linux Foundation and hosts projects like Prometheus and Envoy.

questions.question: 'Immutable infrastructure' means:

options.A: Servers are never shut down or restarted, so that the infrastructure stays stable for years
options.B: Infrastructure cannot be monitored or changed by anyone once it has been deployed
options.C: Servers/containers are never modified in place; changes are made by replacing them with new versions
options.D: Data stored on the infrastructure can never be deleted, even after its retention period

questions.answer_text: Servers/containers are never modified in place; changes are made by replacing them with new versions
questions.explanation: It reduces configuration drift and makes rollbacks predictable.

questions.question: The three pillars of observability in cloud-native systems are:

options.A: CPU, RAM and disk
options.B: Users, roles and groups
options.C: HTML, CSS and JS
options.D: Logs, metrics and traces

questions.answer_text: Logs, metrics and traces
questions.explanation: Distributed tracing follows a request across many microservices.

questions.question: According to the Twelve-Factor App methodology, application configuration (like database URLs) should be:

options.A: Stored in the environment, separate from the code
options.B: Hard-coded in the source code of each service
options.C: Compiled into the binary at build time
options.D: Kept in the user's browser as a cookie

questions.answer_text: Stored in the environment, separate from the code
questions.explanation: The same build can then be promoted across dev, test and production.

questions.question: Edge computing means:

options.A: Using only the fastest CPUs available in the data centre for latency-sensitive workloads
options.B: Storing data only on the outer tracks of a hard disk, where read speeds are the highest
options.C: Running all computation on the perimeter firewall at the edge of the corporate network
options.D: Processing data close to where it is generated instead of sending everything to a central cloud

questions.answer_text: Processing data close to where it is generated instead of sending everything to a central cloud
questions.explanation: It reduces latency and bandwidth use.

questions.question: Which banking scenario benefits MOST from edge computing?

options.A: Preparing the bank's monthly profit and loss statement from data held in the general ledger system
options.B: Real-time video analytics at ATMs to detect tampering without sending all video to the data centre
options.C: Storing archived customer statements for ten years to meet record-keeping requirements
options.D: Compiling the annual audit report from data collected across all branches and departments

questions.answer_text: Real-time video analytics at ATMs to detect tampering without sending all video to the data centre
questions.explanation: Local processing gives instant response even with limited network bandwidth.

questions.question: Fog computing refers to:

options.A: A type of encryption that obscures data so that it cannot be read in transit
options.B: An intermediate layer of computing and storage between edge devices and the central cloud
options.C: Computing carried out only during bad weather when satellite links are unavailable
options.D: Cloud storage located in very cold regions to reduce data-centre cooling costs

questions.answer_text: An intermediate layer of computing and storage between edge devices and the central cloud
questions.explanation: Fog nodes aggregate and pre-process data from many edge devices.

questions.question: 5G is considered a major improvement over 4G mainly because of:

options.A: Much higher speeds, very low latency and support for massive numbers of connected devices
options.B: Use of only lower frequency bands, which gives every user the same fixed speed
options.C: Use of copper cables instead of radio waves for faster mobile data connections
options.D: Longer battery life for all phones because 5G radios consume no power at all when they are idle

questions.answer_text: Much higher speeds, very low latency and support for massive numbers of connected devices
questions.explanation: Low latency and network slicing enable real-time IoT and edge applications.

questions.question: MEC (Multi-access Edge Computing) in 5G networks means:

options.A: A brand of 5G smartphone designed for enterprise users who need very long battery life
options.B: Computing resources placed within the telecom operator's network near the radio access, giving ultra-low latency
options.C: An email encryption standard used by telecom operators to protect messages over 5G
options.D: A billing model in which cloud providers charge customers based on the amount of mobile data that they use each month

questions.answer_text: Computing resources placed within the telecom operator's network near the radio access, giving ultra-low latency
questions.explanation: Applications run close to users instead of in distant data centres.

questions.question: Robotic Process Automation (RPA) uses:

options.A: Physical robots deployed in branches to greet customers and guide them to counters
options.B: Hardware machines that automate cash counting and note sorting in currency chests
options.C: AI systems that learn every task from data without needing any rules or process steps
options.D: Software bots that mimic human actions on application screens to perform rule-based tasks

questions.answer_text: Software bots that mimic human actions on application screens to perform rule-based tasks
questions.explanation: Bots log in, read, type, click and move data between systems.

questions.question: Which process is the BEST candidate for RPA?

options.A: Handling a customer's emotional complaint about a disputed transaction
options.B: High-volume, rule-based and repetitive tasks with structured inputs, like daily reconciliation
options.C: Negotiating loan terms with a customer who is asking for a lower interest rate at the time of renewal
options.D: Designing a new product strategy for the bank's retail lending business

questions.answer_text: High-volume, rule-based and repetitive tasks with structured inputs, like daily reconciliation
questions.explanation: Stable, well-defined processes give the best automation return.

questions.question: What is the difference between attended and unattended RPA bots?

options.A: Attended bots run on servers without any human involvement; unattended bots need a user to trigger and supervise every step
options.B: There is no difference; the two terms are used interchangeably by different RPA vendors
options.C: Both attended and unattended bots are physical robots, differing only in whether a supervisor is present
options.D: Attended bots work alongside a user on their desktop when triggered; unattended bots run on their own on servers per schedule

questions.answer_text: Attended bots work alongside a user on their desktop when triggered; unattended bots run on their own on servers per schedule
questions.explanation: Unattended bots typically handle back-office batch processes.

questions.question: Which of the following is an RPA tool?

options.A: UiPath
options.B: Nmap
options.C: Oracle RMAN
options.D: Wireshark

questions.answer_text: UiPath
questions.explanation: Automation Anywhere and Blue Prism are other well-known RPA platforms.

questions.question: Combining RPA with AI capabilities like OCR, NLP and ML to handle unstructured inputs is called:

options.A: Server virtualization and consolidation
options.B: Batch job scheduling with cron
options.C: Intelligent Automation (Hyperautomation)
options.D: Manual processing with maker-checker

questions.answer_text: Intelligent Automation (Hyperautomation)
questions.explanation: Plain RPA follows fixed rules and cannot interpret unstructured documents by itself.

questions.question: RPA helps an organisation use its resources more efficiently mainly by:

options.A: Increasing the amount of manual data entry so that every transaction is checked twice by different staff members
options.B: Requiring more staff for each process so that bots can be supervised continuously
options.C: Freeing staff from repetitive work for higher-value tasks while bots work 24x7 with fewer errors
options.D: Removing the need for any IT systems because bots perform the work themselves

questions.answer_text: Freeing staff from repetitive work for higher-value tasks while bots work 24x7 with fewer errors
questions.explanation: Benefits include speed, accuracy, auditability and scalability.

questions.question: A common operational risk with RPA bots is that:

options.A: Bots cannot record any log of their actions, so audits of bot activity are impossible
options.B: Bots refuse to process transactions on weekends and public holidays by default
options.C: Bots break when application screens or processes change, and bot credentials need secure management
options.D: Bots slow down over time and must be restarted manually every hour to keep working accurately and reliably

questions.answer_text: Bots break when application screens or processes change, and bot credentials need secure management
questions.explanation: Bot accounts should follow least privilege and be governed like privileged IDs.

questions.question: A qubit differs from a classical bit because it:

options.A: Can exist in a superposition of 0 and 1 at the same time
options.B: Stores three states: 0, 1 and an error state
options.C: Can store only the value 0 until it is measured by the system
options.D: Is simply a faster version of a classical bit

questions.answer_text: Can exist in a superposition of 0 and 1 at the same time
questions.explanation: Measurement collapses the qubit to 0 or 1.

questions.question: Quantum entanglement means:

options.A: Each qubit is encrypted with a key that is shared with another qubit
options.B: The states of two or more qubits are linked so that measuring one instantly determines the state of the other
options.C: Two quantum computers share a single power supply and cooling system
options.D: The wires connecting the qubits are twisted together in pairs to reduce electrical interference and noise in the chip

questions.answer_text: The states of two or more qubits are linked so that measuring one instantly determines the state of the other
questions.explanation: Entanglement and superposition give quantum computers their power.

questions.question: Shor's algorithm on a large quantum computer threatens which cryptography?

options.A: Only passwords stored in plain text
options.B: Only hashing algorithms like SHA-256 and SHA-3
options.C: Public-key algorithms such as RSA and ECC
options.D: Only AES-256

questions.answer_text: Public-key algorithms such as RSA and ECC
questions.explanation: It can factor large numbers and solve discrete logarithms efficiently.

questions.question: Grover's algorithm effectively reduces the security of a symmetric key by about half (e.g. AES-128 to ~64-bit strength). The recommended response is to:

options.A: Use shorter keys to speed up re-keying
options.B: Use larger symmetric keys such as AES-256
options.C: Stop using symmetric encryption altogether
options.D: Switch from AES to MD5 for encryption

questions.answer_text: Use larger symmetric keys such as AES-256
questions.explanation: Symmetric crypto with doubled key length remains safe against known quantum attacks.

questions.question: 'Harvest now, decrypt later' refers to:

options.A: Adversaries collecting encrypted data today to decrypt it in future with quantum computers
options.B: Backing up encrypted data now and deleting the encryption keys at a later date
options.C: Attackers decrypting captured data immediately using cloud-based cracking services
options.D: Organisations collecting customer data now and deciding later how to use it for analytics

questions.answer_text: Adversaries collecting encrypted data today to decrypt it in future with quantum computers
questions.explanation: Long-life sensitive data needs migration to post-quantum cryptography early.

questions.question: Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) refers to:

options.A: Older algorithms such as DES and 3DES that were used before quantum computing
options.B: Encryption applied to data after a computer has been switched off and stored
options.C: New algorithms that run on classical computers but resist attacks from quantum computers
options.D: Cryptographic algorithms that can only run on quantum computers using many entangled qubits

questions.answer_text: New algorithms that run on classical computers but resist attacks from quantum computers
questions.explanation: NIST published its first PQC standards (FIPS 203, 204, 205) in August 2024.

questions.question: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) secures key exchange by:

options.A: Printing keys on paper and delivering them by hand to each communicating party
options.B: Using longer passwords that quantum computers cannot guess in a reasonable time
options.C: Sending keys by encrypted email so that only the intended receiver is able to open and use them
options.D: Using quantum physics so that any eavesdropping disturbs the transmitted states and is detected

questions.answer_text: Using quantum physics so that any eavesdropping disturbs the transmitted states and is detected
questions.explanation: QKD needs special hardware and has distance limitations.

questions.question: Quantum computers are not yet widely used mainly because:

options.A: Qubits are fragile (decoherence), error rates are high and many systems need extreme cooling
options.B: They cannot be connected to normal power supplies and need dedicated power plants
options.C: They are too cheap to manufacture, so vendors do not find it profitable to sell them
options.D: They already have too many stable qubits, which makes programming them very difficult

questions.answer_text: Qubits are fragile (decoherence), error rates are high and many systems need extreme cooling
questions.explanation: Error correction needs many physical qubits per logical qubit.

questions.question: Even though TLS 1.3 fixed many weaknesses of TLS 1.2, it is still considered vulnerable to future quantum computers because:

options.A: It depends on Telnet for the initial connection, which quantum computers can intercept easily
options.B: It still uses MD5 and SHA-1 for message integrity checks, which quantum computers are able to reverse almost instantly today
options.C: It sends data without encryption after the handshake, which quantum computers can read directly
options.D: Its key exchange (ECDHE) and certificate signatures rely on elliptic-curve/RSA mathematics that Shor's algorithm can break

questions.answer_text: Its key exchange (ECDHE) and certificate signatures rely on elliptic-curve/RSA mathematics that Shor's algorithm can break
questions.explanation: Hybrid post-quantum key exchange (e.g. combining X25519 with ML-KEM) is being deployed to address this.

questions.question: India's National Quantum Mission, approved by the Union Cabinet in 2023, aims to:

options.A: Build only classical supercomputers for weather forecasting and research
options.B: Replace the UPI payment system with a new quantum-secured national payment network by 2030
options.C: Ban research on quantum computing until international standards are finalised
options.D: Develop quantum computing, communication, sensing and materials capabilities in India

questions.answer_text: Develop quantum computing, communication, sensing and materials capabilities in India
questions.explanation: It has an outlay of about ₹6,000 crore over eight years.

questions.question: The RBI's Central Bank Digital Currency is called the:

options.A: Digital Rupee (e₹)
options.B: UPI Coin
options.C: RuPay Token
options.D: BharatCoin

questions.answer_text: Digital Rupee (e₹)
questions.explanation: It is legal tender issued by RBI in digital form.

questions.question: In CBDC-R, the 'R' stands for:

options.A: Reserve
options.B: Remittance
options.C: Regulated
options.D: Retail

questions.answer_text: Retail
questions.explanation: CBDC-W is Wholesale, for interbank settlement.

questions.question: RBI started the pilots of the wholesale (e₹-W) and retail (e₹-R) Digital Rupee in:

options.A: April 2024 and May 2024 respectively
options.B: January 2020 and March 2020 respectively
options.C: November 2022 and December 2022 respectively
options.D: December 2022 and November 2022 respectively

questions.answer_text: November 2022 and December 2022 respectively
questions.explanation: e₹-W pilot began on 1 November 2022 for government securities settlement; e₹-R on 1 December 2022.

questions.question: A key difference between CBDC and money in a UPI-linked bank account is that:

options.A: CBDC can be used only for cross-border payments, while UPI money can be used only within India
options.B: CBDC is a direct liability of the central bank, while a bank deposit is a liability of the commercial bank
options.C: CBDC is a private cryptocurrency issued by NPCI, while a bank deposit is a direct liability of the RBI itself
options.D: UPI money is issued directly by RBI, while CBDC is a liability of the customer's own bank

questions.answer_text: CBDC is a direct liability of the central bank, while a bank deposit is a liability of the commercial bank
questions.explanation: UPI moves bank deposits between accounts; e₹ is digital central bank money held in a wallet.

questions.question: UPI (Unified Payments Interface) is operated by:

options.A: National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI)
options.B: Institute for Development and Research in Banking Technology (IDRBT)
options.C: Reserve Bank Innovation Hub (RBIH)
options.D: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)

questions.answer_text: National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI)
questions.explanation: UPI was launched in 2016 and is regulated/overseen by RBI.

questions.question: 'Hello! UPI' launched by NPCI enables:

options.A: Payments only by scanning merchant QR codes
options.B: Conversational, voice-based UPI payments
options.C: Cheque deposits through the UPI app
options.D: UPI payments only for foreign tourists

questions.answer_text: Conversational, voice-based UPI payments
questions.explanation: Users can make payments by speaking instructions, improving inclusion.

questions.question: UPI 123PAY is designed for:

options.A: Smartphone users on 5G networks who want faster QR-based payments at merchant outlets
options.B: Non-resident Indians sending international remittances to India
options.C: Feature phone users, using IVR, missed calls or app-based options without internet
options.D: Corporate customers making bulk salary and vendor payments

questions.answer_text: Feature phone users, using IVR, missed calls or app-based options without internet
questions.explanation: It extends UPI to users without smartphones.

questions.question: UPI Lite is meant for:

options.A: Small-value payments from an on-device balance without entering the UPI PIN each time
options.B: Loans above ₹1 crore disbursed directly through a UPI-linked account
options.C: Clearing of cheques deposited through the mobile banking app
options.D: Large-value RTGS-style payments that settle individually, immediately and irrevocably in real time

questions.answer_text: Small-value payments from an on-device balance without entering the UPI PIN each time
questions.explanation: It reduces load on bank core systems and speeds up low-value transactions.

questions.question: 'UPI Circle', launched in 2024, allows:

options.A: Group chats between UPI users to split bills before making payments
options.B: Payments to be made only to beneficiaries within the same city or district as the payer's home branch
options.C: UPI payments to be made by people who do not hold any bank account at all
options.D: A primary user to delegate UPI payments to a trusted secondary user, with full or partial delegation

questions.answer_text: A primary user to delegate UPI payments to a trusted secondary user, with full or partial delegation
questions.explanation: Useful for family members who do not have their own bank accounts linked to UPI.

questions.question: The full form of USSD, used in *99# mobile banking, is:

options.A: Universal SIM Service Data
options.B: Unstructured Secure Supplementary Data
options.C: Unstructured Supplementary Service Data
options.D: Unified Secure Service Data

questions.answer_text: Unstructured Supplementary Service Data
questions.explanation: *99# works on basic phones without internet.

questions.question: Bharat QR is:

options.A: A QR code printed on cheques to speed up deposit and clearing at branches
options.B: An interoperable QR code standard developed by NPCI with card networks for merchant payments
options.C: A proprietary QR code that can be scanned only by the customers of one particular bank's mobile app
options.D: A government identity card with a QR code used for KYC verification at branches

questions.answer_text: An interoperable QR code standard developed by NPCI with card networks for merchant payments
questions.explanation: A single QR accepts payments from RuPay, Visa, Mastercard (and UPI).

questions.question: The main advantage of the Cheque Truncation System (CTS) is that:

options.A: The physical cheque does not travel; its image and data are used for clearing, making it faster, cheaper and safer
options.B: Cheques are collected and cleared only once a month, which reduces processing costs
options.C: Cheques no longer need the drawer's signature, since the image is verified automatically
options.D: Physical cheques are sent by courier to the drawee bank's branch, which makes the whole clearing process much more secure

questions.answer_text: The physical cheque does not travel; its image and data are used for clearing, making it faster, cheaper and safer
questions.explanation: CTS-2010 standard cheques have security features for image-based processing.

questions.question: In 2025, RBI moved CTS from batch clearing towards:

options.A: Discontinuing all cheques and replacing them completely with UPI payments
options.B: Monthly clearing cycles, so that all cheques are settled together at month end
options.C: Manual clearing at RBI regional offices, with physical presentation of every cheque
options.D: Continuous clearing with settlement on realisation, so cheques can be credited within hours

questions.answer_text: Continuous clearing with settlement on realisation, so cheques can be credited within hours
questions.explanation: Cheques are scanned and presented continuously during business hours instead of in fixed batches.

questions.question: Under RBI's Positive Pay System (from January 2021) for CTS, the issuer re-confirms key cheque details for cheques of:

options.A: ₹500 and above
options.B: ₹10 lakh and above only
options.C: ₹50,000 and above
options.D: Any amount above ₹1

questions.answer_text: ₹50,000 and above
questions.explanation: Banks may make it mandatory for cheques of ₹5 lakh and above.

questions.question: Which statement about NEFT and RTGS is correct?

options.A: Both NEFT and RTGS settle all transactions together only once a day at the end of business hours
options.B: RTGS has no minimum amount and settles in batches, while NEFT works only during branch working hours
options.C: RTGS settles in half-hourly batches; NEFT settles each transaction individually in real time with a ₹2 lakh minimum
options.D: NEFT settles in half-hourly batches; RTGS settles each transaction individually in real time with a ₹2 lakh minimum

questions.answer_text: NEFT settles in half-hourly batches; RTGS settles each transaction individually in real time with a ₹2 lakh minimum
questions.explanation: NEFT became 24x7 in December 2019 and RTGS in December 2020.

questions.question: IMPS (Immediate Payment Service) is:

options.A: A cheque clearing system based on images instead of physical cheques
options.B: An instant 24x7 interbank electronic fund transfer service operated by NPCI
options.C: A domestic card network used for debit and credit card payments
options.D: A deferred net settlement system operated by RBI in half-hourly batches

questions.answer_text: An instant 24x7 interbank electronic fund transfer service operated by NPCI
questions.explanation: IMPS is the foundation on which UPI was later built.

questions.question: NACH (National Automated Clearing House) is mainly used for:

options.A: Bulk and repetitive payments like salary credits, dividends and EMI/SIP mandates
options.B: Foreign exchange trading between banks and authorised dealers
options.C: Single high-value urgent transfers between banks that settle in real time
options.D: Card-present payments at merchant POS terminals in shops

questions.answer_text: Bulk and repetitive payments like salary credits, dividends and EMI/SIP mandates
questions.explanation: It replaced the older ECS system.

questions.question: AePS (Aadhaar enabled Payment System) allows customers to:

options.A: Clear cheques at any bank branch by quoting their Aadhaar number
options.B: Pay merchants only through credit cards linked to their Aadhaar number at POS terminals in shops and petrol pumps
options.C: Do basic banking at micro-ATMs/Business Correspondents using Aadhaar number and biometric authentication
options.D: Transfer money abroad using their Aadhaar number instead of a SWIFT code

questions.answer_text: Do basic banking at micro-ATMs/Business Correspondents using Aadhaar number and biometric authentication
questions.explanation: It supports financial inclusion in rural areas.

questions.question: Straight-Through Processing (STP) means:

options.A: Every transaction is manually checked twice before it is posted to accounts
options.B: Transactions are processed in a single straight batch at the end of the day
options.C: Payments are processed only by cheque so that a paper trail exists
options.D: A transaction is processed end-to-end electronically without manual intervention

questions.answer_text: A transaction is processed end-to-end electronically without manual intervention
questions.explanation: STP reduces delays, errors and operating costs.

questions.question: ISO 20022 is:

options.A: A global standard for password policies in banking applications
options.B: A global XML-based standard for financial messaging with rich, structured data
options.C: A global standard for classifying data centres into tiers
options.D: A global standard for business continuity management in financial firms

questions.answer_text: A global XML-based standard for financial messaging with rich, structured data
questions.explanation: SWIFT cross-border payments and many domestic RTGS systems are migrating to ISO 20022.

questions.question: SFMS (Structured Financial Messaging System), used as the messaging backbone for RTGS and NEFT in India, is developed by:

options.A: NPCI
options.B: SWIFT
options.C: IDRBT
options.D: NIC

questions.answer_text: IDRBT
questions.explanation: IDRBT is RBI's Institute for Development and Research in Banking Technology.

questions.question: Secure Electronic Transaction (SET) was a protocol developed by:

options.A: RBI to secure cheque images in the CTS grid
options.B: Visa and Mastercard to secure card payments over the internet
options.C: NPCI to secure UPI payments made through mobile banking apps
options.D: Microsoft to secure email exchanged between banks

questions.answer_text: Visa and Mastercard to secure card payments over the internet
questions.explanation: SET used digital certificates for all parties but was too complex and was replaced by 3-D Secure/TLS-based methods.

questions.question: For online card-not-present transactions in India, the additional factor of authentication (AFA) is commonly implemented through:

options.A: Only the 16-digit card number and expiry date
options.B: The cardholder's signature on the merchant's screen
options.C: 3-D Secure with an OTP or similar second factor
options.D: Only the CVV printed on the back of the card

questions.answer_text: 3-D Secure with an OTP or similar second factor
questions.explanation: AFA protects customers when the card is not physically present.

questions.question: Account Aggregators (AA) in India are:

options.A: RBI-regulated NBFCs that enable consent-based sharing of a customer's financial data between institutions
options.B: Credit bureaus that collect repayment data and calculate customers' credit scores
options.C: Banks that merge a customer's accounts held at different banks into a single consolidated savings account
options.D: Payment gateways that aggregate payments from many merchants into one settlement

questions.answer_text: RBI-regulated NBFCs that enable consent-based sharing of a customer's financial data between institutions
questions.explanation: AAs are 'data blind' - they transfer encrypted data on consent but cannot read or store it.

questions.question: The Unified Lending Interface (ULI), announced by RBI in 2024, aims to:

options.A: Replace UPI with a new payment system designed specifically for loan disbursements and monthly EMI repayments
options.B: Clear loan-related cheques faster through a dedicated clearing grid for lenders
options.C: Issue the retail Digital Rupee to borrowers instead of disbursing loans in bank deposits
options.D: Provide frictionless credit by giving lenders consented access to digital data like land records and GST data

questions.answer_text: Provide frictionless credit by giving lenders consented access to digital data like land records and GST data
questions.explanation: It was developed with the Reserve Bank Innovation Hub (RBIH).

questions.question: Under RBI's Digital Lending Guidelines (2022), loan disbursals and repayments must:

options.A: Pass through the lending app's own wallet, so that the app can track repayments in real time
options.B: Be made only in cash at the lender's branch, so that the borrower's identity can be verified in person by a bank officer
options.C: Be routed through the loan service provider's personal account for faster processing
options.D: Flow directly between the borrower's bank account and the regulated entity's account, not through a third-party pool account

questions.answer_text: Flow directly between the borrower's bank account and the regulated entity's account, not through a third-party pool account
questions.explanation: A Key Fact Statement must also be given to the borrower before the loan contract.

questions.question: Omnichannel banking means:

options.A: Banking services are provided only through branches, with digital channels used only for enquiries
options.B: Customers get a seamless, connected experience across branch, mobile, internet, ATM and call centre
options.C: Each channel works with its own separate data, so customers must repeat information on every channel
options.D: Only one channel is offered to customers so that all transactions follow a single standard process

questions.answer_text: Customers get a seamless, connected experience across branch, mobile, internet, ATM and call centre
questions.explanation: A transaction started on one channel can be continued on another.

questions.question: Video-based Customer Identification Process (V-CIP) allows banks to:

options.A: Complete customer KYC remotely through a live, consent-based video interaction
options.B: Store video recordings of every transaction made by customers at ATMs
options.C: Record CCTV footage of branches and store it for security investigations
options.D: Replace physical branches with video kiosks in rural areas

questions.answer_text: Complete customer KYC remotely through a live, consent-based video interaction
questions.explanation: V-CIP must include liveness checks and secure, auditable recording.

questions.question: Behavioural biometrics in digital banking analyse:

options.A: Only the user's face photo compared with the KYC photograph
options.B: How a user types, swipes, holds the phone and navigates, to continuously detect impostors
options.C: The user's credit score and repayment history from credit bureaus
options.D: Only the user's fingerprint, captured once at the time of login using the phone's built-in sensor

questions.answer_text: How a user types, swipes, holds the phone and navigates, to continuously detect impostors
questions.explanation: It works silently in the background without adding steps for the user.

questions.question: Digital Banking Units (DBUs), launched in October 2022, are:

options.A: Mobile vans that carry ATMs and cash to villages and hamlets that do not have any bank branch nearby
options.B: Exchanges set up by banks to allow customers to trade cryptocurrencies
options.C: Specialised fixed-point units offering digital banking products and services in select districts
options.D: Call centres that handle digital banking complaints for all banks

questions.answer_text: Specialised fixed-point units offering digital banking products and services in select districts
questions.explanation: 75 DBUs were launched across 75 districts.

questions.question: RBI's Regulatory Sandbox allows:

options.A: Banks to avoid all regulations permanently for any of the products that they themselves classify as innovative or experimental
options.B: Fintech firms to test new products on all customers without any limits or monitoring
options.C: Fintech products to be tested with real customers in a controlled environment under relaxed regulatory requirements
options.D: Only foreign fintech companies to operate in India without a licence for a fixed period

questions.answer_text: Fintech products to be tested with real customers in a controlled environment under relaxed regulatory requirements
questions.explanation: Successful cohorts have covered retail payments, cross-border payments and MSME lending.

questions.question: The national helpline number for reporting cyber financial fraud in India is:
questions.explanation: Complaints can also be filed on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (cybercrime.gov.in).

questions.question: The metaverse is best described as:

options.A: A new payment card network for virtual and online-only transactions
options.B: A set of firewall rules that protect virtual machines in the cloud
options.C: A distributed database that stores customer data across many virtual servers in the cloud
options.D: A shared, immersive virtual environment where users interact through avatars using VR/AR

questions.answer_text: A shared, immersive virtual environment where users interact through avatars using VR/AR
questions.explanation: Some banks have experimented with virtual branches and customer lounges.

questions.question: Augmented Reality (AR) differs from Virtual Reality (VR) because AR:

options.A: Fully replaces the real world with a virtual environment, while VR only overlays digital information on it
options.B: Works only with expensive headsets, while VR works on any ordinary smartphone camera
options.C: Requires no device at all, while VR requires a dedicated computer and sensors
options.D: Overlays digital information on the real-world view, while VR fully replaces it with a virtual environment

questions.answer_text: Overlays digital information on the real-world view, while VR fully replaces it with a virtual environment
questions.explanation: Banks can use AR to show nearby ATMs/branches or offers through the phone camera.
